"""Create the 'implementing more strategies' issue batch on bjl14710/HFT_practice.

Run with: uv run python create_arena_issues.py
Requires a valid GH_TOKEN env var (repo scope). Idempotent: skips issues
whose titles already exist open, reuses the milestone if present.
"""
import os
import sys

import requests

REPO = "bjl14710/HFT_practice"
USERNAME = "bjl14710"
API = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}"

MILESTONE_TITLE = "Strategy Arena — Strategy Layer"
MILESTONE_DESC = (
    "Implement the four DailyStrategy participants scaffolded from "
    ".claude/plans/strategy-arena.md (plan steps 1-3). Interface, registry, "
    "and test stubs already exist on disk; these issues fill in the stubs. "
    "Later milestones cover the generic walk-forward, filter, live loop, and report."
)

ISSUE_TEMPLATE = """## What to change
{what}

## Where it is
{where}

## How to verify it's done
{verify}

## Constraints
{constraints}

## Code economy note
{economy_note}

## Branch name
`feature/issue-{number}-{slug}`

## Concept for learning materials
{concept}
"""

SPECS = [
    {
        "title": "feat(strategies): implement DailyEngulfingStrategy adapter",
        "slug": "daily-engulfing-adapter",
        "what": (
            "Fill in `DailyEngulfingStrategy.generate_signal` in "
            "`strategies/candlestick_daily.py` per its TODO docstring: return HOLD when "
            "`len(df) < warmup_bars`; otherwise delegate to the existing intraday "
            "`EngulfingStrategy` with `prev=df.iloc[-2]`, `curr=df.iloc[-1]` and map "
            "BUY -> DailySignal(+1, 1.0, \"bullish engulfing\"), SELL -> DailySignal(-1, 1.0, "
            "\"bearish engulfing\"), HOLD -> HOLD. Then remove the 4 `@pytest.mark.skip` "
            "markers on the engulfing tests in `tests/test_daily_strategies.py` and make them pass."
        ),
        "where": "`strategies/candlestick_daily.py` (stub exists), `tests/test_daily_strategies.py` (stubs exist)",
        "verify": (
            "`uv run pytest tests/test_daily_strategies.py -v` — all engulfing tests pass, "
            "none skipped. `uv run pytest tests/ -m \"not exercise\"` stays green, in particular "
            "`tests/test_engulfing.py` and `tests/test_intraday_sim.py` unmodified and passing."
        ),
        "constraints": (
            "Do NOT modify `strategies/engulfing.py`, `strategies/base.py`, or any intraday code. "
            "No pattern logic in the adapter — delegation only. No live API calls in tests."
        ),
        "economy_note": (
            "~15 lines inside one existing method plus deleting 4 skip decorators. "
            "Zero new files, zero new abstractions."
        ),
        "concept": "Adapter pattern: bridging two incompatible interfaces without duplicating domain logic",
    },
    {
        "title": "feat(strategies): implement TechnicalStrategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover)",
        "slug": "technical-strategy",
        "what": (
            "Implement `_rsi`, `_macd`, and `generate_signal` in `strategies/technical.py` "
            "following the signal rules already spelled out in the class docstring "
            "(LONG when fast MA > slow MA, MACD line > signal line, RSI < overbought; SHORT on "
            "the mirror; else HOLD; confidence = normalized |MACD histogram|). Remove the 3 "
            "skip markers on the technical tests in `tests/test_daily_strategies.py`."
        ),
        "where": "`strategies/technical.py` (skeleton with params and warmup_bars already wired), `tests/test_daily_strategies.py`",
        "verify": "`uv run pytest tests/test_daily_strategies.py -k technical -v` — 3 tests pass, none skipped; full suite green.",
        "constraints": (
            "pandas-only indicators (`rolling`/`ewm`) — no TA-Lib or any new dependency. "
            "Mirror the RSI formula already in `paper_trading_sim.build_features` (rolling-mean "
            "gains/losses) so both code paths agree, but do not import build_features here."
        ),
        "economy_note": (
            "Implement inside the existing skeleton methods (~60 lines total). "
            "No new files, no indicator utility module — inline pandas is enough."
        ),
        "concept": "MACD and EMA-based momentum: indicator construction and signal-line crossover logic",
    },
    {
        "title": "feat(strategies): implement MeanReversionStrategy (z-score fade + breakout override)",
        "slug": "mean-reversion-strategy",
        "what": (
            "Implement `generate_signal` in `strategies/mean_reversion.py` per the class "
            "docstring: breakout check first (close beyond the `breakout_lookback` high/low "
            "channel, EXCLUDING the current bar from the channel), then z-score fade at "
            "+/-`entry_z`, else HOLD. Confidence = min(|z|/entry_z, 2.0); breakouts get 1.0 and "
            "a reason containing 'breakout'. Guard near-zero rolling std -> HOLD. Remove the 3 "
            "skip markers on the meanrev tests."
        ),
        "where": "`strategies/mean_reversion.py` (skeleton exists), `tests/test_daily_strategies.py`",
        "verify": "`uv run pytest tests/test_daily_strategies.py -k meanrev -v` — 3 tests pass, none skipped; full suite green.",
        "constraints": (
            "pandas rolling ops only, no new dependencies. Breakout must beat the fade when both "
            "trigger (that ordering is the point of the strategy). Deterministic given df — no "
            "randomness, no wall-clock reads."
        ),
        "economy_note": "One method (~40 lines) in the existing skeleton. No new files.",
        "concept": "Z-score mean reversion vs channel breakout: resolving conflicting regime signals",
    },
    {
        "title": "feat(strategies): implement GBMStrategy model-bundle adapter",
        "slug": "gbm-bundle-adapter",
        "what": (
            "Implement `_ensure_loaded` and `generate_signal` in `strategies/gbm_adapter.py` per "
            "the TODO docstrings: lazy `joblib.load` of the `{'model', 'features'}` bundle, "
            "features via `paper_trading_sim.build_features`, predict on the LAST row, "
            "HOLD when any feature is NaN (note: NaN `fwd_ret_1d` on the last row is the target, "
            "not an input — expected), else position=sign(pred), confidence=abs(pred), "
            "reason=f\"pred_ret={yhat:+.4%}\". Also implement the two test stubs "
            "(`test_gbm_adapter_*`): train a throwaway 5-tree GradientBoostingRegressor on "
            "synthetic data in-test, dump to tmp_path, assert signal shape."
        ),
        "where": "`strategies/gbm_adapter.py` (skeleton exists), `tests/test_daily_strategies.py`",
        "verify": (
            "`uv run pytest tests/test_daily_strategies.py -k gbm -v` — 2 tests pass, none "
            "skipped, no network access, no model file committed to the repo."
        ),
        "constraints": (
            "Do NOT modify `paper_trading_sim.py` or any saved model in `models/`. Import joblib "
            "function-locally and build_features at module top only once implemented (keep "
            "`import strategies` free of yfinance side effects). joblib.load only ever reads "
            "locally-trained bundles — same trust model as walkforward_sim.py."
        ),
        "economy_note": (
            "Two methods in the existing skeleton plus two test bodies. The test bundle is "
            "built in-memory per test — never committed."
        ),
        "concept": "Feature-column contracts at inference time: preventing train/serve skew",
    },
]


def main() -> None:
    tok = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN", "")
    H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {tok}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"}
    who = requests.get("https://api.github.com/user", headers=H)
    if who.status_code != 200:
        sys.exit("GH_TOKEN invalid — set a real token (repo scope) in your shell config first.")
    print(f"Authenticated as {who.json()['login']}")

    issues = requests.get(f"{API}/issues?state=open&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    existing_titles = {i["title"].lower() for i in issues if "pull_request" not in i}
    print(f"Existing open issues: {len(existing_titles)}")

    # ready-for-ai label
    if requests.get(f"{API}/labels/ready-for-ai", headers=H).status_code == 404:
        requests.post(f"{API}/labels", headers=H,
                      json={"name": "ready-for-ai", "color": "0e8a16",
                            "description": "Queued for the overnight session"}).raise_for_status()
        print("Created label: ready-for-ai")

    # milestone (reuse if present)
    ms = requests.get(f"{API}/milestones?state=open&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    ms_num = next((m["number"] for m in ms if m["title"] == MILESTONE_TITLE), None)
    if ms_num is None:
        r = requests.post(f"{API}/milestones", headers=H,
                          json={"title": MILESTONE_TITLE, "description": MILESTONE_DESC})
        r.raise_for_status()
        ms_num = r.json()["number"]
        print(f"Created milestone #{ms_num}: {MILESTONE_TITLE}")
    else:
        print(f"Reusing milestone #{ms_num}: {MILESTONE_TITLE}")

    created = []
    for spec in SPECS:
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue
        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(number="N", **{k: spec[k] for k in
                ("what", "where", "verify", "constraints", "economy_note", "slug", "concept")})
        r = requests.post(f"{API}/issues", headers=H, json={
            "title": spec["title"], "body": body, "labels": ["ready-for-ai"],
            "assignees": [USERNAME], "milestone": ms_num,
        })
        r.raise_for_status()
        issue = r.json()
        fixed = body.replace("issue-N-", f"issue-{issue['number']}-")
        requests.patch(f"{API}/issues/{issue['number']}", headers=H, json={"body": fixed}).raise_for_status()
        print(f"  Created #{issue['number']}: {spec['title']}")
        created.append({"number": issue["number"], "title": spec["title"],
                        "concept": spec["concept"], "url": issue["html_url"]})

    print("\n=== Tonight's ready-for-ai queue ===")
    q = requests.get(f"{API}/issues?state=open&labels=ready-for-ai&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    for i in q:
        if "pull_request" not in i:
            print(f"  #{i['number']:3} {i['title']}\n       {i['html_url']}")
    print(f"\nTotal queued: {sum(1 for i in q if 'pull_request' not in i)}")

    # local summary for step 7
    lines = ["# Issue Planning Summary",
             "Repo: bjl14710/HFT_practice",
             'Focus: "implementing more strategies"', "",
             "## Issues Created"]
    for c in created:
        lines += [f"- #{c['number']}: {c['title']}",
                  f"  Concept: {c['concept']}", f"  URL: {c['url']}", ""]
    lines += ["## What Was NOT Planned",
              "- Arena orchestrator, SQLite state, filter, live loop, comparison report",
              "  (plan steps 4-7) — deliberately deferred to a separate milestone once the",
              "  strategy layer lands, per the 'implementing more strategies' focus.",
              "- webapp arena page — stretch, phase 2 in the plan.",
              ""]
    os.makedirs(".claude/memory", exist_ok=True)
    with open(".claude/memory/planning-session.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print("Plan summary saved to .claude/memory/planning-session.md")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            "reason=f\"pred_ret={yhat:+.4%}\". Also implement the two test stubs "
            "(`test_gbm_adapter_*`): train a throwaway 5-tree GradientBoostingRegressor on "
            "synthetic data in-test, dump to tmp_path, assert signal shape."
        ),
        "where": "`strategies/gbm_adapter.py` (skeleton exists), `tests/test_daily_strategies.py`",
        "verify": (
            "`uv run pytest tests/test_daily_strategies.py -k gbm -v` — 2 tests pass, none "
            "skipped, no network access, no model file committed to the repo."
        ),
        "constraints": (
            "Do NOT modify `paper_trading_sim.py` or any saved model in `models/`. Import joblib "
            "function-locally and build_features at module top only once implemented (keep "
            "`import strategies` free of yfinance side effects). joblib.load only ever reads "
            "locally-trained bundles — same trust model as walkforward_sim.py."
        ),
        "economy_note": (
            "Two methods in the existing skeleton plus two test bodies. The test bundle is "
            "built in-memory per test — never committed."
        ),
        "concept": "Feature-column contracts at inference time: preventing train/serve skew",
    },
]


def main() -> None:
    tok = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN", "")
    H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {tok}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"}
    who = requests.get("https://api.github.com/user", headers=H)
    if who.status_code != 200:
        sys.exit("GH_TOKEN invalid — set a real token (repo scope) in your shell config first.")
    print(f"Authenticated as {who.json()['login']}")

    issues = requests.get(f"{API}/issues?state=open&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    existing_titles = {i["title"].lower() for i in issues if "pull_request" not in i}
    print(f"Existing open issues: {len(existing_titles)}")

    # ready-for-ai label
    if requests.get(f"{API}/labels/ready-for-ai", headers=H).status_code == 404:
        requests.post(f"{API}/labels", headers=H,
                      json={"name": "ready-for-ai", "color": "0e8a16",
                            "description": "Queued for the overnight session"}).raise_for_status()
        print("Created label: ready-for-ai")

    # milestone (reuse if present)
    ms = requests.get(f"{API}/milestones?state=open&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    ms_num = next((m["number"] for m in ms if m["title"] == MILESTONE_TITLE), None)
    if ms_num is None:
        r = requests.post(f"{API}/milestones", headers=H,
                          json={"title": MILESTONE_TITLE, "description": MILESTONE_DESC})
        r.raise_for_status()
        ms_num = r.json()["number"]
        print(f"Created milestone #{ms_num}: {MILESTONE_TITLE}")
    else:
        print(f"Reusing milestone #{ms_num}: {MILESTONE_TITLE}")

    created = []
    for spec in SPECS:
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue
        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(number="N", **{k: spec[k] for k in
                ("what", "where", "verify", "constraints", "economy_note", "slug", "concept")})
        r = requests.post(f"{API}/issues", headers=H, json={
            "title": spec["title"], "body": body, "labels": ["ready-for-ai"],
            "assignees": [USERNAME], "milestone": ms_num,
        })
        r.raise_for_status()
        issue = r.json()
        fixed = body.replace("issue-N-", f"issue-{issue['number']}-")
        requests.patch(f"{API}/issues/{issue['number']}", headers=H, json={"body": fixed}).raise_for_status()
        print(f"  Created #{issue['number']}: {spec['title']}")
        created.append({"number": issue["number"], "title": spec["title"],
                        "concept": spec["concept"], "url": issue["html_url"]})

    print("\n=== Tonight's ready-for-ai queue ===")
    q = requests.get(f"{API}/issues?state=open&labels=ready-for-ai&per_page=100", headers=H).json()
    for i in q:
        if "pull_request" not in i:
            print(f"  #{i['number']:3} {i['title']}\n       {i['html_url']}")
    print(f"\nTotal queued: {sum(1 for i in q if 'pull_request' not in i)}")

    # local summary for step 7
    lines = ["# Issue Planning Summary",
             "Repo: bjl14710/HFT_practice",
             'Focus: "implementing more strategies"', "",
             "## Issues Created"]
    for c in created:
        lines += [f"- #{c['number']}: {c['title']}",
                  f"  Concept: {c['concept']}", f"  URL: {c['url']}", ""]
    lines += ["## What Was NOT Planned",
              "- Arena orchestrator, SQLite state, filter, live loop, comparison report",
              "  (plan steps 4-7) — deliberately deferred to a separate milestone once the",
              "  strategy layer lands, per the 'implementing more strategies' focus.",
              "- webapp arena page — stretch, phase 2 in the plan.",
              ""]
    os.makedirs(".claude/memory", exist_ok=True)
    with open(".claude/memory/planning-session.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print("Plan summary saved to .claude/memory/planning-session.md")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

I'm blocked on credentials — everything else is prepared and one command from done.

## What happened

Your shell exports `GH_TOKEN`, but its value is the literal 5-character placeholder string `TOKEN`, so GitHub returns 401 Bad Credentials. There's no `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no `gh` CLI, and no stored gh config to fall back on. Creating issues is an outward-facing write, so I stopped rather than guess at credentials.

## What's ready to go

I planned the batch and wrote an idempotent creation script to the scratchpad (`create_arena_issues.py`). It authenticates, skips any issue whose title already exists, creates the `ready-for-ai` label if missing, creates/reuses one milestone, and writes the `.claude/memory/planning-session.md` summary. The plan, scoped to your "implementing more strategies" focus (the four scaffolded stubs — the arena orchestrator/state/report are deliberately deferred to their own milestone):

**Milestone: "Strategy Arena — Strategy Layer"**

| Issue | Verifies via | Learning concept |
|---|---|---|
| `feat(strategies): implement DailyEngulfingStrategy adapter` | 4 unskipped tests in `test_daily_strategies.py` | Adapter pattern — bridging incompatible interfaces without duplicating logic |
| `feat(strategies): implement TechnicalStrategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover)` | 3 unskipped `-k technical` tests | MACD/EMA momentum indicator construction and signal-line crossovers |
| `feat(strategies): implement MeanReversionStrategy (z-score fade + breakout override)` | 3 unskipped `-k meanrev` tests | Z-score mean reversion vs channel breakout — resolving conflicting regime signals |
| `feat(strategies): implement GBMStrategy model-bundle adapter` | 2 implemented `-k gbm` tests, in-test throwaway model, no network | Feature-column contracts at inference — preventing train/serve skew |

Each issue body carries the full template: exact files (all stubs already exist on disk from the scaffold), verify commands, constraints (no intraday-stack changes, no new deps, no live APIs in tests), and a specific economy note (e.g. "~15 lines in one existing method plus deleting 4 skip decorators"). Concepts were checked against `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md` — none overlap with the candlestick-detection, bar-by-bar-sim, or strategy-ABC lessons already covered.

## What I need from you

Put a real token (classic PAT with `repo` scope, or fine-grained with issues read/write on `HFT_practice`) in your shell config, replacing the placeholder — e.g. in `~/.zshrc`:


Then just say "run it" — my next shell picks up the updated profile automatically and I'll execute the script and report the created issue numbers and URLs. (Or run it yourself: `cd` into the repo and `uv run python <scratchpad>/create_arena_issues.py`.)

You are running an overnight autonomous development session on this
repository. Use the overnight-coordinator agent to manage the full session.
You have full permission to read, write, commit, push, and open draft PRs.
You do NOT have permission to merge to main or close PRs after opening them.

## SETUP (run once at session start)

```bash
# 1. Ensure we are on main and up to date
git checkout main
git pull

# 2. Rebuild the knowledge graph so you navigate current code, not stale code
# (only if graphify is installed — skip silently if not)
graphify update . --force 2>/dev/null || echo "graphify not installed — skipping"

# 3. Check for a prior checkpoint (resume if interrupted)
cat .claude/memory/checkpoint.md 2>/dev/null || echo "No checkpoint — starting fresh"

# 4. Read tonight's issues
gh issue list --label "ready-for-ai" --json number,title,body,labels \
  --order created --limit 20
```

If a checkpoint exists and shows IN PROGRESS or FAILED stages, resume
from there rather than starting over.

Write the session start to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
# Checkpoint
Session started: [timestamp]
Goal: Work through all ready-for-ai issues
Status: IN PROGRESS
Issues to process: [list from gh output]
Issues completed: []
Issues failed: []
Issues skipped: []
```

---

## FOR EACH ISSUE (in number order, lowest first)

### A. READ AND ASSESS

```bash
gh issue view [N] --comments
```

Ask: Is this issue clear enough to attempt autonomously?

**Blockers that cause a SKIP:**
- Requires a design decision not documented in the issue
- Depends on another issue that isn't complete yet
- Requires credentials, API keys, or external resources not available
- Scope is too vague to produce a verifiable result

If blocked, label and move on — do NOT guess at intent:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "needs-human" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Skipped overnight: [specific reason]. Please clarify before re-queuing."
```

### B. ORIENT

Invoke the git-historian agent:
"Use the git-historian agent to understand the code area this issue will touch."

This surfaces hot files, recent decisions, and things NOT to redo.
Read .claude/memory/history-brief.md after it completes.

### C. MARK IN PROGRESS

```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "ai-in-progress" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Starting overnight implementation. Planning now."
```

### D. BRANCH

```bash
git checkout main
git checkout -b feature/issue-[N]
```

### E. PLAN

Use /plan-feature [concept from issue title] and wait for a plan.
Save the plan to .claude/plans/issue-[N].md

Do not implement until you have a written plan.

### F. IMPLEMENT

Use the appropriate specialist agents for this repo (see repo-specific
section below). Follow the plan. Write complete code — no placeholders.

If you hit a problem after 2 attempts on the same sticking point, SKIP
the issue and mark it ai-blocked. Do not spiral.

### G. TEST

Run the project's test suite. The exact commands are in the repo-specific
section below. Tests MUST pass before committing.

If tests fail after 2 fix attempts: skip, mark blocked, move on.
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --remove-label "ai-in-progress" --add-label "ai-blocked"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Blocked: tests failing after 2 attempts. [describe failure]. Needs human attention."
git checkout main
git branch -D feature/issue-[N]
```

### H. COMMIT AND PUSH

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "fix(#[N]): [issue title, shortened]"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### I. OPEN DRAFT PR

Generate the PR description using the /mr-description command, then:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "fix(#[N]): [issue title]" \
  --body "[output from /mr-description]" \
  --base main \
  --head feature/issue-[N] \
  --draft
```

Label the issue complete and close it with a reference to the PR:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] \
  --remove-label "ai-in-progress" \
  --add-label "ai-completed"
gh issue close [N] \
  --comment "Implemented. Draft PR open for review — see above."
```

### J. GENERATE LEARNING MATERIALS

**Identify the primary concept:**
Ask yourself: "What is the single most important technical concept a
developer would need to understand to maintain or extend this change?"

Guidelines:
- Choose the concept, not the feature name
  ("triple-channel SCPI addressing" not "E3631A support")
- Should be teachable in one lesson
- Should have testable recall in a drill
- Should introduce vocabulary worth learning

Then generate all three artifacts. In overnight/automated context:
- Generate the HTML files fully
- Skip in-chat interactive knowledge checks (no user present)
- Make the HTML content thorough — it is the only output
- Update PROGRESS.md with what was covered

```
/teach [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/drill-me [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/drills/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/terms [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/vocab/NNNN-[concept].html
and updates docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md

Commit the learning materials on the same feature branch:
```bash
git add docs/learning/
git commit -m "docs(learning): add lesson, drill and vocab for [concept] (from issue #[N])"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### K. UPDATE CHECKPOINT

Append to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
Issue #[N]: [COMPLETED | FAILED | SKIPPED]
  Branch: feature/issue-[N]
  PR: #[PR number if opened]
  Concept taught: [concept]
  Learning files: lessons/NNNN-x.html, drills/NNNN-x.html, vocab/NNNN-x.html
  Notes: [anything notable]
```

Return to main: `git checkout main`

---

## END OF ALL ISSUES

### 1. Rebuild the learning index

```
/index
```

Commit:
```bash
git add docs/learning/index.html
git commit -m "docs(learning): rebuild index after overnight run $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

### 2. Write the morning report

Write OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md to the repo root:

```markdown
# Overnight Build Report
Date: [date]
Session duration: [start] to [finish]
Issues attempted: [N]

## Summary
[2-3 sentences on what was accomplished overall]

## Completed ✅
| Issue | Title | Branch | PR | Concept Taught |
|-------|-------|--------|----|----------------|
| #N | [title] | feature/issue-N | #PR | [concept] |

## Failed ❌
| Issue | Title | Failure Reason |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| #N | [title] | [why — specific, actionable] |

## Skipped (needs human) ⏭
| Issue | Title | Reason |
|-------|-------|--------|
| #N | [title] | [what needs clarification] |

## Learning Materials Created
| Concept | Lesson | Drill | Vocab |
|---------|--------|-------|-------|
| [concept] | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## Test Status
[overall pass/fail and any notable failures]

## Suggested First Move
[The single most useful thing to do when you open your laptop]

## Draft PRs Awaiting Review
[list with PR numbers and one-line description each]
```

Commit and push the report:
```bash
git add OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md .claude/memory/checkpoint.md
git commit -m "chore: overnight report $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
git push origin main
```

---

## LEARNING CONCEPT SELECTION — GENERAL GUIDANCE

These guidelines apply to all repos unless overridden in a repo-specific
overnight-session command.

Choose a concept that:
- Is non-obvious (skip things any developer already knows)
- Will appear again in this codebase (worth learning for maintainability)
- Can be explained in one lesson without splitting into prerequisite lessons
- Has clear vocabulary (terms worth adding to the glossary)
- Produces useful recall questions in a drill

Avoid:
- Concepts named after specific model numbers or vendor names
  ("E3631A" is not a concept; "triple-channel PSU SCPI addressing" is)
- Concepts so generic they produce a useless lesson
  ("adding a class" — skip this)
- Concepts already well-covered in the existing lesson library
  (check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md first)

---

## FAILURE HANDLING POLICY

This policy applies to the entire session.

**Never stop the run because one issue failed.**
**Never silently skip — always label and comment.**
**Never attempt a risky or irreversible action without a prior commit.**

If at any point the session hits a situation that is genuinely ambiguous,
dangerous, or requires a human decision not covered by the issue:
1. Stop work on that issue
2. Label it needs-human
3. Leave a detailed comment explaining exactly what decision is needed
4. Move to the next issue

The goal is to maximize completed work, not to force through stuck issues.

---

## NOTE ON AUTOMATED LEARNING GENERATION

In a live session, /teach, /drill-me, and /terms end with in-chat
knowledge checks. In overnight autonomous mode, skip the interactive
questions and put that energy into making the HTML content more thorough
instead. The HTML is the deliverable — the in-chat conversation is not.

"""Daily adapter for the existing intraday EngulfingStrategy.

Reuses the 2-candle engulfing detection from :mod:`strategies.engulfing`
verbatim — this module only translates between the arena's daily contract
(full history in, DailySignal out) and the intraday contract (prev/curr
bars in, Signal out). Pattern logic must NOT be duplicated here.
"""
import pandas as pd

from strategies.daily import HOLD, DailySignal, DailyStrategy
from strategies.engulfing import EngulfingStrategy


class DailyEngulfingStrategy(DailyStrategy):
    """Bullish/bearish engulfing patterns evaluated on the last two daily bars."""

    name = "engulfing"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._inner = EngulfingStrategy()

    @property
    def warmup_bars(self) -> int:
        """Two bars: the engulfed candle and the engulfing candle."""
        return 2

    def generate_signal(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> DailySignal:
        """Map the intraday Signal on df's last two rows to a DailySignal.

        TODO(implement): take prev = df.iloc[-2], curr = df.iloc[-1], call
        self._inner.generate_signal(prev, curr), then map:
          BUY  -> DailySignal(+1, confidence=1.0, reason="bullish engulfing")
          SELL -> DailySignal(-1, confidence=1.0, reason="bearish engulfing")
          HOLD -> HOLD
        Return HOLD if len(df) < self.warmup_bars.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("scaffold: see TODO above")

def _rsi(self, close: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
        """RSI over self.rsi_period — same rolling-mean formula as
        paper_trading_sim.build_features so both code paths agree."""
        delta = close.diff()
        gain = delta.clip(lower=0).rolling(self.rsi_period).mean()
        loss = (-delta.clip(upper=0)).rolling(self.rsi_period).mean()
        rs = gain / loss
        return 100.0 - 100.0 / (1.0 + rs)

    def _macd(self, close: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
        """(macd_line, signal_line) from fast/slow EMAs of close."""

def make_ohlcv(closes, opens=None, highs=None, lows=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a date-indexed OHLCV frame from close prices (fetch_history shape)."""
    closes = list(closes)
    n = len(closes)
    opens = list(opens) if opens is not None else closes
    highs = list(highs) if highs is not None else [max(o, c) * 1.01 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    lows = list(lows) if lows is not None else [min(o, c) * 0.99 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2024-01-02", periods=n)
    return pd.DataFrame(

"""Mean-reversion / breakout strategy on daily closes.

Two regimes in one strategy (plan step 2):
  - Mean reversion: fade extremes — when the z-score of close vs its
    rolling mean is beyond entry_z, position AGAINST the move.
  - Breakout override: a close beyond the rolling high/low channel signals
    a genuine trend, so breakout direction wins over the fade.
"""
import pandas as pd

from strategies.daily import HOLD, DailySignal, DailyStrategy


class MeanReversionStrategy(DailyStrategy):
    """Fade z-score extremes unless a channel breakout overrides.

    Intended signal logic:
      - z = (close - rolling_mean(lookback)) / rolling_std(lookback)
      - close > max(High, breakout_lookback) -> +1 breakout long
      - close < min(Low, breakout_lookback)  -> -1 breakout short
      - z <= -entry_z -> +1 (buy the dip)
      - z >= +entry_z -> -1 (sell the rip)
      - otherwise HOLD. Confidence = min(|z| / entry_z, 2.0) so deeper
        extremes rank higher; breakouts get confidence 1.0.

    name = "meanrev"

    def __init__(
        self,
        lookback: int = 20,
        entry_z: float = 2.0,
        breakout_lookback: int = 55,
    ) -> None:
        self.lookback = lookback
        self.entry_z = entry_z
        self.breakout_lookback = breakout_lookback

    @property
    def warmup_bars(self) -> int:
        """Longest of the z-score and breakout-channel windows."""
        return max(self.lookback, self.breakout_lookback) + 1

"""Tests for the Strategy Arena daily-strategy layer.

One stub per strategy behaviour promised in .claude/plans/strategy-arena.md
(plan steps 1-3). All stubs are skipped until the implementations land —
the suite stays green on the scaffold. No live API calls: every test uses
synthetic OHLCV frames built in-process.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from strategies.daily import HOLD, DailySignal, DailyStrategy
from strategies.registry import available_strategies, get_strategy

SKIP_REASON = "scaffold: strategy not implemented yet"


def make_ohlcv(closes, opens=None, highs=None, lows=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a date-indexed OHLCV frame from close prices (fetch_history shape)."""
    closes = list(closes)
    n = len(closes)
    opens = list(opens) if opens is not None else closes
    highs = list(highs) if highs is not None else [max(o, c) * 1.01 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    lows = list(lows) if lows is not None else [min(o, c) * 0.99 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2024-01-02", periods=n)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"Open": opens, "High": highs, "Low": lows, "Close": closes, "Volume": [1000] * n},
        index=idx,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Interface contract
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_hold_sentinel_is_flat():
    """The shared HOLD sentinel is position 0 with zero confidence."""
    assert HOLD.position == 0
    assert HOLD.confidence == 0.0


def test_registry_lists_all_four_strategy_types():
    """Acceptance: all 4 strategy types are selectable by CLI name."""
    assert available_strategies() == ["engulfing", "gbm", "meanrev", "technical"]


def test_registry_unknown_name_lists_options():
    """Unknown names raise a KeyError that names the valid choices."""
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="engulfing"):
        get_strategy("nope")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DailyEngulfingStrategy (adapter over the intraday EngulfingStrategy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_engulfing_daily_bullish():
    """Red bar then engulfing green bar on daily closes -> position +1.

    Same pattern as tests/test_engulfing.py::test_bullish_engulf, expressed
    as the last two rows of a daily history frame.
    """
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 100, 106], opens=[100, 105, 99])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 1


def test_engulfing_daily_bearish():
    """Green bar then engulfing red bar -> position -1."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 105, 99], opens=[100, 100, 106])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_engulfing_daily_no_pattern_is_hold():
    """Acceptance edge case: no valid 2-candle pattern -> hold, not error."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 101, 102], opens=[99, 100, 101])  # steady greens
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


def test_engulfing_daily_insufficient_history_is_hold():
    """Fewer bars than warmup_bars -> hold with a logged reason, no crash."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TechnicalStrategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_technical_uptrend_goes_long():
    """Noisy sustained uptrend (fast MA > slow MA, MACD > signal, RSI < 70) -> +1.

    The trend needs pullbacks: a perfectly monotonic series has zero losses,
    pinning RSI at 100 and (correctly) blocking the long as overbought.
    """
    closes = [100 + 0.35 * i + 1.5 * np.sin(i) for i in range(80)]  # RSI ~61
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1
    assert sig.confidence > 0


def test_technical_downtrend_goes_short():
    """Mirror condition on a noisy sustained downtrend -> -1.

    Bounces keep RSI above the oversold floor (~37 here); the sine phase is
    chosen so the final bars sit on a downswing (MACD below its signal line).
    """
    closes = [130 - 0.25 * i + 2.5 * np.sin(i + 1) for i in range(80)]
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_technical_flat_series_is_hold():
    """No trend, conflicting indicators -> hold."""
    closes = [100.0] * 80
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 0

def _ensure_loaded(self) -> None:
        """Lazily load the joblib bundle on first signal.

        Security note: joblib.load executes pickled code, so bundles must
        only ever come from models/ trained locally by paper_trading_sim —
        never from a downloaded or user-supplied path. This matches the
        existing trust model in walkforward_sim.py and predict_next.py.
        """
        if self._model is not None:
            return
        import joblib  # function-local: constructing the strategy stays cheap

        bundle = joblib.load(self.bundle_path)
        self._model = bundle["model"]
        self._feat_cols = list(bundle["features"])

    def generate_signal(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> DailySignal:
        """Predict next-day return for the final bar of df."""
        if len(df) < self.warmup_bars:
            return HOLD
        self._ensure_loaded()
        # Function-local so `import strategies.registry` never pulls yfinance.
        from paper_trading_sim import build_features

        # build_features drops every row whose fwd_ret_1d target is NaN,
        # which is always the newest bar — the one we need to predict on.
        # Pad with a copy of the last bar: the real last bar then gets a
        # finite dummy target (never used as an input) and survives, while
        # the pad row becomes the dropped NaN-target row. Features only look
        # backward, so the pad cannot contaminate the real bar's inputs.
        padded = pd.concat([df, df.iloc[[-1]]])
        feats = build_features(padded)
        if feats.empty or feats.index[-1] != df.index[-1]:
            return HOLD
        row = feats.iloc[-1]
        if any(c not in feats.columns or pd.isna(row[c]) for c in self._feat_cols):
            return HOLD

        X = row[self._feat_cols].astype(float).values.reshape(1, -1)
        yhat = float(self._model.predict(X)[0])
        if abs(yhat) <= self.min_abs_pred:
            return DailySignal(position=0, confidence=0.0,
                               reason=f"pred_ret={yhat:+.4%} below threshold")
        return DailySignal(position=1 if yhat > 0 else -1, confidence=abs(yhat),
                           reason=f"pred_ret={yhat:+.4%}")

GBM_FEATURES = ["close", "ret_1d", "ma_5", "ma_10", "ma_gap", "vol_10", "rsi_14"]


def _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path):
    """Train a throwaway 5-tree GBM on synthetic prices; return (path, ohlcv_df).

    Built entirely in-process: no shipped model file, no network.
    """
    import joblib
    from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor

    from paper_trading_sim import build_features

    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
    closes = 100.0 * np.cumprod(1.0 + rng.normal(0.0, 0.01, 200))
    df = make_ohlcv(closes)
    feats = build_features(df)
    model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=5, random_state=42)
    model.fit(feats[GBM_FEATURES].values, feats["fwd_ret_1d"].values)
    path = tmp_path / "tiny_bundle.joblib"
    joblib.dump({"model": model, "features": GBM_FEATURES}, path)
    return str(path), df


def test_gbm_adapter_signals_from_tiny_bundle(tmp_path):
    """Adapter loads a bundle and emits sign(pred) / abs(pred) / reason."""
    path, df = _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path)
    strat = get_strategy("gbm", bundle_path=path)
    sig = strat.generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position in (-1, 0, 1)
    assert sig.confidence >= 0.0
    assert "pred_ret=" in sig.reason


def test_gbm_adapter_nan_features_is_hold(tmp_path):
    """History shorter than the feature warmup -> hold, bundle untouched."""
    path, df = _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path)
    strat = get_strategy("gbm", bundle_path=path)
    sig = strat.generate_signal(df.iloc[:10])
    assert sig.position == 0
    assert sig.confidence == 0.0

"""Tests for the Strategy Arena daily-strategy layer.

One stub per strategy behaviour promised in .claude/plans/strategy-arena.md
(plan steps 1-3). All stubs are skipped until the implementations land —
the suite stays green on the scaffold. No live API calls: every test uses
synthetic OHLCV frames built in-process.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from strategies.daily import HOLD, DailySignal, DailyStrategy
from strategies.registry import available_strategies, get_strategy

SKIP_REASON = "scaffold: strategy not implemented yet"


def make_ohlcv(closes, opens=None, highs=None, lows=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a date-indexed OHLCV frame from close prices (fetch_history shape)."""
    closes = list(closes)
    n = len(closes)
    opens = list(opens) if opens is not None else closes
    highs = list(highs) if highs is not None else [max(o, c) * 1.01 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    lows = list(lows) if lows is not None else [min(o, c) * 0.99 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2024-01-02", periods=n)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"Open": opens, "High": highs, "Low": lows, "Close": closes, "Volume": [1000] * n},
        index=idx,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Interface contract
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_hold_sentinel_is_flat():
    """The shared HOLD sentinel is position 0 with zero confidence."""
    assert HOLD.position == 0
    assert HOLD.confidence == 0.0


def test_registry_lists_all_four_strategy_types():
    """Acceptance: all 4 strategy types are selectable by CLI name."""
    assert available_strategies() == ["engulfing", "gbm", "meanrev", "technical"]


def test_registry_unknown_name_lists_options():
    """Unknown names raise a KeyError that names the valid choices."""
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="engulfing"):
        get_strategy("nope")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DailyEngulfingStrategy (adapter over the intraday EngulfingStrategy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_engulfing_daily_bullish():
    """Red bar then engulfing green bar on daily closes -> position +1.

    Same pattern as tests/test_engulfing.py::test_bullish_engulf, expressed
    as the last two rows of a daily history frame.
    """
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 100, 106], opens=[100, 105, 99])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 1


def test_engulfing_daily_bearish():
    """Green bar then engulfing red bar -> position -1."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 105, 99], opens=[100, 100, 106])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_engulfing_daily_no_pattern_is_hold():
    """Acceptance edge case: no valid 2-candle pattern -> hold, not error."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 101, 102], opens=[99, 100, 101])  # steady greens
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


def test_engulfing_daily_insufficient_history_is_hold():
    """Fewer bars than warmup_bars -> hold with a logged reason, no crash."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TechnicalStrategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_technical_uptrend_goes_long():
    """Noisy sustained uptrend (fast MA > slow MA, MACD > signal, RSI < 70) -> +1.

    The trend needs pullbacks: a perfectly monotonic series has zero losses,
    pinning RSI at 100 and (correctly) blocking the long as overbought.
    """
    closes = [100 + 0.35 * i + 1.5 * np.sin(i) for i in range(80)]  # RSI ~61
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1
    assert sig.confidence > 0


def test_technical_downtrend_goes_short():
    """Mirror condition on a noisy sustained downtrend -> -1.

    Bounces keep RSI above the oversold floor (~37 here); the sine phase is
    chosen so the final bars sit on a downswing (MACD below its signal line).
    """
    closes = [130 - 0.25 * i + 2.5 * np.sin(i + 1) for i in range(80)]
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_technical_flat_series_is_hold():
    """No trend, conflicting indicators -> hold."""
    closes = [100.0] * 80
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MeanReversionStrategy (z-score fade + breakout override)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_meanrev_buys_the_dip():
    """A drop pushing z below -entry_z -> +1 (fade the move).

    The dip (98.7, z~-2.7) must stay ABOVE the 55-bar low channel (~98.5) —
    any deeper and the breakout override correctly fires SHORT instead.
    """
    closes = [100 + 0.5 * np.sin(i) for i in range(60)] + [98.7]
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1


def test_meanrev_breakout_overrides_fade():
    """A close above the 55-bar high is a breakout long, not a short fade."""
    closes = list(np.linspace(100, 101, 60)) + [115.0]  # explosive new high
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1
    assert "breakout" in sig.reason


def test_meanrev_flat_series_zero_std_is_hold():
    """Rolling std ~0 must not divide by zero -> hold."""
    closes = [100.0] * 60
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 0

# GBMStrategy (model-bundle adapter)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.skip(reason=SKIP_REASON)

    """Adapter loads a bundle and emits sign(pred) / abs(pred) / reason.

    """
    raise NotImplementedError

    """History shorter than the feature warmup (NaN features) -> hold."""

"""Tests for the Strategy Arena daily-strategy layer.

One stub per strategy behaviour promised in .claude/plans/strategy-arena.md
(plan steps 1-3). All stubs are skipped until the implementations land —

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from strategies.daily import HOLD, DailySignal, DailyStrategy
from strategies.registry import available_strategies, get_strategy

SKIP_REASON = "scaffold: strategy not implemented yet"


def make_ohlcv(closes, opens=None, highs=None, lows=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a date-indexed OHLCV frame from close prices (fetch_history shape)."""
    closes = list(closes)
    n = len(closes)
    opens = list(opens) if opens is not None else closes
    highs = list(highs) if highs is not None else [max(o, c) * 1.01 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    lows = list(lows) if lows is not None else [min(o, c) * 0.99 for o, c in zip(opens, closes)]
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2024-01-02", periods=n)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"Open": opens, "High": highs, "Low": lows, "Close": closes, "Volume": [1000] * n},
        index=idx,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Interface contract
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_hold_sentinel_is_flat():
    """The shared HOLD sentinel is position 0 with zero confidence."""
    assert HOLD.position == 0
    assert HOLD.confidence == 0.0


def test_registry_lists_all_four_strategy_types():
    """Acceptance: all 4 strategy types are selectable by CLI name."""
    assert available_strategies() == ["engulfing", "gbm", "meanrev", "technical"]


def test_registry_unknown_name_lists_options():
    """Unknown names raise a KeyError that names the valid choices."""
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="engulfing"):
        get_strategy("nope")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DailyEngulfingStrategy (adapter over the intraday EngulfingStrategy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_engulfing_daily_bullish():
    """Red bar then engulfing green bar on daily closes -> position +1.

    Same pattern as tests/test_engulfing.py::test_bullish_engulf, expressed
    as the last two rows of a daily history frame.
    """
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 100, 106], opens=[100, 105, 99])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 1


def test_engulfing_daily_bearish():
    """Green bar then engulfing red bar -> position -1."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 105, 99], opens=[100, 100, 106])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_engulfing_daily_no_pattern_is_hold():
    """Acceptance edge case: no valid 2-candle pattern -> hold, not error."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100, 101, 102], opens=[99, 100, 101])  # steady greens
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


def test_engulfing_daily_insufficient_history_is_hold():
    """Fewer bars than warmup_bars -> hold with a logged reason, no crash."""
    df = make_ohlcv(closes=[100])
    sig = get_strategy("engulfing").generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TechnicalStrategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_technical_uptrend_goes_long():
    """Noisy sustained uptrend (fast MA > slow MA, MACD > signal, RSI < 70) -> +1.

    The trend needs pullbacks: a perfectly monotonic series has zero losses,
    pinning RSI at 100 and (correctly) blocking the long as overbought.
    """
    closes = [100 + 0.35 * i + 1.5 * np.sin(i) for i in range(80)]  # RSI ~61
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1
    assert sig.confidence > 0


def test_technical_downtrend_goes_short():
    """Mirror condition on a noisy sustained downtrend -> -1.

    Bounces keep RSI above the oversold floor (~37 here); the sine phase is
    chosen so the final bars sit on a downswing (MACD below its signal line).
    """
    closes = [130 - 0.25 * i + 2.5 * np.sin(i + 1) for i in range(80)]
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == -1


def test_technical_flat_series_is_hold():
    """No trend, conflicting indicators -> hold."""
    closes = [100.0] * 80
    sig = get_strategy("technical").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MeanReversionStrategy (z-score fade + breakout override)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_meanrev_buys_the_dip():
    """A drop pushing z below -entry_z -> +1 (fade the move).

    The dip (98.7, z~-2.7) must stay ABOVE the 55-bar low channel (~98.5) —
    any deeper and the breakout override correctly fires SHORT instead.
    """
    closes = [100 + 0.5 * np.sin(i) for i in range(60)] + [98.7]
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1


def test_meanrev_breakout_overrides_fade():
    """A close above the 55-bar high is a breakout long, not a short fade."""
    closes = list(np.linspace(100, 101, 60)) + [115.0]  # explosive new high
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 1
    assert "breakout" in sig.reason


def test_meanrev_flat_series_zero_std_is_hold():
    """Rolling std ~0 must not divide by zero -> hold."""
    closes = [100.0] * 60
    sig = get_strategy("meanrev").generate_signal(make_ohlcv(closes))
    assert sig.position == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GBMStrategy (model-bundle adapter)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GBM_FEATURES = ["close", "ret_1d", "ma_5", "ma_10", "ma_gap", "vol_10", "rsi_14"]


def _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path):
    """Train a throwaway 5-tree GBM on synthetic prices; return (path, ohlcv_df).

    Built entirely in-process: no shipped model file, no network.
    """
    import joblib
    from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor

    from paper_trading_sim import build_features

    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
    closes = 100.0 * np.cumprod(1.0 + rng.normal(0.0, 0.01, 200))
    df = make_ohlcv(closes)
    feats = build_features(df)
    model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=5, random_state=42)
    model.fit(feats[GBM_FEATURES].values, feats["fwd_ret_1d"].values)
    path = tmp_path / "tiny_bundle.joblib"
    joblib.dump({"model": model, "features": GBM_FEATURES}, path)
    return str(path), df


def test_gbm_adapter_signals_from_tiny_bundle(tmp_path):
    """Adapter loads a bundle and emits sign(pred) / abs(pred) / reason."""
    path, df = _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path)
    strat = get_strategy("gbm", bundle_path=path)
    sig = strat.generate_signal(df)
    assert sig.position in (-1, 0, 1)
    assert sig.confidence >= 0.0
    assert "pred_ret=" in sig.reason


def test_gbm_adapter_nan_features_is_hold(tmp_path):
    """History shorter than the feature warmup -> hold, bundle untouched."""
    path, df = _make_tiny_bundle(tmp_path)
    strat = get_strategy("gbm", bundle_path=path)
    sig = strat.generate_signal(df.iloc[:10])
    assert sig.position == 0
    assert sig.confidence == 0.0

The user wants to learn "contracts" (or, if blank, you choose the most valuable concept to teach next based on their progress and this project's code). This is a STATEFUL, multi-session teaching relationship. Treat the folder `docs/learning/` as the teaching workspace. Learning persists there between sessions. Read what already exists before teaching anything new. ## The Core Difference From Generic Teaching Everything you teach must be grounded in THIS project. You are not teaching abstract computer science — you are teaching the concepts that show up in the code the user is actually writing, using their own files as examples. Abstract knowledge that isn't tied to their project will not stick. ## Workspace Files (read these first if they exist) - `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md` — what the user has learned so far, what they found hard, what to teach next. Your map of their knowledge. If it doesn't exist, create it on the first lesson. - `docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md` — terms the user now understands. Only add a term here once they've demonstrably grasped it. All lessons should use terminology consistent with this glossary. - `docs/learning/lessons/*.html` — the lessons themselves, numbered `0001-.html` and incrementing. These are the main artifact. ## Step 1 — Ground the Lesson Before teaching, establish two things: **Relevance to the project:** Where does this concept appear in the codebase? Grep/read to find the actual files, classes, or functions that use it. If the concept isn't in the project yet but is about to be (the user is heading there), say so. If it has nothing to do with the project, gently check whether they want a project-grounded lesson or just a general explanation. **The right difficulty (zone of proximal development):** Read PROGRESS.md. Teach the thing that builds on what they know and is challenging but not overwhelming. Keep scope tight — one concept taught well beats five rushed. If they say they already know something, record that in PROGRESS.md and move to the next useful thing. ## Step 2 — Gather Trustworthy Knowledge Do not rely only on your own parametric knowledge for technical specifics — it can be outdated or subtly wrong. For anything where accuracy matters (library behavior, protocol specs, version-specific details), web-search to ground the explanation in current, authoritative sources. Note the sources. ## Step 3 — Produce an HTML Lesson Create a self-contained, single-file HTML lesson saved to `docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-.html` (increment NNNN from the highest existing lesson; start at 0001). The HTML must be: **Self-contained** — all CSS and JS inline, no external dependencies, opens correctly with a plain `file://` open in any browser. **Beautiful and readable** — clean typography, comfortable line length, good contrast, syntax-highlighted code blocks (a small inline highlighter or hand-applied span colors are fine), responsive. This should feel like a polished lesson, not a wall of text. **Structured** with these sections: 1. Title and a one-line "why this matters for [project]" 2. The concept explained plainly (the knowledge) 3. A minimal standalone example, heavily commented 4. "In this project" — the real code from their repo that uses this, with the actual file path shown, walked through line by line 5. "Often confused with" — when a similar concept exists, contrast them clearly (what they share, where they diverge, when to use each). Examples of pairs worth contrasting: container vs VM, process vs thread, concurrency vs parallelism, class vs instance, argument vs parameter, sync vs async, compiler vs interpreter, declaration vs definition. 6. Interactive practice (the skill): 3-5 quiz questions or small in-browser exercises with immediate feedback. Use inline JS so clicking an answer instantly shows whether it's right and why. This tight feedback loop is where skill actually forms — don't skip it. CRITICAL — randomize answer position. A common failure is putting the correct answer first every time, which trains the user to click the top option instead of thinking. Prevent this STRUCTURALLY, not by hoping: - Do NOT encode correctness by position (never "the answer is option A" or "index 0 is correct"). - Mark the correct option with a data attribute, e.g. `data-correct="true"`, and give wrong options `data-correct="false"`. - Have the JavaScript SHUFFLE the options in the DOM on page load (e.g. a Fisher-Yates shuffle of each question's option elements), so the rendered order is randomized every time the page opens. - The click handler checks the clicked element's `data-correct` attribute, never its position. This makes "always first" impossible regardless of the order you authored them in. - Also vary the authored order yourself as a backstop — don't write every correct answer first in the source either. - Each option should carry its own short explanation (why it's right or wrong) shown on click, so distractors teach too. 7. A short "check your understanding" set of scenario questions. **Progress-aware** — include a simple completion mechanism: checkboxes or a "mark complete" button for each section, with state held in-page via JS (plain variables/DOM state, NOT localStorage — that's unreliable here). At minimum, the quiz should show a score. The goal is the user can see how far they've gotten through the lesson. ### Reference pattern for shuffled quiz options Follow this structure so the correct answer is never tied to position: ```html

Which SCPI command queries DC voltage?

  • MEAS:VOLT:DC?
  • SET:VOLT:DC
  • VOLT:DC 3.3

``` The key line is `li.dataset.correct === 'true'` — correctness comes from the attribute, and `shuffle` reorders the DOM on load, so position is meaningless. ## Step 4 — Make It Trivial to Open After writing the file, give the user the exact command to open it: - macOS: `open docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-name.html` - Linux: `xdg-open docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-name.html` Print the right one for their platform. ## Step 5 — Discuss and Refine Invite questions. Answer them directly. If a question reveals the explainer was unclear, amend the HTML or add a follow-up lesson. Once it's clear the user understands a term, add it to GLOSSARY.md using a concise definition. ## Step 6 — Record Progress Update `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md`: - What was taught this session (link the lesson file) - How well the user seemed to grasp it - What they struggled with - A suggested next concept, tied to the project and their current level ## Step 7 — Knowledge Check Before Closing End the session with 2-3 spoken (in-chat) questions that verify the lesson landed. Let the user attempt them; correct gently with reference back to the lesson. This is the retention check that flat documents skip. ## Tone Encouraging but honest. The user is building real skills they'll rely on to maintain this codebase alone. Challenge them appropriately. Never pad. The HTML lesson is the durable artifact; the chat is the live tutoring around it.

HFT Practice · Lesson 0035

Feature Contracts at Inference: Train/Serve Skew and the Last-Bar Problem

Why this matters here: your model bundles are saved as {"model": ..., "features": [...]} and CLAUDE.md warns that the features list "defines exact column order at inference." This lesson explains what that contract really is, how build_features silently eats the one row you most want to predict on, and why strategies/gbm_adapter.py pads the frame with a copy of the last bar.

1 · The concept: a feature contract

When you train a model on a table of features, you implicitly sign a contract with your future self. At inference time you must reproduce:

ClauseMeaningWhat breaks if violated
NamesThe same columns existKeyError, or silently missing features filled with garbage
OrderColumns feed the model in training orderNo error at all — sklearn sees a bare numpy array and happily multiplies RSI by the coefficient it learned for volume. Predictions are nonsense.
SemanticsEach column is computed the same waySubtle drift: RSI via rolling mean ≠ RSI via EMA (Wilder). Same name, different number.
AvailabilityEvery input is knowable at decision timeLookahead bias (using tomorrow) or inference lag (using yesterday when today exists)

Violating any clause produces train/serve skew: the model runs on inputs distributionally different from what it was trained on. The insidious part is that clauses 2–4 usually fail silently — the code runs, numbers come out, and the equity curve quietly rots.

2 · Minimal standalone example

# The last-bar problem in eight lines.
import pandas as pd

All 5 ready-for-ai issues were completed successfully with draft PRs opened. The session delivered the full PWA mobile web app stack: icon generation, web app manifest, iOS meta tags, mobile-responsive CSS, and a Mac launch script with ngrok tunnel — enabling the AlgoTrade dashboard to be installed on an iPhone home screen without the App Store. All PRs pass `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise" -q` — 26 passed, 54 deselected. No new tests were added (issues were documentation, CSS, and scripting — no new Python logic).

## PR Dependency Order
PRs #47 (icons) → #48 (manifest) are loosely ordered: the manifest references icon paths that exist after #47 is merged. Merge #47 first, then #48. PRs #49, #50, #51 are independent.

Suggested merge order:
1. **PR #47** — icon PNGs (prerequisite for manifest icons)

3. **PR #49** — mobile CSS (independent, safe to merge any time)
4. **PR #50** — mac-setup.sh (independent)
5. **PR #51** — MAC_SETUP.md (independent)

## Key Technical Details

### PWA install requirements (must all be true)
- HTTPS URL — provided by ngrok free tier
- `<link rel="manifest">` in `<head>`
- Manifest with `display: standalone` and at least one icon
- `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes">` for iOS standalone mode
- Must be opened in **Safari** on iOS — Chrome on iOS cannot install PWAs

### iOS vs Android/Chrome icon handling
- **iOS** reads `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">` → uses `icon-180.png` (180×180, @3x Retina)
- **Android Chrome** reads `manifest.json → "icons"` → uses `icon-192.png` and `icon-512.png`
- iOS **ignores** the manifest icons array entirely

### ngrok URL rotation (free tier)
The ngrok URL changes every time `mac-setup.sh` is restarted. The user must re-open the new URL in Safari and re-add to home screen. Paid ngrok plans allow a reserved subdomain.

### iOS font-size auto-zoom
iOS Safari zooms in when a user taps any `<input>` / `<select>` with `font-size < 16px`. The fix (now in `style.css`) is `font-size: 16px` on all form controls inside the mobile media query.

content.text:
Produce a Merge Request description for the current branch, comparing it to
its base branch. The output should be ready to paste directly into GitHub,
GitLab, or wherever I open the MR.

## Step 1 — Identify the Base
- Determine the base branch. Priority order:
  1. Use "vs" if given (e.g. `/mr-description develop`)
  2. Otherwise detect: `git merge-base` against `main`, `master`, or `develop`
     — whichever exists and gives a sensible diff
  3. If ambiguous, ask which base I want before continuing
- State which base you chose and which commit hash it resolves to.

## Step 2 — Gather the Facts
Run these and use their output (don't show me the raw output):
- `git log <base>..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s"`  (commit list)
- `git diff <base>..HEAD --stat`                   (file change summary)
- `git diff <base>..HEAD`                          (actual changes, for the why)
- Read the meaningfully-changed files yourself to understand purpose, not
  just lines moved.

## Step 3 — Produce the Description
Output exactly this structure, in Markdown, ready to paste:

```markdown
## Summary
[2-3 sentences: what this change accomplishes and why it exists.
Plain language, no jargon dump. Lead with the user-visible impact
or the problem being solved, not the implementation detail.]

## Changes by File

[For each meaningfully-changed file, a short section: the file path as a
bold heading with its change type, then a sentence or two underneath
explaining why it changed and what the change does.]

**`path/to/file.py`** — modified
Explanation of why this file changed and what the change accomplishes.
Can run to a second sentence if the change warrants it.

**`path/to/other.py`** — added
What this new file is for and why it was needed.

[Group trivial changes — formatting-only, generated files, lockfile updates
— at the end under a single heading like "**Minor / generated**" with a
one-line summary rather than a section each.]

## Why
[A short section explaining the reasoning behind the change. What problem
prompted it? What alternative approaches were considered or rejected?
What tradeoffs were accepted? This is the part future-you and reviewers
care about most. 1-2 short paragraphs.]

## Testing
[How was this verified? Tests added, tests run, manual checks, edge cases
exercised. If a test suite was run, give pass/fail numbers.]

## Risk and Rollback
[What's the blast radius if this breaks? How to revert?
Skip this section entirely for trivial changes — only include for changes
touching shared infrastructure, data models, auth, public APIs, or
anything else with meaningful blast radius.]

## Diagram
[INCLUDE ONLY WHEN IT GENUINELY HELPS. Apply this test:
- Does the change reorganize architecture, add a new flow between modules,
  introduce a state machine, or change how components communicate? → diagram
- Is it a bug fix, small refactor, doc update, config tweak, or single-file
  change? → no diagram, omit this section entirely

When included, use Mermaid. Pick the right type:
- flowchart  → for data or call flow between components
- sequenceDiagram  → for ordered interactions over time
- stateDiagram-v2  → for state transitions
- classDiagram  → for new type hierarchies

Show the "after" state, optionally with a brief "before" if the contrast
is the point of the change.]

## Checklist
- [ ] Tests pass locally
- [ ] No new linter or type-check errors
- [ ] Documentation updated (if user-facing)
- [ ] Breaking changes noted in description (if any)
[Add or remove items based on what this project actually cares about —
infer from CLAUDE.md and the repo's existing PR template if one exists
at .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md or similar.]
```

# MR: feat(arena): Strategy Arena strategy layer — DailyStrategy interface + 4 implementations

Branch: `feature/arena-strategy-layer` → `main` (base commit `5d8f3ae`)

## Summary
Adds the strategy layer of the Strategy Arena (`.claude/plans/strategy-arena.md`, steps 1–3): a daily-bar `DailyStrategy` interface plus four selectable implementations — an adapter over the existing intraday engulfing detector, a technical-indicator strategy (RSI + MACD + MA crossover), a z-score mean-reversion strategy with breakout override, and an adapter that puts the existing GBM model bundles behind the same contract. This is the prerequisite for backtesting heterogeneous strategies apples-to-apples and paper-trading the survivors side by side; the arena orchestrator itself (filter, SQLite state, live loop, report) is deliberately NOT in this MR.

## Changes by File

**`strategies/daily.py`** — added
The contract everything else implements: `DailyStrategy` ABC (`generate_signal(df) -> DailySignal`, `warmup_bars`) and the `DailySignal` dataclass (`position` −1/0/+1, `confidence` for top-N ranking, human-readable `reason`). Kept separate from the intraday 2-bar `BaseStrategy` so ML models needing long feature windows and rule strategies share one daily interface without touching the intraday stack.

**`strategies/candlestick_daily.py`** — added
`DailyEngulfingStrategy`: a thin adapter that runs the existing `EngulfingStrategy` on the last two daily bars. Delegation only — zero pattern logic duplicated.

**`strategies/technical.py`** — added
`TechnicalStrategy`: long when fast MA > slow MA, MACD above its signal line, and RSI not overbought; mirrored short. Confidence is the price-normalized MACD histogram. RSI uses the same rolling-mean formula as `paper_trading_sim.build_features` so both code paths agree; pandas-only, no new dependencies.

**`strategies/mean_reversion.py`** — added
`MeanReversionStrategy`: fades z-score extremes (±2σ over 20 bars) unless the close breaks the 55-bar high/low channel, in which case the breakout direction wins. Channel excludes the current bar; near-zero rolling std returns hold instead of dividing by zero.

**`strategies/gbm_adapter.py`** — added
`GBMStrategy`: wraps a saved `{"model", "features"}` joblib bundle behind `DailyStrategy` — sign of predicted return → position, magnitude → confidence. The subtle part: `build_features` ends with `dropna()`, which always deletes the newest bar (its `fwd_ret_1d` target is NaN), so the adapter pads the frame with a copy of the last bar. The real bar then survives with a finite dummy target (never used as an input) and the copy is dropped instead. Features only look backward, so the pad cannot contaminate inputs — same-day features from the unmodified production pipeline.

**`strategies/registry.py`** — added
Name → constructor map (`engulfing`, `technical`, `meanrev`, `gbm`) so the upcoming `arena-run --strategies ...` CLI can select strategies by string. Unknown names raise a KeyError listing valid options.

**`tests/test_daily_strategies.py`** — added
15 tests: interface/registry contract, per-strategy signal cases (long/short/hold/insufficient-history), and GBM adapter tests that train a throwaway 5-tree model in-test (no shipped model file, no network). Two scaffolded fixtures were corrected during implementation because they were mathematically impossible: a monotonic uptrend pins RSI at 100 (correctly blocked as overbought) and a dip to 92 crosses the 55-bar low channel (correctly a breakout short, not a fade) — replaced with numerically verified series; docstrings explain both.

**Minor / generated** — `.claude/plans/strategy-arena.md` (the plan this implements), `docs/learning/` (lesson 0035 + drill 0006 on feature contracts at inference, index/PROGRESS updates), `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md`, `.claude/memory/checkpoint.md`, `.gitignore` (pycache/egg-info), `uv.lock` (locks the dev extra so `uv run pytest` works from a clean sync).

## Why
The repo has one validated ML strategy (~27% annualized backtest) and, since the intraday work, a growing set of rule-based ideas — but no way to compare them under identical methodology. The plan's answer is a shared contract screened by one backtest harness. Two design decisions worth reviewer attention: (1) a **new** daily interface beside the intraday one rather than unifying them — unification would have touched `intraday_sim`/`PaperEngine` and their tests for zero arena benefit; (2) the GBM padding trick rather than refactoring `build_features` — refactoring would have rippled into `walkforward_sim`/`predict_next`, which this MR deliberately leaves untouched. Trade-off accepted: the padding is subtle enough to need its comment block (and lesson 0035 documents it in depth).

Related finding, NOT fixed here: `predict_next.py:136–144` predicts off the second-newest bar for the same dropna reason — a pre-existing one-day inference lag. Left as-is because changing it alters live trading behavior; suggested as its own follow-up issue.

## Testing
`uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"` → **85 passed** (15 new). No live API calls anywhere; GBM tests build their model in-memory per test. The intraday stack's tests (`test_engulfing.py`, `test_intraday_sim.py`, `test_paper_trading.py`) pass unmodified — zero blast radius on existing behavior.

## Risk and Rollback
Additive only: no existing module is modified except `uv.lock`/`.gitignore`; nothing imports `strategies.daily` yet, so reverting the merge is a clean rollback with no data or behavioral implications. Real-money paths are untouched (`rh-exec` gating unchanged).

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass locally (85 passed)
- [x] No new dependencies (stdlib + existing pandas/sklearn/joblib)
- [x] Every public function has a docstring; type hints throughout
- [x] Intraday stack untouched and green
- [ ] Reviewer: sanity-check the GBM padding trick (`strategies/gbm_adapter.py`)

def run_strategy_walkforward(strategy,
                             data: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
                             top_n: int = 5,
                             capital: float = 100000.0,
                             trade_cost_bps: float = 1.0) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Backtest any DailyStrategy over pre-fetched daily OHLCV frames.

    Generic counterpart to ``simulate_walkforward`` (which is GBM-specific):
    on each date, every ticker's history up to and including that bar is
    handed to ``strategy.generate_signal``; the ``top_n`` non-hold signals
    ranked by confidence are held equal-weight for one bar, realizing the
    next close-to-close return (signed by position). Each ticker's final
    bar produces no trade — its forward return does not exist yet.

    Data is injected rather than fetched so tests stay offline and the
    arena's live loop can reuse the same code path (backfill == backtest).

    Args:
        strategy: A ``strategies.daily.DailyStrategy`` instance.
        data: ``{ticker: OHLCV DataFrame}`` as returned by ``fetch_history``.
        top_n: Maximum concurrent positions per day.
        capital: Starting equity.
        trade_cost_bps: Flat cost applied on each day with any position.

    Returns:
