The user wants to learn "to" (or, if blank, you choose the most valuable concept to teach next based on their progress and this project's code). This is a STATEFUL, multi-session teaching relationship. Treat the folder `docs/learning/` as the teaching workspace. Learning persists there between sessions. Read what already exists before teaching anything new. ## The Core Difference From Generic Teaching Everything you teach must be grounded in THIS project. You are not teaching abstract computer science — you are teaching the concepts that show up in the code the user is actually writing, using their own files as examples. Abstract knowledge that isn't tied to their project will not stick. ## Workspace Files (read these first if they exist) - `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md` — what the user has learned so far, what they found hard, what to teach next. Your map of their knowledge. If it doesn't exist, create it on the first lesson. - `docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md` — terms the user now understands. Only add a term here once they've demonstrably grasped it. All lessons should use terminology consistent with this glossary. - `docs/learning/lessons/*.html` — the lessons themselves, numbered `0001-.html` and incrementing. These are the main artifact. ## Step 1 — Ground the Lesson Before teaching, establish two things: **Relevance to the project:** Where does this concept appear in the codebase? Grep/read to find the actual files, classes, or functions that use it. If the concept isn't in the project yet but is about to be (the user is heading there), say so. If it has nothing to do with the project, gently check whether they want a project-grounded lesson or just a general explanation. **The right difficulty (zone of proximal development):** Read PROGRESS.md. Teach the thing that builds on what they know and is challenging but not overwhelming. Keep scope tight — one concept taught well beats five rushed. If they say they already know something, record that in PROGRESS.md and move to the next useful thing. ## Step 2 — Gather Trustworthy Knowledge Do not rely only on your own parametric knowledge for technical specifics — it can be outdated or subtly wrong. For anything where accuracy matters (library behavior, protocol specs, version-specific details), web-search to ground the explanation in current, authoritative sources. Note the sources. ## Step 3 — Produce an HTML Lesson Create a self-contained, single-file HTML lesson saved to `docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-.html` (increment NNNN from the highest existing lesson; start at 0001). The HTML must be: **Self-contained** — all CSS and JS inline, no external dependencies, opens correctly with a plain `file://` open in any browser. **Beautiful and readable** — clean typography, comfortable line length, good contrast, syntax-highlighted code blocks (a small inline highlighter or hand-applied span colors are fine), responsive. This should feel like a polished lesson, not a wall of text. **Structured** with these sections: 1. Title and a one-line "why this matters for [project]" 2. The concept explained plainly (the knowledge) 3. A minimal standalone example, heavily commented 4. "In this project" — the real code from their repo that uses this, with the actual file path shown, walked through line by line 5. "Often confused with" — when a similar concept exists, contrast them clearly (what they share, where they diverge, when to use each). Examples of pairs worth contrasting: container vs VM, process vs thread, concurrency vs parallelism, class vs instance, argument vs parameter, sync vs async, compiler vs interpreter, declaration vs definition. 6. Interactive practice (the skill): 3-5 quiz questions or small in-browser exercises with immediate feedback. Use inline JS so clicking an answer instantly shows whether it's right and why. This tight feedback loop is where skill actually forms — don't skip it. CRITICAL — randomize answer position. A common failure is putting the correct answer first every time, which trains the user to click the top option instead of thinking. Prevent this STRUCTURALLY, not by hoping: - Do NOT encode correctness by position (never "the answer is option A" or "index 0 is correct"). - Mark the correct option with a data attribute, e.g. `data-correct="true"`, and give wrong options `data-correct="false"`. - Have the JavaScript SHUFFLE the options in the DOM on page load (e.g. a Fisher-Yates shuffle of each question's option elements), so the rendered order is randomized every time the page opens. - The click handler checks the clicked element's `data-correct` attribute, never its position. This makes "always first" impossible regardless of the order you authored them in. - Also vary the authored order yourself as a backstop — don't write every correct answer first in the source either. - Each option should carry its own short explanation (why it's right or wrong) shown on click, so distractors teach too. 7. A short "check your understanding" set of scenario questions. **Progress-aware** — include a simple completion mechanism: checkboxes or a "mark complete" button for each section, with state held in-page via JS (plain variables/DOM state, NOT localStorage — that's unreliable here). At minimum, the quiz should show a score. The goal is the user can see how far they've gotten through the lesson. ### Reference pattern for shuffled quiz options Follow this structure so the correct answer is never tied to position: ```html

Which SCPI command queries DC voltage?

  • MEAS:VOLT:DC?
  • SET:VOLT:DC
  • VOLT:DC 3.3

``` The key line is `li.dataset.correct === 'true'` — correctness comes from the attribute, and `shuffle` reorders the DOM on load, so position is meaningless. ## Step 4 — Make It Trivial to Open After writing the file, give the user the exact command to open it: - macOS: `open docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-name.html` - Linux: `xdg-open docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-name.html` Print the right one for their platform. ## Step 5 — Discuss and Refine Invite questions. Answer them directly. If a question reveals the explainer was unclear, amend the HTML or add a follow-up lesson. Once it's clear the user understands a term, add it to GLOSSARY.md using a concise definition. ## Step 6 — Record Progress Update `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md`: - What was taught this session (link the lesson file) - How well the user seemed to grasp it - What they struggled with - A suggested next concept, tied to the project and their current level ## Step 7 — Knowledge Check Before Closing End the session with 2-3 spoken (in-chat) questions that verify the lesson landed. Let the user attempt them; correct gently with reference back to the lesson. This is the retention check that flat documents skip. ## Tone Encouraging but honest. The user is building real skills they'll rely on to maintain this codebase alone. Challenge them appropriately. Never pad. The HTML lesson is the durable artifact; the chat is the live tutoring around it.

input.content:
HFT Practice · Lesson 0038

The GUI, and the Three Ways to Run a Trading Method (like the 2-Candle)

Why this matters: "run the 2-candle strategy" means three different things in this codebase depending on the engine you pick — and the desktop GUI, which predates the strategies package, runs none of them. Knowing which door leads where saves you from hunting the GUI for a button that doesn't exist.

1 · The mental model: one pattern, three engines

The pattern (bullish/bearish engulfing — a red candle whose body is swallowed by the next green one, or vice versa) is defined exactly once, in strategies/engulfing.py. Three engines can drive it:

EngineCommandBar frequencyExit logicPersists?
Intraday PaperEngineintraday-sim1m–60m barsStop-loss / take-profit / forced end-of-day closeCSV files per run
Arena backtestarena-run backtestDailyOne-bar hold, next closeVerdict in arena.db
Arena livearena-run liveDailyOne-bar hold, next closeOngoing ledger in arena.db

The GUI is a fourth thing entirely: a Tkinter front-end over the GBM/mean-variance pipeline (train, walk-forward, news, universe, execution, metrics). It was built before strategies/ existed and has no engulfing/arena tabs.

2 · The GUI tour

uv run gui-hft     # Docker users: MPLBACKEND=Agg is already set in docker-compose.yml

gui_app.py — class App(tk.Tk), six ttk.Notebook tabs Each tab is a form wrapped around one CLI's functionality, run on a background thread so the window doesn't freeze:

TabWrapsWhat you do there
Walkforwardwalkforward-simPick a .joblib bundle + tickers file + dates, optionally pre-download OHLCV, hit Run Walkforward
Train/Backtestpaper-backtestTrain the GBM and save the bundle (Run Backtest + Save Model)
Universe Builderuniverse-builderScrape S&P 500 / NASDAQ ticker lists into tickers/
Newsnews-fetch / news-featuresPull Alpha Vantage sentiment, engineer features (needs ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY)
Executionrh-execPredict + allocate + (dry-run) submit. The "Dry run (no orders)" checkbox defaults to CHECKED — unticking it is the GUI's real-money gate
Analyze Equityanalyze-equityPoint at any equity CSV, get Sharpe/CAGR/MaxDD

Rule of thumb: anything the GUI does, the CLI does too (the tabs call the same functions) — but not the reverse. Strategies, the arena, stress tests, SHAP, and drift checks are CLI-only today.

3 · Running the 2-candle, both ways

Intraday, with stops (the PaperEngine path)

uv run intraday-sim --tickers AAPL,MSFT --start 2026-06-20 \
    --interval 5m --strategy engulfing \
    --position_dollars 1000 --stop_loss_pct 0.005 --take_profit_pct 0.01
# outputs equity.csv + trades.csv; --no_short to go long-only
# intervals: 1m 5m 15m 30m 60m — yfinance only serves ~7 days of 1m bars

Mechanics (strategies/paper_engine.py): a signal on bar N enters at bar N+1's open; each later bar checks stop-loss first (it wins ties with take-profit); any open position force-closes on the day's last bar — never hold overnight.

Daily, in the arena (screen → live → compare)

uv run arena-run backtest --start 2023-01-01 --end 2025-01-01 \
    --strategies engulfing            # or engulfing,technical,meanrev
uv run arena-run live                 # daily tick; breaker + divergence watching
uv run arena-run report

Same pattern code, adapted to daily bars by strategies/candlestick_daily.py (last two daily candles). One behavioral difference to expect: the regime gate keeps engulfing out of trending markets — a reversal pattern is a mean-reversion bet, so on trending days it holds by design (disable with --no_regime_gate to experiment).

4 · Often confused

PairThe difference
GUI Execution tab vs rh-execSame engine — the tab is a form over the executor. Both default to dry-run; the checkbox and --no_dry_run are the same gate wearing two outfits.
intraday-sim engulfing vs arena engulfingIdentical pattern detector, different worlds: 5-minute bars with SL/TP/EOD exits vs daily bars with one-bar holds, costs, sizing, and watchdogs. Their results are NOT comparable to each other.
Train/Backtest tab vs Walkforward tabTrain/Backtest fits the model once on a single split (optimistic, produces the bundle); Walkforward replays history without ever training on the traded day (honest validation). Lesson 0037's rule: validate with the second.
"strategy" in intraday-sim --strategy vs arena --strategiesTwo separate registries: intraday_sim.STRATEGIES (intraday contract, engulfing only today) vs strategies/registry.py (daily contract: engulfing, technical, meanrev, gbm).

5 · Practice

Score: 0 / 0

Q1. You open the GUI looking for a "run engulfing strategy" button. Where is it?

  • Walkforward tab, under strategy dropdown
  • Nowhere — the GUI doesn't drive rule strategies; use intraday-sim or arena-run
  • Execution tab, strategy picker
  • Universe Builder tab

Q2. In an intraday-sim run, a bar triggers BOTH the stop-loss and the take-profit. What happens?

  • Take-profit wins — you get the gain
  • Stop-loss wins — the engine assumes the worse fill
  • The position rides until end of day
  • The two exits average out

Q3. Arena-run live shows engulfing holding on a day when you can SEE a textbook engulfing pattern on the chart. Most likely reason?

  • The daily adapter uses a different pattern definition
  • That day's market regime was classified trending/high_vol, so the gate held it out
  • The circuit breaker paused it
  • Both candles were dojis

Q4. Why does --interval 1m only work for recent dates?

  • PaperEngine can't process that many bars
  • yfinance only provides ~7 days of 1-minute history
  • A repo setting blocks intervals under 5m
  • Alpha Vantage rate limits

Q5. The GUI Execution tab's dry-run checkbox: what's its default, and what does unticking it mean?

  • Unchecked by default; ticking it simulates
  • Checked by default; unticking sends REAL orders via Robinhood
  • It toggles whether predictions run at all
  • It switches between arena paper and live ledgers

6 · Check your understanding (scenarios)

Scenario A. You want to know whether the 2-candle works better with tighter stops. Which engine, which flags, and what do you compare?

Intraday engine — stops only exist there. Two runs differing only in --stop_loss_pct (e.g. 0.005 vs 0.003), same tickers/dates/interval, distinct --out_csv names, then analyze-equity --equity_csv on each. The arena can't answer this: its daily one-bar hold has no stop-loss concept.

Scenario B. Your friend wants to try the platform but is command-line-averse. What CAN you honestly give them via the GUI, and where's the line?

The full GBM lifecycle: train a model (Train/Backtest), validate it (Walkforward), build ticker lists, pull news, compute metrics, and even dry-run executions — all point-and-click. The line: anything strategy-arena related (2-candle, technical, meanrev, ensembles, breaker, reports) is CLI-only today. A GUI arena tab would be a reasonable future issue.

Scenario C. intraday-sim's engulfing made money last week but the arena's engulfing is EXCLUDED. Contradiction?

No — different games. Intraday: 5-minute bars, SL/TP risk control, flat overnight. Arena: daily bars, one-bar holds, transaction costs, screened over years of history. A pattern can have intraday edge and no daily edge (or vice versa). The two results answer different questions and neither invalidates the other.

The lesson walks each GUI tab and what CLI it wraps (including the Execution tab's dry-run checkbox — checked by default; unticking it is the GUI's real-money gate), the exact intraday-sim invocation with its flags, and three scenarios contrasting the engines. content.text:
Shell launcher only — **the .dmg doesn't exist**. The `HFT-Trader-1.0.0.dmg` you've seen is a placeholder in the demo SaaS site (`web/dashboard.html`, `web/pricing.html`) — those download links are fake by design (CLAUDE.md flags them as placeholders; nothing in the repo builds a macOS installer).

What you actually launch with:

| Launcher | What it starts |
|---|---|
| `bash mac-setup.sh` | The full Mac+iPhone setup: checks prereqs (Python 3.12, uv, ngrok), starts the FastAPI web app + ngrok tunnel, prints the public URL, cleans both up on Ctrl-C |
| `uv run gui-hft` | The Tkinter desktop GUI (lesson 0038's six tabs) |
| `uv run web-hft` | Just the FastAPI web app on :8000, no tunnel |
| `docker compose up -d` | Containerized web app (needs `.env.docker`) |

So for the desktop GUI there's no installer at all — it's `uv run gui-hft` from a synced checkout, which is why the setup steps are `git clone` + `uv sync` rather than "download and drag to Applications."

If you ever want a real double-clickable app, the usual route for a Tkinter app would be PyInstaller/py2app producing an `.app` you could wrap in a .dmg — that'd be a reasonable issue to queue (and it would make the SaaS site's download card honest), but it's a real chunk of packaging work, especially with the matplotlib/yfinance dependency tree.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Real-time signal watcher (entry point: live-watch).

Polls recent intraday bars for a set of tickers and runs an intraday
strategy (e.g. the 2-candle engulfing) on the latest COMPLETED bars,
printing a quote line per ticker and highlighting fresh BUY/SELL signals —
a paper-trading tape watcher, not an execution engine.

Honesty notes, because "real time" carries baggage:
  - yfinance intraday bars arrive with roughly a minute of delay and the
    newest bar is still forming until its interval elapses. The watcher
    therefore evaluates only completed bars — signaling off a half-formed
    candle is lookahead's ugly cousin (the candle can un-engulf before it
    closes). Professionals pay for tick feeds (Polygon, Alpaca, IEX,
    exchange direct); this gives you the same *workflow* on a free feed.
  - Signals print to the console/GUI. Nothing is ordered anywhere —
    execution remains rh-exec's job, gated behind --no_dry_run.

Usage:
    uv run live-watch --tickers AAPL,MSFT --interval 5m --refresh 30
    uv run live-watch --tickers AAPL --once        # single pass, then exit
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import time
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Tuple

import pandas as pd

from intraday_sim import STRATEGIES, VALID_INTERVALS
from strategies.base import BaseStrategy, Signal

_INTERVAL_MINUTES = {"1m": 1, "5m": 5, "15m": 15, "30m": 30, "60m": 60}


def completed_bars(df: pd.DataFrame, interval: str, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Drop the still-forming final bar, if it is still forming.

    A bar stamped T covers [T, T+interval); it is complete once
    now >= T + interval. After the session closes the last bar is complete
    and must NOT be dropped — a naive "always drop the last row" would
    permanently hide the day's final signal.
    """
    if df.empty:
        return df
    minutes = _INTERVAL_MINUTES[interval]
    last_start = df.index[-1]
    if now is None:
        now = dt.datetime.now(tz=getattr(last_start, "tz", None))
    bar_end = last_start + dt.timedelta(minutes=minutes)
    if now < bar_end:
        return df.iloc[:-1]
    return df


def evaluate_latest(df: pd.DataFrame, strategy: BaseStrategy) -> Tuple[pd.Timestamp, Signal] | None:
    """Run the 2-bar strategy on the last two completed bars.

    Returns (bar_timestamp, Signal) or None when fewer than 2 bars exist.
    """
    if len(df) < 2:
        return None
    prev, curr = df.iloc[-2], df.iloc[-1]
    return df.index[-1], strategy.generate_signal(prev, curr)


def format_tick_line(ticker: str, bar_ts, price: float, signal: Signal, fresh: bool) -> str:
    """One human-readable tape line; fresh non-hold signals shout."""
    ts = pd.Timestamp(bar_ts).strftime("%H:%M")
    base = f"{ticker:6s} bar {ts}  close={price:,.2f}  {signal.direction}"
    if fresh and signal.direction != "HOLD":
        return f"{base}   <<< NEW SIGNAL"
    return base


def watch_once(tickers: List[str], strategy: BaseStrategy, interval: str,
               fetch: Callable[[str, str], pd.DataFrame],
               seen: Dict[str, pd.Timestamp],
               now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> List[str]:
    """One polling pass over all tickers. Mutates ``seen`` (last bar per
    ticker) so a bar only ever counts as a fresh signal once.

    Returns the formatted lines (pure-ish: printing is the caller's job,
    which keeps this testable and lets the GUI reuse it verbatim).
    """
    lines = []
    for ticker in tickers:
        try:
            df = fetch(ticker, interval)
        except Exception as exc:  # one dead ticker must not kill the tape
            lines.append(f"{ticker:6s} fetch error: {exc}")
            continue
        df = completed_bars(df, interval, now=now)
        result = evaluate_latest(df, strategy)
        if result is None:
            lines.append(f"{ticker:6s} waiting for bars...")
            continue
        bar_ts, signal = result
        fresh = seen.get(ticker) != bar_ts
        seen[ticker] = bar_ts
        lines.append(format_tick_line(ticker, bar_ts, float(df["Close"].iloc[-1]), signal, fresh))
    return lines


def _default_fetch(ticker: str, interval: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch ~2 days of intraday bars (network path, excluded from tests)."""
    import yfinance as yf

    df = yf.download(ticker, period="2d", interval=interval,
                     auto_adjust=True, progress=False)
    if isinstance(df.columns, pd.MultiIndex):
        df.columns = df.columns.get_level_values(0)
    return df


def main() -> None:
    """CLI entry point for live-watch."""
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Watch live intraday bars and print strategy signals")
    p.add_argument("--tickers", type=str, required=True, help="Comma-separated, e.g. AAPL,MSFT")
    p.add_argument("--interval", type=str, default="5m", choices=sorted(VALID_INTERVALS))
    p.add_argument("--strategy", type=str, default="engulfing", choices=list(STRATEGIES))
    p.add_argument("--refresh", type=int, default=30, help="Seconds between polls (default 30)")
    p.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="Single pass, then exit")
    args = p.parse_args()

    tickers = [t.strip().upper() for t in args.tickers.split(",") if t.strip()]
    strategy = STRATEGIES[args.strategy]()
    seen: Dict[str, pd.Timestamp] = {}

    print(f"Watching {', '.join(tickers)} on {args.interval} bars with '{args.strategy}' "
          f"(refresh {args.refresh}s; completed bars only; Ctrl-C to stop)")
    while True:
        stamp = dt.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        for line in watch_once(tickers, strategy, args.interval, _default_fetch, seen):
            print(f"[{stamp}] {line}")
        if args.once:
            break
        try:
            time.sleep(args.refresh)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\nstopped")
            break


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Tests for live_watch.py — completed-bar logic, signal evaluation, and the
fresh-signal dedupe. All offline: fetch is injected, no yfinance."""
import datetime as dt

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from live_watch import completed_bars, evaluate_latest, format_tick_line, watch_once
from strategies.engulfing import EngulfingStrategy


def _bars(rows, start="2026-07-13 09:30", freq="5min"):
    """Intraday OHLCV frame from (open, close) tuples."""
    idx = pd.date_range(start, periods=len(rows), freq=freq)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"Open": [o for o, _ in rows], "High": [max(o, c) * 1.001 for o, c in rows],
         "Low": [min(o, c) * 0.999 for o, c in rows], "Close": [c for _, c in rows],
         "Volume": [1000] * len(rows)}, index=idx)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# completed_bars
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_forming_bar_is_dropped_mid_interval():
    df = _bars([(100, 101), (101, 102), (102, 103)])
    # "now" is 2 minutes into the last 5m bar (bar starts 09:40) -> forming
    now = dt.datetime(2026, 7, 13, 9, 42)
    out = completed_bars(df, "5m", now=now)
    assert len(out) == 2
    assert out.index[-1] == df.index[-2]


def test_last_bar_kept_once_its_interval_has_elapsed():
    df = _bars([(100, 101), (101, 102), (102, 103)])
    # last bar starts 09:40, ends 09:45 — at 09:45 sharp it is complete
    now = dt.datetime(2026, 7, 13, 9, 45)
    out = completed_bars(df, "5m", now=now)
    assert len(out) == 3  # nothing dropped — the day's final signal survives


def test_completed_bars_empty_frame_passthrough():
    empty = pd.DataFrame()
    assert completed_bars(empty, "5m").empty


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# evaluate_latest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_evaluate_needs_two_bars():
    assert evaluate_latest(_bars([(100, 101)]), EngulfingStrategy()) is None


def test_evaluate_detects_bullish_engulfing_on_last_two_bars():
    # prev red (105->100), curr green engulfing (99->106)
    df = _bars([(100, 100), (105, 100), (99, 106)])
    ts, signal = evaluate_latest(df, EngulfingStrategy())
    assert ts == df.index[-1]
    assert signal.direction == "BUY"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# watch_once: dedupe + error isolation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_watch_once_flags_signal_fresh_only_once():
    df = _bars([(100, 100), (105, 100), (99, 106)])  # ends in a BUY
    fetch = lambda ticker, interval: df
    seen = {}
    now = dt.datetime(2026, 7, 13, 10, 0)  # all bars long complete

    first = watch_once(["AAA"], EngulfingStrategy(), "5m", fetch, seen, now=now)
    second = watch_once(["AAA"], EngulfingStrategy(), "5m", fetch, seen, now=now)
    assert "NEW SIGNAL" in first[0]
    assert "NEW SIGNAL" not in second[0]  # same bar -> not fresh again
    assert "BUY" in second[0]             # but the state is still shown


def test_watch_once_isolates_a_failing_ticker():
    good = _bars([(100, 100), (105, 100), (99, 106)])

    def fetch(ticker, interval):
        if ticker == "BAD":
            raise RuntimeError("feed down")
        return good

    lines = watch_once(["BAD", "AAA"], EngulfingStrategy(), "5m", fetch, {},
                       now=dt.datetime(2026, 7, 13, 10, 0))
    assert "fetch error" in lines[0]
    assert "BUY" in lines[1]  # the healthy ticker still evaluated


def test_format_tick_line_hold_never_shouts():
    sig_hold = EngulfingStrategy().generate_signal(
        _bars([(100, 101), (101, 102)]).iloc[0], _bars([(100, 101), (101, 102)]).iloc[1])
    line = format_tick_line("AAPL", pd.Timestamp("2026-07-13 09:35"), 102.0, sig_hold, fresh=True)
    assert "NEW SIGNAL" not in line
    assert "HOLD" in line

Done — the GUI is relaunched with everything you asked for. Here's the rundown:

## 1. Scrolling ✅
Every tab now lives in a `ScrollableTab` (canvas + scrollbar, the standard Tkinter pattern). Content wraps to the window width, the scrollbar appears when content overflows, and the mouse wheel works — bound only while your pointer is over a tab, so tabs don't fight over it. All existing tab layouts unchanged.

## 2. Running the 2-candle — now three ways
- **NEW — GUI "Live Signals" tab** (rightmost): enter tickers, pick `engulfing` + interval + refresh, hit **Start Watching**. A tape scrolls with each ticker's latest completed bar, price, and signal — fresh BUY/SELLs highlighted in bold green. Stop button ends it. Read-only by design: nothing is ordered from this tab, execution stays behind the Execution tab / `rh-exec` gate.
- **CLI intraday backtest:** `uv run intraday-sim --tickers AAPL --start 2026-07-06 --interval 5m --strategy engulfing` (stop-loss/take-profit engine, results to CSVs)
- **CLI daily arena:** `arena-run backtest --strategies engulfing` → `arena-run live` → `arena-run report` (lesson 0038 covers all three in depth)

## 3. Real-time signal reading ✅ — with honest caveats
New `live-watch` CLI (same engine as the GUI tab): `uv run live-watch --tickers AAPL,MSFT --interval 5m --refresh 30`. I verified it against the real feed just now — it correctly pulled Friday's closing bars and flagged a genuine bullish engulfing on AAPL's final 5-minute bar.

Two design points that matter for "like real day traders and quant engineers":
- **Completed bars only.** The newest candle is still forming until its interval elapses — it can *un-engulf* before it closes, so signaling off it is lookahead's ugly cousin. The watcher drops forming bars (but keeps the day's final bar after the close — that edge case is test-pinned).
- **yfinance runs ~1 minute delayed.** This gives you the professional *workflow* on a free feed. Actual pros pay for tick-level feeds (Polygon, Alpaca, IEX Cloud — roughly $30–200/mo tiers); if you ever want that, the `fetch` function in `live_watch.py` is injectable, so a Polygon websocket adapter would slot in without touching the signal logic.

All committed and pushed on `feature/gui-scroll-live-signals` (stacked on your PR chain), 8 new tests, **201 passing** total. The GUI window that just opened has the new tab — try Start Watching with the defaults; even on a closed market it'll show Friday's bars and that AAPL BUY.

# Plan: Statistical Rigor — Deflated Sharpe, t-Stat Promotion Gate, Purged CV
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: L

## The Idea (one paragraph)
The arena currently promotes strategies on a lenient bar (Sharpe > 0) that a
lucky coin-flipper clears half the time. This adds the standard defenses from
the quant-research literature: a Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & López de
Prado) that discounts each backtest Sharpe by how many trials were ever run
(tracked honestly in a persistent ledger), a Harvey-Liu-style t-statistic
promotion gate (t ≥ 3.0 for full PASS), and purged/embargoed K-fold
cross-validation for the GBM model so overlapping return windows can't leak
training information into evaluation.

## Goal
A strategy's arena status now answers "is this edge statistically real given
everything I've tried?" instead of "was it above zero once" — and the GBM's
evaluation numbers survive the leakage audit a quant interviewer would run.

## Decisions Made (were open questions)
- **Two-tier gate** (user decision): t ≥ 3.0 AND DSR ≥ 0.95 → `PASS`;
  2.0 ≤ t < 3.0 (or t ≥ 3.0 with DSR < 0.95) → new `PROBATION` status —
  trades live paper exactly like PASS but is prominently flagged as
  statistically unproven in every report; t < 2.0 → `EXCLUDED`. The MaxDD
  bound still applies to both live tiers. Context that drove this: t ≈
  Sharpe_ann × √years, so a 2-year window demands Sharpe ≈ 2.1 for t=3 — a
  hard gate would leave the arena empty for years and kill its
  compare-live-track-records purpose.
- **Persistent trial ledger** (user decision): every `arena-run backtest`
  appends one row per (strategy, config) to a `trials` table in arena.db —
  config-hash (sha256 of strategy name + sizing + cost mode + window +
  tickers + top_n) as PK, `INSERT OR REPLACE` so identical re-runs update
  rather than inflate. N = COUNT(trials); cross-trial Sharpe variance feeds
  the expected-max-Sharpe term. `--n_trials` overrides for what-if analysis.
- **Purged CV scoped to where leakage actually lives** (my call,
  documented): the arena's generic walk-forward has NO training step for
  rule strategies — "switching" it to CV would be cargo cult. Purging
  applies to (a) a new purged/embargoed K-fold evaluation mode for the GBM
  (`paper-backtest --purged_cv`), and (b) an actual live bug: `split_by_time`
  in paper_trading_sim.py puts the boundary row's label (which contains the
  first test day's return) in the TRAINING set — a 1-day leak, fixed by
  purging `label_horizon` rows at the split. Walk-forward remains the
  arena's engine; CPCV (combinatorial) is out of scope.
- **PROBATION interactions**: breaker and divergence watchdogs apply to
  PROBATION identically to PASS. Ensembles may include PROBATION members
  (their weights come from live track records anyway) but the ensemble
  itself inherits PROBATION status if any member is on probation — a chain
  is as proven as its weakest link.
- **Statuses are recomputed only at screen time.** Live performance never
  upgrades PROBATION → PASS automatically; you re-run `arena-run backtest`
  over a longer window when you believe the evidence has accumulated.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Combinatorial Purged CV (CPCV) and walk-forward path resampling
- Multiple-testing corrections on the LIVE divergence/drift alerts (they
  remain per-strategy; noted caveat stands)
- Retro-fitting the trial ledger with screens run before this feature
  (N starts counting from deployment; documented)
- False Discovery Rate control across strategy families (Benjamini-Hochberg
  etc.) — DSR's expected-max adjustment is this version's answer
- Any change to real-money gating (rh-exec untouched, as always)

## Affected Areas
- New: `sharpe_stats.py` (root py-module) — pure math, no I/O:
  `t_stat(mean_daily, std_daily, n_days)`;
  `probabilistic_sharpe(sr, skew, kurt, n) -> float` (PSR vs SR₀=0);
  `expected_max_sharpe(n_trials, var_trial_sr) -> float` (E[max SR] under
  the null, Euler–Mascheroni form);
  `deflated_sharpe(sr, skew, kurt, n, sr0) -> float`.
  Every function hand-verifiable against the Bailey–LdP paper's examples.
- `strategy_arena.py` —
  `_SCHEMA`: new `trials` table (config_hash PK, strategy, sharpe_daily,
  n_days, screened_at); `record_trial()` + `trial_stats()` (N, var of trial
  SRs) on ArenaState.
  `cmd_backtest`: compute daily-return t-stat, skew, kurtosis; record the
  trial; derive status via the two-tier gate (`--t_pass 3.0`,
  `--t_probation 2.0`, `--dsr_pass 0.95`, `--n_trials` override); print
  t/DSR per strategy with the tier verdict.
  `cmd_live` + `cmd_ensemble`: treat `PROBATION` as live-eligible everywhere
  `PASS` currently is; ensemble status inherits PROBATION from any member.
- `analyze_equity.py` — `compare_strategies`: new `t_stat` and `dsr` columns
  (from the strategies row, stored at screen time), status column now
  surfaces PROBATION.
- New: `purged_cv.py` (root py-module) —
  `PurgedKFold(n_splits=5, purge=1, embargo_frac=0.01)` with
  `split(index) -> (train_idx, test_idx)` pairs: contiguous test folds,
  training rows within `purge` labels of the test block dropped, plus an
  embargo strip after each test block;
  `evaluate_purged_cv(feats, feat_cols, n_splits, ...) -> DataFrame` — fits
  the GBM per fold, reports per-fold OOS hit-rate, IC (rank corr of pred vs
  realized), and mean return of top-decile predictions.
- `paper_trading_sim.py` — `split_by_time` gains `purge: int = 1`, dropping
  the last `purge` rows of the training split (the boundary leak fix —
  changes existing single-split results slightly, which is the point);
  `main` gains `--purged_cv` printing the fold table after (or instead of)
  the standard run.
- Migration note: `trials` is a new table (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS — no ALTER
  needed); `strategies.status` already TEXT, PROBATION needs no schema
  change. Existing DBs upgrade in place, consistent with prior migrations.
- New tests: `tests/test_sharpe_stats.py` (hand-computed PSR/E[maxSR]/DSR
  pins), `tests/test_purged_cv.py` (no train index within purge+embargo of
  any test index — property-checked; boundary-leak regression on
  split_by_time), `tests/test_trial_ledger.py` (hash dedupe, N growth,
  two-tier gate transitions incl. PROBATION live-eligibility and ensemble
  inheritance).

## Implementation Order
1. `sharpe_stats.py` + paper-pinned unit tests — pure math first, no
   behavior change anywhere.
2. `purged_cv.py` + `split_by_time` purge fix + `--purged_cv` CLI — the
   leakage half, independent of the arena.
3. Trial ledger in ArenaState (`trials` table, record/stats) + tests —
   still no gate change.
4. Two-tier gate in `cmd_backtest` + PROBATION handling in
   `cmd_live`/`cmd_ensemble`/report + tests — the behavior flip, last,
   after all its inputs exist.
5. Docs: CLAUDE.md conventions note; PROGRESS.md next-lesson suggestion
   ("why your backtest Sharpe is a maximum, not an estimate").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sharpe_stats` reproduces a hand-computed PSR and DSR case to 1e-9,
      and `expected_max_sharpe` is monotonically increasing in N
- [ ] Screening the same config twice leaves N unchanged (hash dedupe);
      screening a new window/config increments N
- [ ] A synthetic strategy with t ≈ 4 and DSR > 0.95 lands PASS; t ≈ 2.5
      lands PROBATION and still receives live ticks; t ≈ 1 lands EXCLUDED
- [ ] PROBATION rows are visibly tiered in `arena-run report` (status +
      t_stat + dsr columns)
- [ ] An ensemble containing one PROBATION member reports PROBATION itself
- [ ] `PurgedKFold`: property test — no training index falls within
      `purge` labels before or `embargo` after any test block, across
      random fold counts and lengths
- [ ] `split_by_time(purge=1)`: the last training row's `fwd_ret_1d` no
      longer overlaps the first test row's return window (regression-pinned
      against the old leaky split)
- [ ] `paper-backtest --purged_cv` prints one row per fold with OOS
      hit-rate and IC, no fold trained on purged rows
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| N = 1 trial (first ever screen) | E[max SR] term ≈ 0 → DSR degrades to plain PSR; gate still functions on t-stat |
| Cross-trial SR variance is 0 (identical trials) | expected_max_sharpe returns 0, not NaN — guarded |
| Backtest window too short for kurtosis estimation (< ~30 days) | DSR reported as None with a printed note; t-stat still computed; gate falls back to t-only |
| Strategy screened pre-feature (no t/dsr stored) | Report shows blanks; status untouched until re-screened |
| `--n_trials` given smaller than ledger N | Used as given but printed with a warning — what-if mode is explicit, never silent |
| PurgedKFold with purge+embargo consuming an entire fold | Raises with a clear message (too many splits for the data), never yields an empty train set silently |
| PROBATION strategy trips the drawdown breaker | PAUSED as usual; `arena-run resume` returns it to PROBATION (its screened tier), not PASS |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(stats): sharpe_stats.py — PSR, expected-max Sharpe, Deflated Sharpe` — pure math + paper-pinned tests
2. `feat(cv): purged/embargoed K-fold + split_by_time boundary-leak fix` — purged_cv.py, --purged_cv CLI, regression pin
3. `feat(arena): persistent trial ledger with config-hash dedupe` — trials table, N/variance stats
4. `feat(arena): two-tier PASS/PROBATION promotion gate wired to t-stat + DSR` — gate, live/ensemble/report handling

- [ ] Screening the same config twice leaves N unchanged (hash dedupe);

- [ ] A synthetic strategy with t ≈ 4 and DSR > 0.95 lands PASS; t ≈ 2.5

- [ ] PROBATION rows are visibly tiered in `arena-run report` (status +

- [ ] An ensemble containing one PROBATION member reports PROBATION itself

- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| N = 1 trial (first ever screen) | E[max SR] term ≈ 0 → DSR degrades to plain PSR; gate still functions on t-stat |

content.text:
This one overlaps heavily with work already shipped — the honest starting point is what's *left*. PR #63's `costs.py` (issue #55) already delivers most of it: commission defaults to $0 (Robinhood), a half-spread term is the dominant flat cost, and impact scales by √(position notional / 20-day dollar volume). What it does **not** do — and where this idea has real teeth — is three things:

1. **Per-ticker spread** — today's `half_spread_bps` is one flat number for every ticker; "each ticker's typical spread" needs estimation from data.
2. **Cost-fragility flagging** — today net-of-cost metrics feed the filter, so a cost-killed strategy just fails quietly; there's no explicit "the edge existed gross and died in costs" flag.
3. **The deferred wiring** — the GBM `simulate_walkforward` and `paper_trading_sim.simulate` still use the legacy flat cost (recorded deferral from #55).

The idea is clear enough to plan the delta without questions. The one methodology choice — how to estimate per-ticker spread from OHLCV-only data — has a standard defensible answer (Corwin–Schultz high-low estimator, no new data source, no new dependency, with a flat-bps fallback), so I'm making that call and documenting it.

# Plan: Per-Ticker Spread Costs & Cost-Fragility Flagging
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Builds on the existing cost model (`costs.py`, issue #55): commission is
already $0-default and impact already scales with position size vs average
dollar volume. This plan adds the two missing pieces plus one deferred one:
(1) the spread term becomes per-ticker, estimated from each ticker's own
OHLC data via the Corwin–Schultz high-low estimator instead of one flat
bps number for the whole universe; (2) a strategy whose edge exists gross
but dies net-of-costs gets an explicit COST-FRAGILE flag in the screen
output and report — not just a quietly lower rank; (3) the realistic cost
model finally reaches the GBM `simulate_walkforward` and
`paper_trading_sim.simulate` loops, closing #55's recorded deferral.

## Goal
Screening output answers "which strategies only look profitable because the
backtest ignored what THIS ticker actually costs to trade" — explicitly,
per strategy, with the spread cost grounded in each ticker's own data.

## Relationship to Existing Work (read first)
`costs.py` (PR #63) already provides: `CostModel` (none/flat/realistic),
commission_bps=0 default, flat half_spread_bps=2.5, sqrt-impact on
participation (notional / 20-day Volume×Close), turnover-based charging,
dual-track `equity`/`equity_gross`/`cost` columns in
`run_strategy_walkforward`, arena CLI flags. This plan EXTENDS that module —
it must not fork a second cost model.

## Design Decisions (documented, none blocking)
- **Spread estimator: Corwin–Schultz (2012)** — uses only High/Low columns
  already in every fetched frame; no new data source, no new dependency.
  Per-ticker daily estimates are noisy, so the usable number is a rolling
  60-day median, floored at 1 bps and capped at 200 bps (sanity bounds),
  negative daily estimates floored at 0 per the paper's convention.
  Fallback chain: estimate unavailable/degenerate → the existing flat
  `half_spread_bps` → never zero. `CostModel` gains
  `spread_mode: "flat" | "estimated"` (default "flat" — no silent change
  to existing results; "estimated" is opt-in like "realistic" was).
- **Cost-fragile definition**: run the promotion gate twice per strategy at
  screen time — once on gross metrics, once on net. `cost_fragile = True`
  when gross passes but net fails. Implemented against the gate FUNCTION,
  not hardcoded thresholds, so it composes unchanged with the planned
  two-tier t-stat gate (statistical-rigor plan). Also computed:
  `cost_drag = gross_CAGR − net_CAGR`, shown always. Fragile strategies
  keep their net-based status (usually EXCLUDED) — the flag explains WHY,
  loudly, in both the screen printout and a `cost_fragile` report column.
- **GBM/paper_trading_sim wiring** mirrors `run_strategy_walkforward`'s
  pattern exactly: turnover from |Δweight| per ticker (meanvar weights in
  simulate_walkforward; equal-weight pick-set changes in
  paper_trading_sim), same provisional-day conventions, same dual-track
  columns, `--cost_model` flags on both CLIs, default `flat` (legacy
  behavior regression-pinned, same discipline as #55).

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Quote-based (NBBO) spreads — needs a paid feed; the injectable design
  leaves room for a later adapter
- Intraday PaperEngine costs (still its own world)
- Time-varying spread within a day; one estimate per ticker per day
- Changing the DEFAULT spread_mode to "estimated" (flip later, deliberately,
  after comparing outputs)
- Half-spread vs full-spread execution modeling nuances (we charge the
  half-spread per side, as now — only its VALUE becomes per-ticker)

## Affected Areas
- `costs.py` — `estimate_spread_bps(df, window=60) -> pd.Series`
  (Corwin–Schultz with the smoothing/floor/cap above);
  `CostModel.spread_mode` field; `one_way_cost_bps` gains an optional
  `half_spread_bps_override` (per-ticker value threaded per trade, falling
  back to the model's flat value).
- `walkforward_sim.py` — `run_strategy_walkforward`: when
  `spread_mode == "estimated"`, precompute per-ticker spread series next to
  the existing `adv` dict and pass the day's value into `day_cost`'s
  weight_changes tuples (extends the `(dw, adv)` tuple to
  `(dw, adv, spread_bps)`); `simulate_walkforward` gains `cost_model`
  wiring with per-date weight tracking mirroring the generic loop.
- `paper_trading_sim.py` — `simulate` gains `cost_model` on
  `BacktestConfig`, turnover from pick-set changes, dual-track columns,
  `--cost_model` CLI flag.
- `strategy_arena.py` — `cmd_backtest`: gross-vs-net double gate evaluation,
  `cost_fragile` + `cost_drag` persisted on the strategies row (two new
  guarded ALTER columns), loud printout for fragile strategies;
  `--spread_mode` CLI flag threaded through.
- `analyze_equity.py` — `compare_strategies`: `cost_fragile`, `cost_drag`
  columns.
- New tests: `tests/test_spread_estimate.py` (CS formula pinned against a
  hand-computed two-day case; floor/cap/fallback chain; wide-spread
  synthetic ticker estimates higher than tight-spread one),
  cost-fragility cases in `tests/test_strategy_arena.py` (gross-pass/
  net-fail flips the flag; gross-fail never flags; flag composes with the
  gate function), regression pins for the two newly-wired loops
  (`--cost_model flat` byte-identical to current output).

## Implementation Order
1. `estimate_spread_bps` in costs.py + unit tests — pure math, nothing
   consumes it yet.
2. Per-ticker spread threading in `run_strategy_walkforward`
   (`spread_mode="estimated"`) + tests (tight vs wide synthetic tickers pay
   visibly different costs; flat mode regression-pinned).
3. Cost-fragility double-gate in `cmd_backtest` + report columns + schema
   migration + tests.
4. Deferred wiring: `simulate_walkforward` + `paper_trading_sim.simulate`
   cost model support with flat-mode regression pins.
5. Docs: CLAUDE.md conventions note; PROGRESS.md lesson suggestion
   ("estimating what you can't observe: spreads from OHLC").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Corwin–Schultz on a hand-computed 2-day High/Low case matches the
      paper's formula to 1e-9; negative daily estimates floor at 0
- [ ] A synthetic wide-range ticker's estimated spread exceeds a
      tight-range ticker's, and both respect the [1, 200] bps bounds
- [ ] Missing High/Low columns → fallback to flat half_spread_bps with one
      logged notice, never zero spread and never a crash
- [ ] `spread_mode="flat"` (default) reproduces current realistic-mode
      equity exactly (regression-pinned)
- [ ] Under `spread_mode="estimated"`, identical trades in a wide-spread
      ticker cost more than in a tight-spread one (integration test)
- [ ] A strategy engineered to pass on gross metrics and fail on net shows
      `cost_fragile=True`, prints a loud verdict at screen time, and
      appears flagged in `arena-run report`; a strategy failing on gross
      too shows `cost_fragile=False`
- [ ] `simulate_walkforward` and `paper_trading_sim.simulate` accept a
      CostModel; `--cost_model flat` is byte-identical to today for both
      (regression-pinned); `realistic` produces equity/equity_gross/cost
      columns
- [ ] Pre-existing arena DBs migrate in place (two new columns)
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Fewer than ~3 bars of High/Low (estimator undefined) | Fallback to flat half_spread_bps for that ticker/day |
| High == Low for a stretch (halted/illiquid ticker) | CS estimate degenerates to 0 → floored to 1 bps minimum, not free trading |
| Adjusted data where Low > High (bad row) | Row skipped in estimation window; fallback if window becomes empty |
| Gate is later replaced by the two-tier t-stat gate | Fragility calls the gate function with gross vs net inputs — no code change needed here |
| Strategy passes net but cost_drag is huge (edge survives, barely) | Not flagged fragile (it survived) — but cost_drag column makes the margin visible |
| spread_mode="estimated" with a ticker missing Volume (no ADV) | Spread estimation is independent of Volume; impact term falls back to fallback_adv as today |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(costs): Corwin–Schultz per-ticker spread estimation` — estimate_spread_bps + bounds/fallback chain + pinned tests
2. `feat(costs): spread_mode=estimated threading in run_strategy_walkforward` — per-ticker spread in day_cost, regression pins
3. `feat(arena): cost-fragility double gate + cost_drag reporting` — gross-vs-net verdicts, schema migration, loud flagging
4. `feat(costs): wire CostModel into simulate_walkforward and paper_trading_sim (closes #55's deferral)` — flat-mode regression pins

- **Spread estimator: Corwin–Schultz (2012)** — uses only High/Low columns
  already in every fetched frame; no new data source, no new dependency.
  Per-ticker daily estimates are noisy, so the usable number is a rolling
  60-day median, floored at 1 bps and capped at 200 bps (sanity bounds),
  negative daily estimates floored at 0 per the paper's convention.
  Fallback chain: estimate unavailable/degenerate → the existing flat
  `half_spread_bps` → never zero. `CostModel` gains
  `spread_mode: "flat" | "estimated"` (default "flat" — no silent change
  to existing results; "estimated" is opt-in like "realistic" was).
- **Cost-fragile definition**: run the promotion gate twice per strategy at
  screen time — once on gross metrics, once on net. `cost_fragile = True`
  when gross passes but net fails. Implemented against the gate FUNCTION,
  not hardcoded thresholds, so it composes unchanged with the planned
  two-tier t-stat gate (statistical-rigor plan). Also computed:
  `cost_drag = gross_CAGR − net_CAGR`, shown always. Fragile strategies
  keep their net-based status (usually EXCLUDED) — the flag explains WHY,
  loudly, in both the screen printout and a `cost_fragile` report column.
- **GBM/paper_trading_sim wiring** mirrors `run_strategy_walkforward`'s
  pattern exactly: turnover from |Δweight| per ticker (meanvar weights in
  simulate_walkforward; equal-weight pick-set changes in
  paper_trading_sim), same provisional-day conventions, same dual-track
  columns, `--cost_model` flags on both CLIs, default `flat` (legacy
  behavior regression-pinned, same discipline as #55).

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Quote-based (NBBO) spreads — needs a paid feed; the injectable design
  leaves room for a later adapter
- Intraday PaperEngine costs (still its own world)
- Time-varying spread within a day; one estimate per ticker per day
- Changing the DEFAULT spread_mode to "estimated" (flip later, deliberately,
  after comparing outputs)
- Half-spread vs full-spread execution modeling nuances (we charge the
  half-spread per side, as now — only its VALUE becomes per-ticker)

## Affected Areas
- `costs.py` — `estimate_spread_bps(df, window=60) -> pd.Series`
  (Corwin–Schultz with the smoothing/floor/cap above);
  `CostModel.spread_mode` field; `one_way_cost_bps` gains an optional
  `half_spread_bps_override` (per-ticker value threaded per trade, falling
  back to the model's flat value).
- `walkforward_sim.py` — `run_strategy_walkforward`: when
  `spread_mode == "estimated"`, precompute per-ticker spread series next to
  the existing `adv` dict and pass the day's value into `day_cost`'s
  weight_changes tuples (extends the `(dw, adv)` tuple to
  `(dw, adv, spread_bps)`); `simulate_walkforward` gains `cost_model`
  wiring with per-date weight tracking mirroring the generic loop.
- `paper_trading_sim.py` — `simulate` gains `cost_model` on
  `BacktestConfig`, turnover from pick-set changes, dual-track columns,
  `--cost_model` CLI flag.
- `strategy_arena.py` — `cmd_backtest`: gross-vs-net double gate evaluation,
  `cost_fragile` + `cost_drag` persisted on the strategies row (two new
  guarded ALTER columns), loud printout for fragile strategies;
  `--spread_mode` CLI flag threaded through.
- `analyze_equity.py` — `compare_strategies`: `cost_fragile`, `cost_drag`
  columns.
- New tests: `tests/test_spread_estimate.py` (CS formula pinned against a
  hand-computed two-day case; floor/cap/fallback chain; wide-spread
  synthetic ticker estimates higher than tight-spread one),
  cost-fragility cases in `tests/test_strategy_arena.py` (gross-pass/
  net-fail flips the flag; gross-fail never flags; flag composes with the
  gate function), regression pins for the two newly-wired loops
  (`--cost_model flat` byte-identical to current output).

## Implementation Order
1. `estimate_spread_bps` in costs.py + unit tests — pure math, nothing
   consumes it yet.
2. Per-ticker spread threading in `run_strategy_walkforward`
   (`spread_mode="estimated"`) + tests (tight vs wide synthetic tickers pay
   visibly different costs; flat mode regression-pinned).
3. Cost-fragility double-gate in `cmd_backtest` + report columns + schema
   migration + tests.
4. Deferred wiring: `simulate_walkforward` + `paper_trading_sim.simulate`
   cost model support with flat-mode regression pins.
5. Docs: CLAUDE.md conventions note; PROGRESS.md lesson suggestion
   ("estimating what you can't observe: spreads from OHLC").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Corwin–Schultz on a hand-computed 2-day High/Low case matches the
      paper's formula to 1e-9; negative daily estimates floor at 0
- [ ] A synthetic wide-range ticker's estimated spread exceeds a
      tight-range ticker's, and both respect the [1, 200] bps bounds
- [ ] Missing High/Low columns → fallback to flat half_spread_bps with one
      logged notice, never zero spread and never a crash
- [ ] `spread_mode="flat"` (default) reproduces current realistic-mode
      equity exactly (regression-pinned)
- [ ] Under `spread_mode="estimated"`, identical trades in a wide-spread
      ticker cost more than in a tight-spread one (integration test)
- [ ] A strategy engineered to pass on gross metrics and fail on net shows
      `cost_fragile=True`, prints a loud verdict at screen time, and
      appears flagged in `arena-run report`; a strategy failing on gross
      too shows `cost_fragile=False`
- [ ] `simulate_walkforward` and `paper_trading_sim.simulate` accept a
      CostModel; `--cost_model flat` is byte-identical to today for both
      (regression-pinned); `realistic` produces equity/equity_gross/cost
      columns
- [ ] Pre-existing arena DBs migrate in place (two new columns)
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Fewer than ~3 bars of High/Low (estimator undefined) | Fallback to flat half_spread_bps for that ticker/day |
| High == Low for a stretch (halted/illiquid ticker) | CS estimate degenerates to 0 → floored to 1 bps minimum, not free trading |
| Adjusted data where Low > High (bad row) | Row skipped in estimation window; fallback if window becomes empty |
| Gate is later replaced by the two-tier t-stat gate | Fragility calls the gate function with gross vs net inputs — no code change needed here |
| Strategy passes net but cost_drag is huge (edge survives, barely) | Not flagged fragile (it survived) — but cost_drag column makes the margin visible |
| spread_mode="estimated" with a ticker missing Volume (no ADV) | Spread estimation is independent of Volume; impact term falls back to fallback_adv as today |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

1. `feat(costs): Corwin–Schultz per-ticker spread estimation` — estimate_spread_bps + bounds/fallback chain + pinned tests
2. `feat(costs): spread_mode=estimated threading in run_strategy_walkforward` — per-ticker spread in day_cost, regression pins
3. `feat(arena): cost-fragility double gate + cost_drag reporting` — gross-vs-net verdicts, schema migration, loud flagging

You are turning "" into a structured, actionable plan document.

This command has two phases:
- PHASE 1: Interrogate the idea until it is unambiguous
- PHASE 2: Produce the plan document

Do not skip to Phase 2 until Phase 1 is complete.

---

## PHASE 1 — INTERROGATE THE IDEA

Read the codebase first so your questions are grounded in reality:
```bash
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -30
git log --oneline -10
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null || true
```

Then ask clarifying questions — ONE at a time, wait for the answer,
then ask the next. Do not dump a list of questions all at once.
A question only gets asked if you genuinely cannot write a good plan
without knowing the answer.

Things worth asking about (pick the most important ones):

**Scope:**
- What does done look like? What can a user DO when this is complete?
- What is explicitly OUT of scope for this version?
- Is this a new feature, a change to existing behaviour, or a fix?

**Users and context:**
- Who uses this and in what situation?
- What do they have / know before they reach this feature?

**Technical constraints:**
- Does this touch existing code that other things depend on?
- Any performance, security, or compatibility requirements?
- Any third-party APIs or libraries involved?

**Edge cases:**
- What happens when the input is invalid or missing?
- What's the failure mode and how should it be handled?

**Priority:**
- Does this need to be done in a specific order relative to other work?
- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

Stop asking when you have enough to write a plan that could be handed
to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask
you anything.

---

## PHASE 2 — PRODUCE THE PLAN DOCUMENT

Save to `.claude/plans/[slug].md` where slug is a short dash-case
name derived from the idea. Example: "add weapon inventory" →
`.claude/plans/weapon-inventory.md`

The document structure:

```markdown
# Plan: [Feature Name]
Date: [date]
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S / M / L / XL

## The Idea (one paragraph)
[What this is, in plain language. Someone unfamiliar with the codebase
should understand this in 30 seconds.]

## Goal
[One sentence: what a user can DO when this is shipped that they
cannot do now.]

## Out of Scope (this version)
[Explicit list of things NOT included. This prevents scope creep
during implementation.]

## Affected Areas
[Files, modules, or systems this touches. Be specific.]
- `src/path/to/file.py` — [why it changes]
- `src/path/to/other.cpp` — [why it changes]
- New files needed: [list]

## Implementation Order
[Ordered steps. Each step should be independently committable.]

1. [Step 1 — what it produces]
2. [Step 2 — builds on step 1]
3. [Step 3 — etc.]

## Acceptance Criteria
[Testable conditions that define "done". Each one should be
verifiable by running a test or observing a specific behaviour.]

- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] Tests pass: [specific test file or command]

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
[What can go wrong and how each case is handled.]

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| [case] | [what happens] |

## Open Questions
[Anything still unresolved that will need a decision during implementation.
If there are none, write "None — plan is complete."]

## Suggested GitHub Issues
[If this plan should become overnight issues, list them here as a
starting point for /plan-github:]

1. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
2. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
3. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
```

---

## AFTER SAVING THE PLAN

Tell the user:
1. Where the plan was saved
2. How to turn it into GitHub issues:
   `/plan-github "[feature name]"` — or offer to run it now
3. How to start implementation immediately:
   `/develop [feature name]` — uses the plan as the spec
4. How to queue it for overnight:
   Add the suggested issues to GitHub, label ready-for-ai,
   then `bash ~/scripts/nightly.sh`

---

## TONE

Ask questions like a sharp senior engineer reviewing a spec —
direct, specific, not adversarial. The goal is to surface
assumptions before they become bugs, not to gatekeep.

If the idea is already clear enough to plan without questions,
say so briefly and go straight to the plan.

# Plan: Volatility-Targeted Position Sizing (first risk control)
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Scale exposure so risk, not notional, is what's constant. Half of this
already shipped: `sizing="conf_vol"` (PR #63) weights positions by
confidence ÷ trailing σ — that IS inverse-vol relative weighting, giving
each name a roughly equal volatility contribution. The missing half is the
portfolio level: total gross exposure should scale to a target portfolio
volatility (e.g. 15% annualized), shrinking the whole book when realized
vol runs hot and running fully invested when calm — the mechanism the
research credits with cutting crash risk.

## Goal
A strategy's ledger targets a chosen annualized volatility; turbulent
periods automatically de-lever toward cash without any signal changes.

## Design Decisions
- **Realized vol source: the strategy's own equity curve** — trailing
  N-day (default 20) std of the ledger's daily returns, annualized. This is
  deterministic from data already computed in the loop, needs no covariance
  matrix, and measures exactly the thing being targeted. During backtest
  the loop uses its own accumulating daily `realized` series; live inherits
  identically (same code path — the arena invariant).
- **Scalar, never leverage**: `exposure_mult = min(1.0, target_vol /
  realized_vol)`, applied to the day's weights after conf_vol/equal
  weighting and the max_pos cap. Long-only, no borrowing — the multiplier
  only ever de-levers.
- **New sizing mode `vol_target`** stacking ON conf_vol (relative weights
  from conf/σ, gross from the target) — persisted per strategy like
  existing modes; `equal` and `conf_vol` untouched and regression-pinned.
- Warmup: fewer than N days of realized returns → multiplier 1.0
  (fully invested until evidence exists).
- Flags: `--target_vol 0.15`, `--vol_target_window 20` on backtest
  (screened configuration, like sizing itself).

## Out of Scope
- Leverage above 1.0; covariance-based portfolio vol; per-ticker vol
  targets beyond what conf_vol already does; applying to intraday engine.

## Affected Areas
- `walkforward_sim.py` — `run_strategy_walkforward`: sizing mode
  `vol_target`; rolling realized-vol tracker on the loop's own daily
  returns; multiplier applied to weights (cost model then sees the scaled
  |Δweight| turnover automatically — no cost changes needed).
- `strategy_arena.py` — mode choice + params persisted (sizing column
  already exists; add `target_vol` column, guarded ALTER); CLI flags.
- `tests/test_strategy_walkforward.py` — calm vs turbulent synthetic
  series: turbulent period's gross exposure strictly lower; calm ≈ fully
  invested; warmup fully invested; equal/conf_vol regression pins hold.

## Implementation Order
1. Rolling realized-vol tracker + multiplier in the loop, mode plumbed,
   tests (pure loop behavior).
2. Arena persistence (column, flags) + live reuse + migration test.
3. Report: `target_vol` visible for vol_target strategies.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Synthetic high-vol regime cuts gross exposure by ≈ target/realized
      (verified numerically); calm regime runs at 1.0
- [ ] Multiplier never exceeds 1.0 and never goes negative
- [ ] `sizing="equal"`/`"conf_vol"` outputs byte-identical to today
- [ ] Mode + target persisted at screen, reused by live; legacy DBs migrate
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Realized vol ≈ 0 (flat ledger) | Multiplier capped at 1.0 — the min() handles it |
| < window days of history | Multiplier 1.0 (documented warmup) |
| Strategy holds nothing for a stretch | Realized vol decays toward 0; re-entry starts fully invested — acceptable, noted |
| Interaction with Kelly plan (fractional-kelly.md) | Multipliers compose multiplicatively; combined gross still capped at 1.0 — stated in both plans |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(sizing): portfolio vol-targeting multiplier in run_strategy_walkforward` — mode, tracker, tests
2. `feat(arena): persist target_vol as screened config + report column` — migration + flags

# Plan: ATR Trailing Stops + Portfolio-Level Drawdown Breaker
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: L

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Two risk controls. (1) Per-position trailing stops sized to each stock's
own volatility: an ATR(14)-based trail (default 3×ATR) instead of a flat
percentage, applied as an ENGINE overlay in the daily walk-forward so any
strategy gets it without changing its signal code. (2) A portfolio-level
max-drawdown circuit breaker: when the COMBINED equity across all live
ledgers falls past a configurable threshold from its peak, every live
strategy is paused at once — the existing per-strategy breaker's big
sibling, same manual-resume philosophy.

## Design Decisions
- **Stops are an engine overlay, not strategy logic.** The daily loop's
  one-bar-hold semantics make "position continuity" implicit (same ticker
  re-picked = held; #55 costs already treat it that way). The overlay
  tracks continuous same-direction holdings per ticker: entry bar, running
  peak (long) / trough (short), trail = peak − k×ATR(14). When a bar's Close
  crosses the trail, the ticker is SUPPRESSED from candidates for
  `cooldown_days` (default 5) — a deterministic function of history, so
  live backfill replays identically (the arena invariant).
- **ATR from the data already fetched** (High/Low/Close true range, Wilder
  smoothing, min_periods guard). Flat-percentage fallback intentionally NOT
  provided — vol-sized or nothing, per the idea.
- **Opt-in**: `--atr_stop 3.0` (multiplier; absent = no stops, current
  behavior regression-pinned). Persisted as screened configuration.
- **Portfolio breaker**: `portfolio_equity(date) = Σ` live ledgers' equity
  (PASS + PROBATION); running peak since the last portfolio resume;
  breach of `--portfolio_dd` (default 0.25) → every live strategy set
  PAUSED + a `portfolio_events` row; `arena-run resume --all` restores all
  portfolio-paused strategies (each anchored like individual resumes).
  Individual trips/resumes unaffected. Evaluated once per `arena-run live`
  after all ticks.
- Multi-strategy overlap note: combined equity double-counts nothing —
  ledgers are independent paper accounts; the portfolio breaker treats
  their sum as "the book."

## Out of Scope
- Intraday PaperEngine (has its own SL/TP already); take-profit trails;
  per-strategy ATR multipliers (one global flag per run this version);
  auto-resume of anything.

## Affected Areas
- `walkforward_sim.py` — ATR series computation; holding-continuity +
  trail tracker in `run_strategy_walkforward`; candidate suppression +
  cooldown; blotter rows gain `stopped` marker on forced exits.
- `strategy_arena.py` — `--atr_stop`/`--cooldown_days` persisted;
  `portfolio_events` table; portfolio drawdown evaluation in `cmd_live`;
  `resume --all`.
- `analyze_equity.py` — report: `stopped_trades` count column;
  portfolio-paused strategies show `paused_since` as today.
- New tests: `tests/test_atr_stops.py` (trail math pinned; long stopped on
  trail breach; cooldown suppresses re-entry; determinism across replay),
  portfolio-breaker cases in `tests/test_circuit_breaker.py`.

## Implementation Order
1. ATR + trail tracker + suppression in the loop, opt-in flag, tests.
2. Arena persistence of stop config + blotter marker + report count.
3. Portfolio breaker: combined-equity computation, trip-all, events table,
   `resume --all`, tests (individual breaker interplay pinned).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Synthetic runaway-then-crash series: long position exits within one
      bar of the 3×ATR trail breach; without the flag it holds (pinned)
- [ ] Stopped ticker absent from candidates for exactly cooldown_days
- [ ] Same data replayed (live backfill) reproduces identical stops
- [ ] Combined ledgers breaching --portfolio_dd pauses ALL live strategies,
      one portfolio_events row; `resume --all` restores them with fresh
      anchors; individually-tripped strategies need their own resume
- [ ] No-flag runs byte-identical to current behavior
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Direction flip (long→short) on consecutive picks | Continuity resets; new trail from the new entry |
| ATR undefined (short history) | No stop until ATR warms up (min_periods), documented |
| Gap through the trail (Close far past it) | Exit at that bar's realized return — no intrabar fill fantasy; noted honestly |
| Portfolio breaker + individual breaker same tick | Individual evaluated first; portfolio sweep skips already-PAUSED — one event each, no double rows |
| Only one live strategy | Portfolio breaker degenerates to a second threshold on that ledger — fine |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(risk): ATR trailing-stop overlay in the daily walk-forward` — trail tracker, suppression, cooldown, tests
2. `feat(arena): portfolio-level drawdown breaker + resume --all` — combined equity, portfolio_events, tests

# Plan: Per-Ticker Time-Series Trend Following (TSMOM)
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Each stock is judged only against its own history: compute the trailing
return over a 3–12 month lookback and go long only when that trend is
positive — no cross-sectional ranking. Volatility scaling is built in from
day one (the Moskowitz–Ooi–Pedersen result the user cites: vol scaling
roughly doubles Sharpe and cuts crash risk) by emitting confidence =
trend strength ÷ trailing σ, which the existing `conf_vol` sizing then
turns into inverse-vol position weights automatically — the scaling lives
in the signal, not bolted on later.

## Design Decisions
- **Fits the existing loop as-is.** The one-bar-hold walk-forward with
  daily re-picks IS continuous holding: a positive-trend ticker is
  re-picked daily, and since #55 turnover-based costs, holding an unchanged
  weight is free. No multi-day-hold engine work needed.
- **Signal**: lookback L days (default 252, configurable 63–252), optional
  skip of the most recent month (`skip_days=21` default ON — the standard
  short-term-reversal exclusion): `trend = close[-skip] / close[-L] − 1`.
  Long (+1) if trend > 0 else HOLD. Long-only per the idea (no shorting
  negative trends this version).
- **Confidence = trend / (σ_daily × √252)** — trend strength in vol units,
  so conf_vol weighting yields the vol-scaled sizing the research wants,
  and cross-ticker ranking for top_n favors the cleanest trends.
- **compatible_regimes = all four.** TSMOM self-gates by trend sign;
  stacking the regime gate on top would double-filter the same signal.
- Registry name `tsmom`; constructor params lookback/skip_days.

## Out of Scope
- Shorting negative trends; multi-horizon blends (3+6+12 ensemble);
  futures/crypto universes; the separate low-vol strategy (own plan).

## Affected Areas
- New: `strategies/trend.py` — `TrendFollowingStrategy(DailyStrategy)`.
- `strategies/registry.py` — register `tsmom`.
- New tests in `tests/test_research_strategies.py` — monotonic uptrend →
  +1 with positive confidence; downtrend → HOLD (long-only); skip window
  actually excluded (recent-month crash doesn't flip an old uptrend);
  warmup respected; higher-vol ticker gets lower confidence at equal trend.

## Implementation Order
1. Strategy + unit tests (synthetic series, no network).
2. Registry entry + one arena smoke (screens + live-ticks through existing
   machinery unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 12-month uptrend, calm: +1 with confidence ≈ trend/vol (hand-checked)
- [ ] Trend positive only inside the skipped window → HOLD (skip works)
- [ ] Negative trend → HOLD, never −1
- [ ] Equal trends, 2× vol → half the confidence
- [ ] Selectable via `arena-run backtest --strategies tsmom`
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| History < lookback + skip | HOLD via warmup_bars = lookback + skip + 1 |
| σ ≈ 0 (flat series) | Confidence floored via the same _VOL_FLOOR discipline as sizing |
| trend exactly 0 | HOLD (strict >) |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(strategies): TSMOM trend-following with built-in vol scaling` — strategy + registry + tests

# Plan: Low-Volatility Selection (long-only betting-against-beta proxy)
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Rank the tradeable universe by trailing realized volatility and prefer
long positions in the calmest names — the long-only half of the
betting-against-beta premium, no shorting or margin required. In this
codebase that's a small strategy: emit +1 for every ticker with
confidence = 1/σ, and the arena's existing top_n ranking plus conf_vol
sizing do the "prefer the lowest-vol names" work structurally.

## Design Decisions
- **Ranking IS the confidence.** `generate_signal` returns
  `DailySignal(+1, confidence=1/σ_252d, "low-vol")` for any ticker with
  enough history; the loop's confidence sort makes top_n = the N
  lowest-vol names. No cross-sectional machinery needed inside the
  strategy — the per-ticker contract holds.
- **Realized vol, not beta** (my recommended option): beta needs a market
  proxy regression per ticker; trailing 252-day realized σ captures the
  same premium in the long-only setting with far less machinery, matching
  the idea's own parenthetical. Beta variant listed as a future issue.
- **A minimum-vol floor guards the degenerate case**: a near-zero-σ ticker
  (halted, stale data) would otherwise hog the top slot with confidence
  → ∞; σ floored at 1e-4 daily (same constant as sizing).
- **compatible_regimes = all four** — it's a defensive allocation, and
  high_vol days are arguably its whole point.
- Registry name `lowvol`; param `vol_lookback` (default 252).

## Out of Scope
- Shorting the high-vol leg (needs margin — see pairs plan's gating);
  explicit beta computation; sector neutralization; blending with TSMOM.

## Affected Areas
- New: `strategies/low_vol.py` — `LowVolatilityStrategy(DailyStrategy)`.
- `strategies/registry.py` — register `lowvol`.
- Tests in `tests/test_research_strategies.py` — calm ticker outranks wild
  one for the top_n slot (integration through run_strategy_walkforward);
  vol floor holds; warmup respected.

## Implementation Order
1. Strategy + tests. 2. Registry + arena smoke.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two-ticker universe, top_n=1: the lower-vol ticker is always the pick
- [ ] Confidence ordering equals ascending-σ ordering (property test)
- [ ] σ floor prevents a flat ticker from taking infinite confidence
- [ ] Selectable via `arena-run backtest --strategies lowvol`
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| History < vol_lookback | HOLD via warmup (lookback + 1) |
| All tickers equally calm | Equal confidences — top_n picks arbitrary-but-stable order; fine |
| Extreme calm from missing data (stale prices) | σ floor keeps confidence bounded; liquidity/cost model penalizes it downstream anyway |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(strategies): low-volatility long-only selection` — strategy + registry + tests
2. `feat(strategies): beta-ranked variant of lowvol (future)` — placeholder, not this version

# Plan: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (PEAD) Strategy
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: L

## The Idea (one paragraph)
After earnings, prices keep drifting in the direction of the surprise for
weeks — the PEAD anomaly. This strategy ranks names by standardized
earnings surprise and goes long the big positive surprises for a fixed
holding window (default 75 days, the 60–90 day literature range), filtered
to liquid tickers because the research is explicit that PEAD's paper edge
concentrates in small illiquid names where transaction costs eat it — the
exact trap our cost model now measures.

## Design Decisions
- **Data: Alpha Vantage EARNINGS endpoint, free tier, cached** (user
  decision): new `earnings_data.py` fetches per-ticker quarterly history
  (reportedDate, reportedEPS, estimatedEPS), caches JSON per ticker under
  `data/earnings/`, and a `refresh-earnings` CLI drip-fetches respecting a
  `--budget` of calls per run (default 20, under the ~25/day free cap).
  Earnings history is append-only in practice, so a quarterly refresh
  suffices. Universe capped at ~100 liquid names (`--tickers_file` of the
  top-ADV S&P names — universe_builder can emit it).
- **Surprise metric**: `(reportedEPS − estimatedEPS) / max(|estimatedEPS|,
  0.10)` — the denominator floor (10¢) tames the near-zero-estimate
  explosion that plagues raw surprise percentages. Threshold entry
  (surprise ≥ `min_surprise`, default +25%) rather than cross-sectional
  decile ranking — keeps the per-ticker DailyStrategy contract intact.
- **Holding window inside the signal**: emit +1 with confidence ∝ surprise
  for `hold_days` (default 75) after the report date, then HOLD. The
  one-bar-hold loop re-picks daily → continuous holding, free under
  turnover costs. Deterministic given (df, cached earnings) — backfill-safe.
- **Ticker identity**: `generate_signal(df)` has no ticker parameter; the
  engine will set `df.attrs["ticker"]` before each call (one-line,
  backward-compatible change to `run_strategy_walkforward` — my tests
  already used this pattern). PEAD's constructor takes the earnings cache
  dir and looks up by that attr; missing attr/tickers → HOLD.
- **Liquidity filter in-strategy**: reuse `costs.adv_dollars`; ADV below
  `--min_adv` (default $50M) → HOLD regardless of surprise. Belt to the
  cost model's suspenders, per the idea's explicit instruction.
- **Lookahead guard**: signals start the trading day AFTER reportedDate
  (reports land pre-market/post-close; next-day entry is the conservative
  choice and avoids assuming intraday timing we don't have).
- compatible_regimes = all four (event-driven, not regime-driven).

## Out of Scope
- Short leg on negative surprises; SUE (analyst-dispersion-standardized)
  surprise; paid data feeds; intraday entries; ranking across tickers.
