# MR: feat: research-founded batch — 8 strategies & risk controls (#64–#71)

Branch: `feature/research-batch` → `feature/gui-scroll-live-signals` (stacked: #52 → #53 → #63 → gui branch → this)

## Summary
Implements all 8 issues of milestone "Research Ideas — 2026-07-14": volatility-targeted sizing, ATR trailing stops + a portfolio-level drawdown breaker, TSMOM trend following, low-volatility selection, PEAD with a rate-limit-respecting earnings cache, fractional-Kelly gross scaling, demotion of candlestick/technical indicators to GBM features + confirmation filters, and margin-gated pairs stat-arb. One commit per issue, suite green after each — final: **235 passed, zero skips** (34 net new tests; every scaffold stub from the planning session is now live code).

## Changes by Issue

**#64 vol targeting** — `sizing="vol_target"`: conf_vol relative weights × `min(1, target_vol / realized ledger vol)`. De-levers in turbulence, never borrows; measured on the strategy's own accumulating equity curve so backtest and live replay share one code path. `target_vol` persisted as screened config.

**#65 ATR stops + portfolio breaker** — Engine overlay (`--atr_stop 3.0` opt-in): Wilder ATR(14) trail on continuously-held positions, breach ⇒ suppression from candidates for `--cooldown_days`, deterministic across backfill (test-pinned). Portfolio breaker: PASS ledgers date-aligned/ffilled/summed; combined drawdown past `--portfolio_dd` (0.25) pauses ALL live strategies with one `portfolio_events` row; `arena-run resume --all` restores exactly those. Design note: `--portfolio_dd 0` disables it independently of `--no_breaker` — the two protections arm separately.

**#66 TSMOM** — long iff trailing (252d − 21d skip) return > 0; confidence = trend / annualized σ so conf_vol sizing yields the vol-scaled positions from day one. Long-only; all regimes (it self-gates by trend sign).

**#67 low-vol** — always-long, confidence = 1/σ (floored): the arena's top-N confidence ranking does the cross-sectional selection structurally; the per-ticker contract stays clean.

**#68 PEAD** — `refresh-earnings` drip-fetches AV EARNINGS under `--budget 20/day` into `data/earnings/*.json` (fresh-skip at 80 days, rate-limit bodies stop cleanly with partial cache). Surprise = (act−est)/max(|est|, $0.10). Strategy: +1 for `hold_days` starting the day AFTER the report (lookahead guard), threshold +25%, mandatory ADV ≥ $50M filter — the small-cap cost trap is the point. Engine change: `run_strategy_walkforward` tags each history slice with `df.attrs["ticker"]` so aux-data strategies know who they are (regression-safe for everyone else).

**#69 fractional Kelly** — `kelly.py`: continuous f* = μ/σ² on per-trade returns, λ hard-limited [0.25, 0.5], clamp [0, 1], negative edge sizes to 0, <30 trades bootstraps to 1.0. Deviation from plan: estimated from the run's OWN in-window trade history in both backtest and live (not the stored trades table) — one code path, determinism preserved.

**#70 indicators → features** — new sticky `REFERENCE` status + `arena-run demote` (metrics preserved, never live, never ensemble); `ConfirmedStrategy(base, confirmer, mode=direction|veto)` wrapper; `build_features` gains `engulf_signal` (vectorized, parity-pinned against the real detector on every bar pair) and `macd_hist_norm` (TechnicalStrategy's confidence formula, formula-pinned). Old bundles keep working via the feature-list contract. **Reviewer note: retrain + ONNX re-export + C++ rebuild required before the GBM uses the new features live.**

**#71 pairs** — Engle–Granger with numpy OLS + hand-rolled DF test vs hardcoded MacKinnon criticals (zero new deps); `z_positions` pure state machine (entry ±2σ, exit 0.5σ, HARD stop 4σ ⇒ pair dead + `broken` flag); `backtest_pair` charges both legs through the CostModel; `pairs-scan`/`pairs-backtest` CLIs; results register as `RESEARCH` — `arena-run live` refuses them naming the margin/shorting requirements. Deviation: no `--i_have_margin` override since live pairs execution itself is out of scope; an unlock into a nonexistent engine would be theater.

## Why
This batch converts the research review's verdicts into code: the strongest-evidence risk control (vol targeting) landed first per the user's stated priority; weak-evidence standalone indicators were demoted, not deleted; and every "edge" strategy passes through the liquidity/cost machinery that the literature says eats paper profits. Sizing multipliers (vol-target × Kelly) compose multiplicatively and stay ≤ 1 — long-only, never levered, everywhere.

## Testing
`uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"` → **235 passed, 0 skipped**. Determinism (live-backfill replay), parity (feature vs detector), and hand-computed pins (Kelly f*, EG hedge ratio, surprise floors, DF separation of cointegrated vs independent walks) throughout. No network in tests.

## Risk and Rollback
Additive: new sizing modes/flags default off or to prior behavior (equal/conf_vol byte-identical, no ATR without the flag, Kelly off, portfolio breaker only in live). `build_features` gains columns — old bundles unaffected by the feature-list contract, but retraining will now see the new features (intended). Arena DBs migrate in place (2 new columns + 1 table). Revert = drop the merge.

## Checklist
- [x] 235 tests pass; suite green after every one of the 8 commits
- [x] Zero new dependencies (numpy OLS + hardcoded DF criticals for pairs)
- [x] Three documented deviations from plans (portfolio-breaker flag independence, in-window Kelly, no margin override)
- [ ] Reviewer: the ATR breach-day semantics (breach bar's return realized, exit via next-day suppression) and the PEAD calendar-day hold window are the judgment calls worth eyes

HFT Practice · Lesson 0039

The Position-Sizing Pipeline: Relative Weights × Gross Multipliers

Why this matters: after the 2026-07-14 research batch, a single day's position sizes in run_strategy_walkforward flow through up to FOUR stages. Understanding why they compose the way they do — and why every stage is capped at 1 — is the difference between extending this pipeline safely and accidentally building leverage into a long-only paper trader.

1 · The pipeline, in order

StageQuestion it answersRangeCode
1. Relative weightsHow do today's picks split whatever we deploy? (confidence ÷ σ, capped per-name at max_pos, cash remainder)Σ ≤ 1_conf_vol_weights
2. Vol-target multiplierIs the LEDGER's recent volatility above target? Scale the whole book down.(0, 1]min(1, target_vol/realized_vol)
3. Kelly multiplierDoes this strategy's own trade HISTORY justify full deployment?[0, 1]kelly_fraction — λ·μ/σ², clamped
4. ATR stop overlayDid any held name breach its volatility-sized trail? (Removes candidates, not weights)—suppression + cooldown

Stages 2 and 3 multiply: final = relative × vol_mult × kelly_mult. Since each factor is ≤ 1, the product is ≤ 1 — the book can only ever de-lever. That's a STRUCTURAL guarantee, not a hope: no configuration of flags can borrow.

2 · Why multiply, not average or min?

The multipliers answer independent questions: realized-vol says "the market is currently wilder than my target"; Kelly says "my measured edge is thinner than full deployment assumes." If both are true, both discounts should apply — a 0.5 vol scale on a 0.5 Kelly conviction means 25% deployed, and that's correct, not double-counting. min() would ignore one true fact; averaging would invent a number neither control asked for. Multiplication is the only composition that respects both.

3 · Determinism: the constraint that shaped everything

Every stage feeds on data the replay can reconstruct: relative weights from price history, the vol multiplier from the ledger's own accumulating returns, Kelly from the run's own accumulating blotter (deliberately NOT the stored trades table — one code path for backtest and live backfill), ATR trails from OHLC. The arena invariant — live is a deterministic recompute — survives because no sizing stage reads anything a replay can't rebuild. This is also why Kelly sizes today's bet only from trades BEFORE today: letting today's outcome size today's bet is lookahead wearing a risk-management costume.

4 · Often confused

PairDistinction
Inverse-vol weights (stage 1) vs vol targeting (stage 2)Stage 1 equalizes risk ACROSS names (calm names get more of the pie); stage 2 sizes the pie itself against a target. You can be perfectly risk-balanced across names and still have twice the portfolio vol you want.
Kelly multiplier vs the divergence alertBoth read realized performance; Kelly quietly scales exposure with the measured edge, divergence loudly flags statistical inconsistency with the backtest. One acts on size, the other on your attention.
ATR stop vs the drawdown breakerATR: per-POSITION, price-path-based, auto-recovers after cooldown. Breaker: per-LEDGER (or portfolio), equity-based, human-resume only.
Full Kelly vs fractional Kellyf* = μ/σ² is optimal only if μ and σ are KNOWN. They're estimated — and overbetting a noisy edge estimate is ruinous asymmetrically. λ ∈ [0.25, 0.5] is deliberately the only offered range.

5 · Practice

Score: 0 / 0

Q1. vol_mult = 0.6 and kelly_mult = 0.5 on the same day. Deployed fraction of the book?

  • 0.5 — the stricter control wins
  • 0.30
  • 0.55
  • 1.0 — they offset

Q2. Why does the Kelly estimator use only trades from BEFORE today?

  • Including today would be too slow
  • Today's outcome sizing today's bet is lookahead
  • The window would overflow
  • Live can't see today's trades

Q3. A strategy's Kelly multiplier reads 0.0 in the report. What happened, and what does the arena do?

  • Its measured edge went negative; it still ticks but deploys nothing
  • The breaker paused it
  • It has too few trades
  • The lambda flag was set to zero

Q4. The ATR stop breaches on Tuesday's close. When does the position actually stop earning returns?

  • Tuesday — the breach bar's return is cancelled
  • Wednesday — via suppression from the next bar's candidates
  • After cooldown_days
  • When the ledger's breaker also trips

## Overnight session #2 complete — 8 for 8 ✅

All of milestone #4 (**#64–#71**) is implemented, tested, and up as draft **PR #72**: https://github.com/bjl14710/algo_trading_practice/pull/72. One commit per issue, suite green after every single one, final state **235 passed with zero skips** — every stub from yesterday's planning session is now live code. Full details in `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md`.

**What the arena can do this morning that it couldn't last night:**
- **Size by risk, not notional** — `--sizing vol_target` de-levers the whole book when realized vol runs above target; `--kelly 0.25` scales gross exposure to the measured edge. Multipliers compose multiplicatively and each stays ≤ 1, so the long-only book structurally cannot lever.
- **Stop losses that fit each stock** — `--atr_stop 3.0` trails at 3×ATR with cooldown suppression, plus a **portfolio-level breaker** (`--portfolio_dd`) that pauses everything at once, restored only by `arena-run resume --all`.
- **Three new strategies** — `tsmom` (trend, vol-scaled from day one), `lowvol` (calm-name selection via structural confidence ranking), and `pead` (earnings drift with a budgeted Alpha Vantage cache and a hard liquidity filter).
- **The demotion you asked for** — candlestick/technical are now `REFERENCE` (visible, never live, never ensembled; `arena-run demote`), their information feeding the GBM as `engulf_signal` + `macd_hist_norm` features and available as `ConfirmedStrategy` entry filters.
- **Pairs trading as research** — Engle–Granger scan + spread backtest with zero new dependencies, registered as `RESEARCH` and refused by live with the margin requirements spelled out.

**Three things need you** (also in the report): retrain + ONNX re-export before the GBM trades live on the new features; seed the PEAD cache (`refresh-earnings`, ~5 daily runs on the free tier); and the PR stack is now 5 deep (#52 → #53 → #63 → gui branch → #72) — bottom-up review would flatten it before it gets taller.

Lesson `0039` + drill `0008` cover the sizing pipeline — the one concept tying tonight's whole batch together. Three documented deviations from the plans are flagged in the PR body for your judgment, the most interesting being in-window Kelly estimation (chosen over the trades table to preserve the deterministic-replay invariant).

content.text:
You are turning "Please" into a structured, actionable plan document.

This command has two phases:
- PHASE 1: Interrogate the idea until it is unambiguous
- PHASE 2: Produce the plan document

Do not skip to Phase 2 until Phase 1 is complete.

---

## PHASE 1 — INTERROGATE THE IDEA

Read the codebase first so your questions are grounded in reality:
```bash
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -30
git log --oneline -10
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null || true
```

Then ask clarifying questions — ONE at a time, wait for the answer,
then ask the next. Do not dump a list of questions all at once.
A question only gets asked if you genuinely cannot write a good plan
without knowing the answer.

Things worth asking about (pick the most important ones):

**Scope:**
- What does done look like? What can a user DO when this is complete?
- What is explicitly OUT of scope for this version?
- Is this a new feature, a change to existing behaviour, or a fix?

**Users and context:**
- Who uses this and in what situation?
- What do they have / know before they reach this feature?

**Technical constraints:**
- Does this touch existing code that other things depend on?
- Any performance, security, or compatibility requirements?
- Any third-party APIs or libraries involved?

**Edge cases:**
- What happens when the input is invalid or missing?
- What's the failure mode and how should it be handled?

**Priority:**
- Does this need to be done in a specific order relative to other work?
- Is there a simpler version that delivers most of the value?

Stop asking when you have enough to write a plan that could be handed
to a developer (or the overnight session) without them needing to ask
you anything.

---

## PHASE 2 — PRODUCE THE PLAN DOCUMENT

Save to `.claude/plans/[slug].md` where slug is a short dash-case
name derived from the idea. Example: "add weapon inventory" →
`.claude/plans/weapon-inventory.md`

The document structure:

```markdown
# Plan: [Feature Name]
Date: [date]
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S / M / L / XL

## The Idea (one paragraph)
[What this is, in plain language. Someone unfamiliar with the codebase
should understand this in 30 seconds.]

## Goal
[One sentence: what a user can DO when this is shipped that they
cannot do now.]

## Out of Scope (this version)
[Explicit list of things NOT included. This prevents scope creep
during implementation.]

## Affected Areas
[Files, modules, or systems this touches. Be specific.]
- `src/path/to/file.py` — [why it changes]
- `src/path/to/other.cpp` — [why it changes]
- New files needed: [list]

## Implementation Order
[Ordered steps. Each step should be independently committable.]

1. [Step 1 — what it produces]
2. [Step 2 — builds on step 1]
3. [Step 3 — etc.]

## Acceptance Criteria
[Testable conditions that define "done". Each one should be
verifiable by running a test or observing a specific behaviour.]

- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] [Given X, when Y, then Z]
- [ ] Tests pass: [specific test file or command]

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
[What can go wrong and how each case is handled.]

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| [case] | [what happens] |

## Open Questions
[Anything still unresolved that will need a decision during implementation.
If there are none, write "None — plan is complete."]

## Suggested GitHub Issues
[If this plan should become overnight issues, list them here as a
starting point for /plan-github:]

1. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
2. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
3. [Issue title] — [one line scope]
```

---

## AFTER SAVING THE PLAN

Tell the user:
1. Where the plan was saved
2. How to turn it into GitHub issues:
   `/plan-github "[feature name]"` — or offer to run it now
3. How to start implementation immediately:
   `/develop [feature name]` — uses the plan as the spec
4. How to queue it for overnight:
   Add the suggested issues to GitHub, label ready-for-ai,
   then `bash ~/scripts/nightly.sh`

---

## TONE

Ask questions like a sharp senior engineer reviewing a spec —
direct, specific, not adversarial. The goal is to surface
assumptions before they become bugs, not to gatekeep.

If the idea is already clear enough to plan without questions,
say so briefly and go straight to the plan.

# Plan: "Lab" Web Theme — Streamlit Design Language for webapp/, Side by Side
Date: 2026-07-15
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Borrow the visual language of the HFT learning app's dashboard
(`HFT_Trading_Practice_Repo/app/dashboard.py`) and offer it as a SECOND
selectable theme for this repo's FastAPI+Jinja2 webapp — the existing look
stays intact and remains the default ("have both"). Grounding fact that
shapes everything: that dashboard uses STOCK Streamlit (no custom CSS, no
config.toml), so the design language to reproduce is Streamlit's default
aesthetic plus the app's layout patterns — sidebar-of-controls, metric
cards in columns with green/red deltas, clean tabs, wide data tables,
crimson dashed reference lines on charts.

## Goal
A `Theme: Lab ⇄ Classic` toggle in the webapp header restyles every page
into the Streamlit-like look (and back), persisted per browser — plus a new
`/arena` page that showcases it by rendering the arena comparison table
with metric cards.

## Design Decisions (recommended options, per standing preference)
- **One DOM, two stylesheets — not duplicated templates.** `base.html`
  resolves the theme per request in Jinja (no route changes needed):
  `?theme=lab|classic` query overrides, else `ui_theme` cookie, else
  `classic`. A tiny inline script persists a `?theme=` visit into the
  cookie. `<body class="theme-lab|theme-classic">` + conditional second
  stylesheet. The Tkinter GUI and the current web look are untouched;
  classic stays default.
- **Design tokens = Streamlit defaults**, hardcoded as CSS custom
  properties in `webapp/static/theme-lab.css`:
  light: bg `#FFFFFF`, secondary/sidebar `#F0F2F6`, text `#31333F`,
  accent `#FF4B4B`; dark (via `prefers-color-scheme`): bg `#0E1117`,
  secondary `#262730`, text `#FAFAFA`, same accent. Radius 8px,
  system-font stack approximating Source Sans (NO CDN fonts — the PWA
  must stay offline-capable and the repo convention is no external
  fetches). Metric deltas: green `#09AB3B` / red `#FF2B2B`.
- **Layout pattern, lab mode only**: the header nav restyles into a left
  sidebar on wide screens (CSS grid on the same markup; collapses back to
  the existing hamburger pattern under 900px — the mobile PWA behavior
  from PR #49 is preserved verbatim in both themes).
- **Metric cards as a shared Jinja partial** (`_metric.html` macro:
  label, value, optional delta with sign-based class). Both themes render
  it — classic styles it as a plain stat line, lab as a Streamlit metric
  card. Pages adopt it where numbers already appear (analyze results,
  walkforward summary, home status) — light touch-ups, no logic changes.
- **New `/arena` page** (the showcase, explicitly named in the idea):
  reads the arena DB (`ARENA_DB` env or `arena_state/arena.db`) via
  `analyze_equity.compare_strategies`, renders status-tiered rows
  (PASS/PROBATION-ready/PAUSED/EXCLUDED/REFERENCE/RESEARCH badges),
  metric cards for the headline numbers, and a friendly empty state when
  no DB exists. Read-only — no arena mutations from the web.
- **First webapp tests ride along** (`tests/test_webapp_theme.py`,
  FastAPI TestClient): theme resolution (query > cookie > default),
  stylesheet/body-class switching, `/arena` with a seeded tmp DB and with
  no DB. The webapp currently has zero tests; this starts the habit
  without boiling the ocean.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Copying any trading/research logic or pages from the oil app (explicit
  in the idea) — design language only
- Plotly/chart re-theming beyond CSS (the webapp doesn't render charts
  today; when it does, the crimson-dashed-reference-line convention is
  noted here as the pattern to follow)
- Theming the SaaS static site (`web/`) or the learning materials
- A user-accounts/preferences system — one cookie is the persistence
- Making lab the default (revisit after living with it)

## Affected Areas
- New: `webapp/static/theme-lab.css` — the entire lab look (tokens above,
  sidebar grid, metric cards, tables, tabs-like section headers, buttons,
  alerts) with light/dark via `prefers-color-scheme`.
- `webapp/templates/base.html` — theme resolution block, conditional
  stylesheet, body class, header toggle link, cookie-persist snippet.
- New: `webapp/templates/_metric.html` — metric-card macro.
- New: `webapp/templates/arena.html` + route in `webapp/main.py`
  (`GET /arena`), nav link in base.
- `webapp/templates/{index,analyze,walkforward}.html` — adopt the metric
  macro where numbers render (markup only).
- `webapp/static/style.css` — additive rules so the macro renders sanely
  in classic (no visual change to anything existing).
- New: `tests/test_webapp_theme.py`.

## Implementation Order
1. Theme plumbing: base.html resolution + toggle + cookie persist +
   empty theme-lab.css stub; tests for resolution order. (No visual
   change yet — classic byte-identical.)
2. The lab stylesheet: tokens, sidebar layout ≥900px, cards, tables,
   forms, alerts, dark mode.
3. Metric macro + adoption on index/analyze/walkforward; classic-side
   additive styles.
4. `/arena` page + route + nav link + empty-state + tests with seeded
   tmp arena DB.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default (no cookie, no query) renders exactly today's markup +
      stylesheet — classic untouched, regression-pinned in a test
- [ ] `?theme=lab` renders lab (body class + second stylesheet) and
      persists via cookie for subsequent plain requests
- [ ] `?theme=classic` switches back and persists
- [ ] Lab mode ≥900px shows the sidebar layout; <900px keeps the existing
      hamburger behavior (both themes)
- [ ] All 8 existing pages render without template errors in BOTH themes
      (parametrized test hitting every GET route × both themes)
- [ ] `/arena` renders compare_strategies output with status badges and
      metric cards; with no DB present it renders the empty state, not a 500
- [ ] No external network requests introduced (no CDN fonts/scripts) —
      PWA offline behavior unchanged
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Invalid `?theme=banana` | Falls back to cookie-else-classic; cookie not overwritten with garbage |
| Arena DB exists but is empty (no strategies) | Empty state with a pointer to `arena-run backtest` |
| Arena DB from an older schema | compare_strategies' own migration-tolerance applies (ArenaState migrates on open); page renders whatever columns exist |
| Cookies disabled | Toggle still works per-request via query param; just doesn't persist |
| Both `?theme=` and cookie present | Query wins for that request AND rewrites the cookie (explicit choice beats memory) |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(webapp): theme plumbing — resolution, toggle, cookie persistence` — base.html + tests, zero visual change
2. `feat(webapp): lab theme stylesheet — Streamlit design tokens, sidebar, dark mode` — theme-lab.css
3. `feat(webapp): metric-card macro + adoption on numeric pages` — _metric.html + touch-ups
4. `feat(webapp): /arena comparison page with status badges + empty state` — route, template, seeded-DB tests

"""Tests for the lab/classic web theme plumbing and the /arena page.

First webapp tests in the repo. Offline: FastAPI TestClient, no network,
arena data seeded into a tmp SQLite DB via ArenaState.
"""
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from webapp.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

GET_ROUTES = ["/", "/walkforward", "/train", "/universe", "/news",
              "/download", "/execute", "/analyze", "/arena"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Theme resolution: query > cookie > classic default
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_default_is_classic_and_lab_css_absent():
    resp = client.get("/")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert 'class="theme-classic"' in resp.text
    assert "theme-lab.css" not in resp.text


def test_query_param_selects_lab():
    resp = client.get("/?theme=lab")
    assert 'class="theme-lab"' in resp.text
    assert "theme-lab.css" in resp.text
    assert "ui_theme=lab" in resp.text  # the cookie-persist snippet rendered


def test_cookie_selects_lab_without_query():
    resp = client.get("/", cookies={"ui_theme": "lab"})
    assert 'class="theme-lab"' in resp.text
    assert "theme-lab.css" in resp.text


def test_query_overrides_cookie():
    resp = client.get("/?theme=classic", cookies={"ui_theme": "lab"})
    assert 'class="theme-classic"' in resp.text
    assert "theme-lab.css" not in resp.text


def test_invalid_theme_falls_back_and_never_persists_garbage():
    resp = client.get("/?theme=banana", cookies={"ui_theme": "lab"})
    assert 'class="theme-lab"' in resp.text     # cookie still wins
    assert "ui_theme=banana" not in resp.text   # no garbage cookie write
    resp2 = client.get("/?theme=banana")
    assert 'class="theme-classic"' in resp2.text  # no cookie -> classic


@pytest.mark.parametrize("route", GET_ROUTES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("theme", ["classic", "lab"])
def test_every_page_renders_in_both_themes(route, theme):
    resp = client.get(f"{route}?theme={theme}")
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"{route} failed in {theme}"
    assert f'class="theme-{theme}"' in resp.text


def test_toggle_link_points_at_the_other_theme():
    resp = client.get("/analyze?theme=lab")
    assert "?theme=classic" in resp.text
    resp = client.get("/analyze?theme=classic")
    assert "?theme=lab" in resp.text


def test_no_external_urls_in_rendered_pages():
    """PWA offline guarantee: no CDN fonts/scripts introduced."""
    for route in GET_ROUTES:
        text = client.get(f"{route}?theme=lab").text
        assert "https://fonts." not in text
        assert "cdn." not in text


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# /arena page
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_arena_empty_state_when_db_missing(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("ARENA_DB", str(tmp_path / "nope.db"))
    resp = client.get("/arena")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert "No arena data yet" in resp.text
    assert "arena-run backtest" in resp.text


def test_arena_renders_seeded_db_with_badges_and_metrics(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from strategy_arena import ArenaState

    db = str(tmp_path / "arena.db")
    state = ArenaState(db)
    state.record_backtest("tsmom", "PASS", {"Sharpe": 1.2, "CAGR": 0.2, "MaxDD": -0.08})
    state.record_backtest("engulfing", "REFERENCE", {"Sharpe": 0.1, "CAGR": 0.01, "MaxDD": -0.2})
    state.append_ledger("tsmom", [("2026-07-01", 100000.0), ("2026-07-02", 100500.0),
                                  ("2026-07-03", 101000.0)], [])
    monkeypatch.setenv("ARENA_DB", db)

    resp = client.get("/arena?theme=lab")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert "tsmom" in resp.text
    assert "status-pass" in resp.text
    assert "status-reference" in resp.text
    assert "metric-card" in resp.text  # headline cards rendered
    assert "Strategies tracked" in resp.text

You are scaffolding the initial file structure for a planned feature.
This command bridges the gap between a plan document and actual files
on disk — creating skeletons, directories, config updates, and skill
files so the overnight session or /develop has something real to build on.

---

## STEP 1 — READ THE PLAN

```bash
# Find the plan document
ls .claude/plans/
cat .claude/plans/.md 2>/dev/null || \
  cat .claude/plans/$(echo "" | tr ' ' '-' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]').md 2>/dev/null || \
  echo "No plan found for '' — run /idea first"
```

If no plan exists, stop and tell the user to run `/idea` first.
The plan is the spec. Do not scaffold without it.

---

## STEP 2 — READ THE CODEBASE

```bash
# Understand what already exists before creating anything
find src/ lib/ app/ tests/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -50
cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null | head -50 || true
git log --oneline -10
```

Use real class names, real import paths, and real conventions from
what you find — not generic placeholders.

---

## STEP 3 — DERIVE WHAT NEEDS TO BE CREATED

From the plan's "Affected Areas" and "Implementation Order" sections,
determine:

- New directories needed
- New source files (with correct imports and skeleton structure)
- New test files (matching the project's test conventions)
- Config file updates (pytest.ini, CMakeLists.txt, requirements.txt etc.)
- New skill files if the feature introduces patterns Claude needs
  to reference repeatedly (e.g. a new API, a new framework)
- Any one-time setup scripts (e.g. installing system packages)
- .gitignore additions for generated or temporary files

---

## STEP 4 — CREATE THE FILES

For each file derived in Step 3:

**Source files** — create with:
- Correct imports based on existing patterns in the project
- Class/function skeleton matching the plan's interface
- Docstrings explaining what each piece does and why
- TODO comments marking what the overnight session needs to fill in
- No placeholder names — use real names from the codebase

**Test files** — create with:
- Correct pytest conventions for this project
- One test function stub per acceptance criterion in the plan
- Each stub has a docstring explaining what it tests
- `pytest.mark.skip(reason="not implemented yet")` on each stub
  so the test suite runs clean before the feature is built

**Config updates** — update existing files rather than creating new ones
where possible. Add only what the plan requires.

**Skill files** — only if the feature introduces something Claude needs
to reference repeatedly. Write to `.claude/skills/<feature>/SKILL.md`.
Not every feature needs a skill — only ones with non-obvious APIs,
protocols, or patterns.

**Setup scripts** — only if the feature requires one-time environment
setup (installing system packages, external tools, etc.). Write to
`scripts/setup-<feature>.sh`. Make it idempotent — safe to run twice.

---

## STEP 5 — DO NOT CREATE

Things the scaffold should NOT create:

- Implementation code (that's for /develop or the overnight session)
- Golden/reference files (those are generated by running the tests)
- Database migrations (those need careful human review)
- Secrets or credentials
- Anything not mentioned in the plan

If the plan is unclear about something, leave a clear TODO comment
and note it in the summary rather than guessing.

---

## STEP 6 — UPDATE .gitignore

Add any paths that should never be committed:
```bash
# Examples based on feature type:
# Visual testing:   tests/visual/diffs/  tests/visual/actual/
# Build artifacts:  dist/  build/  *.pyc
# Generated files:  whatever the feature produces at runtime

grep -qF "<path>" .gitignore || echo "<path>" >> .gitignore
```

---

## STEP 7 — SUMMARY

After creating all files, print a clear summary:

```
Scaffold complete for: [feature name]
Plan: .claude/plans/[plan].md
```

# Plan: Native Streamlit Dashboard (third GUI)
Date: 2026-07-15
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Add a genuine Streamlit app — not the CSS homage (that's the webapp's "lab"
theme, shipped) — as a third GUI alongside the Tkinter desktop app and the
FastAPI webapp. It mirrors the layout patterns of the HFT learning app's
oil dashboard (`st.set_page_config(layout="wide")`, sidebar of controls,
`st.metric` cards in columns, tabs, wide dataframes) but reads THIS
platform's artifacts: the arena database, equity CSVs, and the live-watch
signal engine. Strictly read-only/research — no arena mutations, no orders.

## Goal
`uv run streamlit run streamlit_app/dashboard.py` opens a wide-layout
research console: arena standings with metric cards and status badges,
equity-curve analysis with charts, and a manual-refresh live-signals tape.

## Design Decisions (recommended options, standing preference)
- **Dependency as an opt-in extra, not a core dep**: `streamlit>=1.30`
  under `[project.optional-dependencies] dashboard`. The scaffold does NOT
  install it; `uv sync --extra dashboard` is the implementer's first step.
  Core `uv sync` stays exactly as heavy as today.
- **Logic/presentation split for testability**: all data access lives in
  `streamlit_app/data.py` (pure functions over the arena DB / CSVs /
  live_watch — importable and testable WITHOUT streamlit installed);
  `dashboard.py` is presentation only and imports streamlit lazily at run
  time. The pytest suite never needs streamlit.
- **Three tabs, mirroring the oil app's structure**:
  ① Arena — headline `st.metric` row (tracked / live / diverged), the
  `compare_strategies` table via `st.dataframe`, status badges as emoji
  prefixes (dataframes can't render HTML badges — ✅ PASS, ⏸ PAUSED,
  📚 REFERENCE, 🔬 RESEARCH, 🚫 EXCLUDED).
  ② Equity — sidebar path input (default `walkforward_equity.csv`),
  `compute_metrics` cards + `st.line_chart` of equity (+ gross overlay
  when the CSV has `equity_gross`).
  ③ Live signals — ticker/interval/strategy controls in the sidebar,
  a "↻ Refresh" button calling `live_watch.watch_once` (manual refresh,
  not st.autorefresh — no extra dependency, no surprise API hammering).
- **Chart convention carried over**: crimson dashed reference lines
  (the oil app's signature) for drawdown peaks/thresholds where drawn.
- **Read-only invariant**: data.py takes paths, opens SQLite read-only
  (`mode=ro` URI) so a dashboard bug can never mutate a ledger.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Running backtests/live ticks from the dashboard (arena-run stays the CLI)
- Auth (localhost tool, same posture as gui-hft)
- st.autorefresh / websocket live streaming; Plotly (st.line_chart first)
- Replacing either existing GUI (this is explicitly a third)

## Affected Areas
- New: `streamlit_app/__init__.py`, `streamlit_app/data.py` (pure:
  `arena_rows(db_path)`, `arena_headline(rows)`, `equity_metrics(csv)`,
  `live_tape(tickers, interval, strategy_name)`),
  `streamlit_app/dashboard.py` (presentation).
- `pyproject.toml` — `dashboard` optional extra; `streamlit_app` added to
  packages.
- New: `tests/test_streamlit_data.py` — data.py only; no streamlit import.
- `.gitignore` — nothing new needed (no artifacts).

## Implementation Order
1. `data.py` pure functions + tests (arena read-only URI, badge mapping,
   headline counts, equity metrics passthrough, live tape lines).
2. `dashboard.py` presentation: page config, sidebar, three tabs wired to
   data.py; verified manually via `streamlit run`.
3. Docs: run instructions in the module docstring + PROGRESS note.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `uv sync` (no extra) unchanged; suite green without streamlit installed
- [ ] `uv sync --extra dashboard && uv run streamlit run
      streamlit_app/dashboard.py` serves all three tabs against real
      artifacts when present
- [ ] `arena_rows()` opens the DB read-only — an attempted write in a test
      raises (pinned)
- [ ] Empty/missing DB and missing CSV render friendly empty states, not
      tracebacks
- [ ] Badge mapping covers all six statuses
- [ ] Tests pass: `uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"` with NO
      streamlit in the environment

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| streamlit not installed, dashboard.py executed | Clear SystemExit naming `uv sync --extra dashboard` |
| Arena DB locked by a concurrent arena-run live | Read-only connection retries once, then friendly notice |
| Equity CSV without an `equity` column | Same error message analyze-equity gives, rendered as st.error |
| live tape fetch failure | The existing per-ticker error isolation from watch_once flows through |

## Open Questions
None — plan is complete.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `feat(dashboard): streamlit_app/data.py — read-only data layer + tests`
2. `feat(dashboard): three-tab Streamlit console (arena / equity / live tape)`

Read .claude/skills/github/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/code-economy/SKILL.md
before doing anything. The GitHub skill covers auth and issue creation.
The code-economy skill defines what makes a good, reviewable change.

---

You are a backlog planning agent for a personal GitHub project.
Your job is to read the current project state and create well-formed
GitHub issues that the overnight session can work through autonomously.

Every issue you create must be:
- Self-contained (completable in one overnight session)
- Specific (clear acceptance criteria, not vague goals)
- Verifiable (a test to run or output to check)
- Code-economy compliant (won't produce bloated PRs)
- Labelled ready-for-ai and assigned to the repo owner

---

## STEP 1 — PREREQUISITES

```python
import os
from github import Github

# Verify auth
token = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN")
username = os.environ.get("GITHUB_USERNAME")
if not token or not username:
    raise SystemExit(
        "Set GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_USERNAME in your shell config first."
    )

gh = Github(token)
repo = get_repo(gh)   # auto-detects from git remote
print(f"Planning issues for: {repo.full_name}")

# Read existing open issues to avoid duplicates
existing = list_issues(repo, state="open")
existing_titles = {i["title"].lower() for i in existing}
print(f"Existing open issues: {len(existing)}")
```

---

## STEP 2 — READ PROJECT CONTEXT

Read all of these before planning any issues:

**CLAUDE.md** — the project purpose, stack, rules, and current state.
This is the source of truth for what the project is trying to be.

**README.md** — user-facing description and roadmap if any.

**Current codebase:**
```bash
# What exists right now
find src/ lib/ app/ -type f 2>/dev/null | head -50 || \
  find . -name "*.py" -o -name "*.cpp" -o -name "*.ts" \
  | grep -v node_modules | grep -v build | head -50

# Where work is heading
git log --oneline -20

# Known gaps and TODOs
grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|NotImplemented\|raise NotImplementedError" \
  src/ lib/ app/ 2>/dev/null | head -30

# Test coverage gaps (uncovered files)
pytest --co -q 2>/dev/null | head -30 || true
```

---

## STEP 3 — CREATE MILESTONE (GITHUB EQUIVALENT OF EPIC)

Group related issues under a milestone:

```python
def create_milestone(repo, title: str, description: str) -> int:
    """Create a GitHub milestone. Returns the milestone number."""
    milestone = repo.create_milestone(
        title=title,
        description=description
    )
    print(f"Created milestone: {milestone.title} (#{milestone.number})")
    return milestone.number
```

Create one milestone per theme of work. For "" focus, one milestone
is enough. For full project analysis, create 2-4 milestones.

Good milestone names:
- "SCPI Device Family — Oscilloscopes"
- "NPC Tier 1: Structured Output"
- "Data Pipeline — Market Data Ingestion"

---

## STEP 4 — CREATE ISSUES

For each issue, use this exact body template so the overnight session
has everything it needs:

```python
ISSUE_TEMPLATE = """## What to change
{what}

## Where it is
{where}

## How to verify it's done
{verify}

## Constraints
{constraints}

## Code economy note
{economy_note}

## Branch name
`feature/issue-{{number}}-{slug}`

## Concept for learning materials
{concept}
"""
```

The **concept** field is critical — it tells the overnight session what
to teach/drill after completing this issue. It must be:
- A technical concept, not a feature name
- Specific enough to produce a useful lesson
- Different from concepts already in docs/learning/PROGRESS.md

```python
def plan_and_create_issues(repo, milestone_number: int,
                           specs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Create a batch of issues. Each spec is a dict with keys:
        title, what, where, verify, constraints, economy_note,
        slug, concept

    Returns list of created issue dicts with number and URL.
    """
    username = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]
    created = []

    # Ensure overnight labels exist
    create_overnight_labels(repo)

    milestone = repo.get_milestone(milestone_number)

    for spec in specs:
        # Skip if similar issue already exists
        if spec["title"].lower() in existing_titles:
            print(f"Skipping (exists): {spec['title']}")
            continue

        body = ISSUE_TEMPLATE.format(
            what=spec["what"],
            where=spec["where"],
            verify=spec["verify"],
            constraints=spec["constraints"],
            economy_note=spec["economy_note"],
            slug=spec["slug"],
            concept=spec["concept"],
            number="N"    # placeholder — updated after creation
        )

        issue = repo.create_issue(
            title=spec["title"],
            body=body,
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[username],
            milestone=milestone
        )

        # Update branch name now that we have the number
        updated_body = body.replace(
            "feature/issue/N",
            f"feature/issue-{issue.number}"
        )
        issue.edit(body=updated_body)

        print(f"  Created #{issue.number}: {spec['title']}")
        print(f"  Concept: {spec['concept']}")
        created.append({
            "number":  issue.number,
            "title":   spec["title"],
            "concept": spec["concept"],
            "url":     issue.html_url
        })

    return created
```

---

## STEP 5 — ECONOMY NOTE GUIDANCE

Every issue should include an `economy_note` that pre-constrains the
implementation. This prevents the overnight session from over-building.

Good economy notes:
```
Use stdlib re for command pattern matching — no regex library needed.
Follow the existing BaseDevice pattern exactly — no new abstractions.
One new file maximum: src/devices/psu_e3631a.py plus its test file.
```

Bad economy notes (too vague):
```
Keep it simple.
Don't over-engineer.
```

The note should name the specific stdlib/pattern to use, or the
specific constraint on scope.

---

## STEP 6 — VERIFY THE QUEUE

After creating all issues:

```python
print("\n=== Tonight's ready-for-ai queue ===")
queue = list_issues(repo, label="ready-for-ai")
for issue in queue:
    print(f"  #{issue['number']:3} {issue['title']}")
    print(f"       URL: {issue['url']}")

print(f"\nTotal: {len(queue)} issues queued")
print("Run nightly-all.sh tonight to work through them.")
```

---

## STEP 7 — WRITE LOCAL PLAN SUMMARY

Save a planning summary locally (not committed):

```python
summary = f"""# Issue Planning Summary
Date: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}
Repo: {repo.full_name}
Focus: {"" or "full project analysis"}

## Issues Created Tonight
"""
for issue in created_issues:
    summary += f"- #{issue['number']}: {issue['title']}\n"
    summary += f"  Concept: {issue['concept']}\n"
    summary += f"  URL: {issue['url']}\n\n"

summary += """
## What Was NOT Planned
[things seen in codebase not turned into issues and why]
"""

Path(".claude/memory/planning-session.md").write_text(summary)
print("\nPlan saved to .claude/memory/planning-session.md")
```

---

## CONCEPT SELECTION GUIDE

The `concept` field in each issue is what drives learning generation.
Choose well — this is what you'll study after the overnight session.

| Issue type | Good concept | Bad concept |
|------------|-------------|-------------|
| New SCPI device | "Multi-channel PSU channel selection in SCPI" | "E3631A support" |
| New Qt block | "Qt drag-and-drop hardware block pattern" | "New block" |
| Bug fix | "SCPI ErrorQueue per IEEE 488.2" | "Fixed a bug" |
| New NPC | "LLM character constraint and knowledge domain" | "Added blacksmith" |
| Backtest fix | "Lookahead bias in rolling feature windows" | "Fixed backtest" |
| Data pipeline | "Point-in-time market data and survivorship bias" | "Data ingestion" |

Before finalizing a concept, check docs/learning/PROGRESS.md to avoid
re-teaching something already well covered.

---

## RUNNING THIS COMMAND

```
/plan-github                        full project analysis
/plan-github "oscilloscope family"  focus on one area
/plan-github "phase 2"             focus on next milestone
```

Re-run after completing a milestone to plan the next set of work.
It reads existing open issues first and skips duplicates.

content.text:
You are running an overnight autonomous development session on this
repository. Use the overnight-coordinator agent to manage the full session.
You have full permission to read, write, commit, push, and open draft PRs.
You do NOT have permission to merge to main or close PRs after opening them.

## SETUP (run once at session start)

```bash
# 1. Ensure we are on main and up to date
git checkout main
git pull

# 2. Rebuild the knowledge graph so you navigate current code, not stale code
# (only if graphify is installed — skip silently if not)
graphify update . --force 2>/dev/null || echo "graphify not installed — skipping"

# 3. Check for a prior checkpoint (resume if interrupted)
cat .claude/memory/checkpoint.md 2>/dev/null || echo "No checkpoint — starting fresh"

# 4. Read tonight's issues
gh issue list --label "ready-for-ai" --json number,title,body,labels \
  --order created --limit 20
```

If a checkpoint exists and shows IN PROGRESS or FAILED stages, resume
from there rather than starting over.

Write the session start to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
# Checkpoint
Session started: [timestamp]
Goal: Work through all ready-for-ai issues
Status: IN PROGRESS
Issues to process: [list from gh output]
Issues completed: []
Issues failed: []
Issues skipped: []
```

---

## FOR EACH ISSUE (in number order, lowest first)

### A. READ AND ASSESS

```bash
gh issue view [N] --comments
```

Ask: Is this issue clear enough to attempt autonomously?

**Blockers that cause a SKIP:**
- Requires a design decision not documented in the issue
- Depends on another issue that isn't complete yet
- Requires credentials, API keys, or external resources not available
- Scope is too vague to produce a verifiable result

If blocked, label and move on — do NOT guess at intent:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "needs-human" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Skipped overnight: [specific reason]. Please clarify before re-queuing."
```

### B. ORIENT

Invoke the git-historian agent:
"Use the git-historian agent to understand the code area this issue will touch."

This surfaces hot files, recent decisions, and things NOT to redo.
Read .claude/memory/history-brief.md after it completes.

### C. MARK IN PROGRESS

```bash
gh issue edit [N] --add-label "ai-in-progress" --remove-label "ready-for-ai"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Starting overnight implementation. Planning now."
```

### D. BRANCH

```bash
git checkout main
git checkout -b feature/issue-[N]
```

### E. PLAN

Use /plan-feature [concept from issue title] and wait for a plan.
Save the plan to .claude/plans/issue-[N].md

Do not implement until you have a written plan.

### F. IMPLEMENT

Use the appropriate specialist agents for this repo (see repo-specific
section below). Follow the plan. Write complete code — no placeholders.

If you hit a problem after 2 attempts on the same sticking point, SKIP
the issue and mark it ai-blocked. Do not spiral.

### G. TEST

Run the project's test suite. The exact commands are in the repo-specific
section below. Tests MUST pass before committing.

If tests fail after 2 fix attempts: skip, mark blocked, move on.
```bash
gh issue edit [N] --remove-label "ai-in-progress" --add-label "ai-blocked"
gh issue comment [N] --body "Blocked: tests failing after 2 attempts. [describe failure]. Needs human attention."
git checkout main
git branch -D feature/issue-[N]
```

### H. COMMIT AND PUSH

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "fix(#[N]): [issue title, shortened]"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### I. OPEN DRAFT PR

Generate the PR description using the /mr-description command, then:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "fix(#[N]): [issue title]" \
  --body "[output from /mr-description]" \
  --base main \
  --head feature/issue-[N] \
  --draft
```

Label the issue complete and close it with a reference to the PR:
```bash
gh issue edit [N] \
  --remove-label "ai-in-progress" \
  --add-label "ai-completed"
gh issue close [N] \
  --comment "Implemented. Draft PR open for review — see above."
```

### J. GENERATE LEARNING MATERIALS

**Identify the primary concept:**
Ask yourself: "What is the single most important technical concept a
developer would need to understand to maintain or extend this change?"

Guidelines:
- Choose the concept, not the feature name
  ("triple-channel SCPI addressing" not "E3631A support")
- Should be teachable in one lesson
- Should have testable recall in a drill
- Should introduce vocabulary worth learning

Then generate all three artifacts. In overnight/automated context:
- Generate the HTML files fully
- Skip in-chat interactive knowledge checks (no user present)
- Make the HTML content thorough — it is the only output
- Update PROGRESS.md with what was covered

```
/teach [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/lessons/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/drill-me [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/drills/NNNN-[concept].html

```
/terms [concept]
```
This creates docs/learning/vocab/NNNN-[concept].html
and updates docs/learning/GLOSSARY.md

Commit the learning materials on the same feature branch:
```bash
git add docs/learning/
git commit -m "docs(learning): add lesson, drill and vocab for [concept] (from issue #[N])"
git push origin feature/issue-[N]
```

### K. UPDATE CHECKPOINT

Append to .claude/memory/checkpoint.md:
```
Issue #[N]: [COMPLETED | FAILED | SKIPPED]
  Branch: feature/issue-[N]
  PR: #[PR number if opened]
  Concept taught: [concept]
  Learning files: lessons/NNNN-x.html, drills/NNNN-x.html, vocab/NNNN-x.html
  Notes: [anything notable]
```

Return to main: `git checkout main`

---

## END OF ALL ISSUES

### 1. Rebuild the learning index

```
/index
```

Commit:

"""Read-only data layer for the Streamlit dashboard.

Every function here is pure and importable WITHOUT streamlit installed —
the pytest suite tests this module only; presentation lives in
dashboard.py. Spec: .claude/plans/streamlit-dashboard.md.

Read-only invariant: the arena DB is opened with a SQLite ``mode=ro`` URI,
so a dashboard bug can never mutate a ledger. Deliberately does NOT use
ArenaState — its constructor runs in-place migrations (writes), which a
viewer must never do.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sqlite3
import time
from typing import Callable, Dict, List

import pandas as pd

#: Status -> emoji badge (st.dataframe can't render HTML badges).
STATUS_BADGES: Dict[str, str] = {
    "PASS": "✅ PASS",
    "PROBATION": "🟡 PROBATION",
    "PAUSED": "⏸ PAUSED",
    "EXCLUDED": "🚫 EXCLUDED",
    "REFERENCE": "📚 REFERENCE",
    "RESEARCH": "🔬 RESEARCH",
}


class FriendlyDashboardError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised for conditions the UI should render as a notice, not a traceback."""


def _readonly_conn(db_path: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """A connection that CANNOT write — sqlite enforces mode=ro at open."""
    return sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)


def arena_rows(db_path: str) -> List[dict]:
    """Comparison rows from the arena DB, badge-decorated; [] when absent.

    Missing file, or a DB without arena tables, is an empty state — not an
    error. A locked DB (concurrent ``arena-run live``) gets one retry, then
    surfaces as a FriendlyDashboardError the UI shows as a notice.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(db_path):
        return []
    from analyze_equity import compare_strategies  # local: pulls pandas/sql glue

    for attempt in (0, 1):
        try:
            conn = _readonly_conn(db_path)
            try:
                table = compare_strategies(conn)
            finally:
                conn.close()
            break
        except (sqlite3.OperationalError, pd.errors.DatabaseError) as exc:
            message = str(exc).lower()
            if "no such table" in message:
                return []  # a DB, but not an arena DB (or never screened)
            if "locked" in message and attempt == 0:
                time.sleep(0.2)
                continue
            raise FriendlyDashboardError(
                f"could not read arena DB at {db_path}: {exc}") from exc
    if table.empty:
        return []
    rows = table.where(table.notna(), None).to_dict(orient="records")
    for row in rows:
        row["badge"] = STATUS_BADGES.get(row.get("status"), str(row.get("status")))
    return rows


def arena_headline(rows: List[dict]) -> Dict[str, int]:
    """{'tracked', 'live', 'diverged'} counts for the st.metric header row."""
    return {
        "tracked": len(rows),
        "live": sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("status") == "PASS"),
        "diverged": sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("diverged")),
    }


def equity_metrics(csv_path: str) -> Dict:
    """{'metrics': compute_metrics dict, 'frame': equity (+gross) DataFrame}.

    Error text matches analyze-equity's CLI so the two tools speak the same
    language; raised as FriendlyDashboardError for st.error rendering.
    """
    from analyze_equity import compute_metrics

    if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        raise FriendlyDashboardError(f"equity CSV not found: {csv_path}")
    frame = pd.read_csv(csv_path, index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
    if "equity" not in frame.columns:
        raise FriendlyDashboardError("CSV must contain an 'equity' column")
    columns = ["equity"] + (["equity_gross"] if "equity_gross" in frame.columns else [])
    return {"metrics": compute_metrics(frame["equity"]), "frame": frame[columns]}


def live_tape(tickers: List[str], interval: str, strategy_name: str,
              seen: Dict | None = None,
              fetch: Callable | None = None) -> List[str]:
    """One live_watch polling pass, returned as printable tape lines.

    ``seen`` carries fresh-signal dedupe state between refreshes (the UI
    keeps it in st.session_state); ``fetch`` is injectable for tests,
    mirroring watch_once's own design — per-ticker failure isolation flows
    through from watch_once unchanged.
    """
    from intraday_sim import STRATEGIES
    from live_watch import _default_fetch, watch_once

    strategy = STRATEGIES[strategy_name]()
    return watch_once(tickers, strategy, interval,
                      fetch or _default_fetch,
                      seen if seen is not None else {})

"""Tests for the Streamlit dashboard's data layer (streamlit_app/data.py).

Must run WITHOUT streamlit installed — data.py is pure by design.
Arena data is seeded through ArenaState (the writer); the layer under test
only ever reads.
"""
import sqlite3

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from streamlit_app.data import (FriendlyDashboardError, STATUS_BADGES,
                                _readonly_conn, arena_headline, arena_rows,
                                equity_metrics, live_tape)


def _seed(tmp_path, statuses):
    """Arena DB with one strategy per requested status; returns db path."""
    from strategy_arena import ArenaState

    db = str(tmp_path / "arena.db")
    state = ArenaState(db)
    for i, status in enumerate(statuses):
        name = f"s{i}_{status.lower()}"
        state.record_backtest(name, "PASS", {"Sharpe": 0.5, "CAGR": 0.1, "MaxDD": -0.1})
        if status != "PASS":
            state.set_status(name, status)
    return db


def test_arena_rows_reads_seeded_db_with_badges(tmp_path):
    """All six statuses map to their badges; rows carry the data columns."""
    db = _seed(tmp_path, list(STATUS_BADGES))
    rows = arena_rows(db)
    assert len(rows) == 6
    badges = {r["status"]: r["badge"] for r in rows}
    for status, badge in STATUS_BADGES.items():
        assert badges[status] == badge
    assert all("backtest_sharpe" in r for r in rows)


def test_arena_rows_is_read_only(tmp_path):
    """The mode=ro connection: an attempted write raises at the SQLite level."""
    db = _seed(tmp_path, ["PASS"])
    conn = _readonly_conn(db)
    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.OperationalError, match="readonly"):
        conn.execute("UPDATE strategies SET status='EXCLUDED'")
    conn.close()


def test_arena_rows_missing_db_returns_empty_list(tmp_path):
    assert arena_rows(str(tmp_path / "nope.db")) == []


def test_arena_rows_non_arena_db_is_empty_state_not_error(tmp_path):
    """A SQLite file without arena tables reads as 'nothing screened yet'."""
    db = str(tmp_path / "other.db")
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db)
    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE misc (x INTEGER)")
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    assert arena_rows(db) == []


def test_arena_headline_counts(tmp_path):
    db = _seed(tmp_path, ["PASS", "PASS", "PAUSED", "REFERENCE"])
    rows = arena_rows(db)
    counts = arena_headline(rows)
    assert counts == {"tracked": 4, "live": 2, "diverged": 0}


def test_equity_metrics_delegates_and_flags_missing_column(tmp_path):
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2026-01-02", periods=30)
    good = tmp_path / "eq.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"equity": 100000 * (1.001 ** pd.RangeIndex(30)),
                  "equity_gross": 100000 * (1.0012 ** pd.RangeIndex(30))},
                 index=idx).to_csv(good)
    out = equity_metrics(str(good))
    assert "Sharpe" in out["metrics"]
    assert list(out["frame"].columns) == ["equity", "equity_gross"]

"""Native Streamlit research console (presentation only).

Run (after ``uv sync --extra dashboard``):

    uv run streamlit run streamlit_app/dashboard.py

Three tabs mirroring the HFT learning app's oil dashboard patterns (wide
layout, sidebar controls, st.metric columns, tabs):
  ① Arena — standings from arena_state/arena.db, strictly read-only
  ② Equity — metrics + chart for any equity CSV
  ③ Live signals — manual-refresh tape via live_watch (completed bars only)

All data access goes through streamlit_app/data.py (pure, testable, no
streamlit imports). This file stays deliberately thin: widgets in, data.py
out, notices instead of tracebacks.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys


def _require_streamlit():
    """Lazy import with a friendly exit — core installs don't carry streamlit."""
    try:
        import streamlit as st
        return st
    except ImportError:
        sys.exit("streamlit is not installed — run: uv sync --extra dashboard")


def main() -> None:
    """Build the whole console. Streamlit reruns this top-to-bottom on every
    interaction — durable state (the live tape's dedupe dict and lines)
    lives in st.session_state, never in module globals."""
    st = _require_streamlit()
    from intraday_sim import STRATEGIES, VALID_INTERVALS
    from streamlit_app import data

    st.set_page_config(page_title="AlgoTrade Research Console", layout="wide")
    st.title("AlgoTrade Research Console")

    with st.sidebar:
        st.header("Sources")
        db_path = st.text_input("Arena DB", value="arena_state/arena.db")
        csv_path = st.text_input("Equity CSV", value="walkforward_equity.csv")
        st.header("Live tape")
        tickers_raw = st.text_input("Tickers", value="AAPL,MSFT")
        interval = st.selectbox("Interval", sorted(VALID_INTERVALS), index=1)
        strategy_name = st.selectbox("Strategy", list(STRATEGIES))
        refresh = st.button("↻ Refresh tape")
        st.caption("Read-only console — screening, ticking, and orders stay "
                   "in the CLI (`arena-run`, `rh-exec`).")

    tab_arena, tab_equity, tab_live = st.tabs(["① Arena", "② Equity", "③ Live signals"])

    with tab_arena:
        try:
            rows = data.arena_rows(db_path)
        except data.FriendlyDashboardError as exc:
            st.error(str(exc))
            rows = []
        if rows:
            counts = data.arena_headline(rows)
            c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
            c1.metric("Strategies tracked", counts["tracked"])
            c2.metric("Live (PASS)", counts["live"])
            c3.metric("Diverged flags", counts["diverged"],
                      delta="review needed" if counts["diverged"] else "all clear",
                      delta_color="inverse" if counts["diverged"] else "normal")
            import pandas as pd

            table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
            show = ["strategy", "badge", "live_sharpe", "live_cagr", "live_maxdd",
                    "win_rate", "trades", "backtest_sharpe", "divergence_z"]
            st.dataframe(table[[c for c in show if c in table.columns]],
                         hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        else:
            st.info("No arena data yet. Screen strategies first:\n\n"
                    "`uv run arena-run backtest --strategies tsmom,lowvol,meanrev "
                    "--start 2023-01-01 --end 2025-01-01`\n\nthen tick daily with "
                    "`uv run arena-run live` and refresh this page.")

    with tab_equity:
        try:
            out = data.equity_metrics(csv_path)
        except data.FriendlyDashboardError as exc:
            st.info(f"{exc} — run a backtest to produce one, e.g. "
                    "`uv run walkforward-sim --model models/... --start ... --end ...`")
            out = None
        if out:
            metrics = out["metrics"]
            m1, m2, m3, m4 = st.columns(4)
            m1.metric("Sharpe", f"{metrics.get('Sharpe', 0):.2f}")
            m2.metric("CAGR", f"{metrics.get('CAGR', 0):.2%}")
            m3.metric("Max drawdown", f"{metrics.get('MaxDD', 0):.2%}")
            m4.metric("Final equity", f"{metrics.get('Final', 0):,.0f}")
            frame = out["frame"].copy()
            # The oil app's chart signature is a crimson dashed reference
            # line; st.line_chart can't dash, so the running peak renders as
            # a plain reference series (plotly upgrade noted as out of scope).
            frame["peak"] = frame["equity"].cummax()
            st.line_chart(frame, use_container_width=True)

    with tab_live:
        st.caption("Completed bars only (a forming candle can un-engulf — "
                   "lesson 0038); yfinance runs ~1 minute delayed.")
        seen = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_seen", {})
        lines = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_lines", [])
        if refresh:
            import datetime as dt

            tickers = [t.strip().upper() for t in tickers_raw.split(",") if t.strip()]
            stamp = dt.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
            for line in data.live_tape(tickers, interval, strategy_name, seen=seen):
                lines.append(f"[{stamp}] {line}")
            st.session_state["tape_lines"] = lines[-200:]  # bounded scrollback
        if lines:
            st.code("\n".join(lines), language=None)
        else:
            st.info("Press ↻ Refresh tape in the sidebar to poll the latest bars.")


def _in_streamlit_run() -> bool:
    """True inside `streamlit run` / AppTest — false for plain imports, so
    importing this module in a streamlit-less environment stays safe."""
    try:
        from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import get_script_run_ctx
        return get_script_run_ctx() is not None
    except Exception:
        return False


if __name__ == "__main__" or _in_streamlit_run():
    main()

HFT Practice · Lesson 0040

Streamlit's Execution Model: Whole-Script Reruns and Where State Lives

Why this matters: the platform now has a real Streamlit app (streamlit_app/dashboard.py, PR #75). Streamlit's core trick — rerun the ENTIRE script on every interaction — is what makes it feel effortless, and it is also the thing that silently breaks apps whose authors don't know where state is allowed to live.

1 · The model

Click a button, type in a box, switch a tab: Streamlit throws away the frame and executes your script again from line 1. Widgets aren't event handlers — they're functions that return their current value during this rerun. st.button returns True exactly once (the rerun caused by the click), then False on every later rerun. There is no callback soup and no DOM to reconcile — but it means module-level variables reset on every interaction, so anything that must SURVIVE a rerun needs an explicit home:

StateCorrect homeIn our console
Widget valuesThe widgets themselves (keyed by position/label)Sidebar paths, tickers, interval
Accumulated data across interactionsst.session_statetape_seen (signal dedupe), tape_lines (bounded scrollback)
Module globalsNowhere — reset every rerunDeliberately none
# dashboard.py — why the tape survives the rerun the button causes:
seen = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_seen", {})
lines = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_lines", [])
if refresh:                      # True only on the click-rerun
    lines.append(...)            # mutates the session_state object
    st.session_state["tape_lines"] = lines[-200:]  # bounded scrollback

2 · The two guards this repo added

Import-safety guard. streamlit run executes the file top-to-bottom, so apps put their build at module level — but our suite must be able to import the module in an environment with NO streamlit. The fix pins the launch to a real script-run context:

if __name__ == "__main__" or _in_streamlit_run():
    main()
# _in_streamlit_run(): streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.get_script_run_ctx()
# is not None — true under `streamlit run` AND under AppTest, false for
# plain imports. Pinned by test_plain_import_never_launches_the_app.

Logic/presentation split. Reruns make UI code awkward to unit test — so everything testable lives in streamlit_app/data.py (pure, no streamlit import, read-only mode=ro SQLite), and the UI file is thin enough that streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest can exercise it whole: run the script, assert on at.metric/at.dataframe/at.exception.

3 · Often confused

PairDistinction
Rerun model vs callback model (Tkinter/FastAPI)gui_app.py wires callbacks to long-lived widgets; webapp routes handle one request each. Streamlit re-executes everything and RECONSTRUCTS widgets — state lives in session_state, not in the widget tree or module.
st.session_state vs @st.cache_datasession_state is per-browser-tab mutable memory; cache_data memoizes function results across reruns (and users) keyed by arguments. The tape's dedupe dict must NOT be cached — it's stateful, not a pure function result.
The lab web theme vs this consoleThe webapp's "lab" theme is FastAPI wearing Streamlit's CSS; this is actual Streamlit — reruns, session_state, AppTest and all. Two different programs that happen to share an aesthetic.

4 · Practice

Score: 0 / 0

Q1. A module-level tape_lines = [] in dashboard.py would appear to "work" briefly, then always show an empty tape. Why?

  • Each interaction reruns the script, resetting the global to []
  • Streamlit runs each widget in its own thread
  • The GC collects lists without references
  • st.code can't display lists

Q2. Why does st.button("↻ Refresh") only fetch the tape once per click instead of on every subsequent rerun?

  • Streamlit debounces buttons for 30 seconds
  • The button returns True only on the click-caused rerun
  • session_state suppresses repeat fetches
  • cache_data memoizes the fetch

Q3. The dashboard deliberately does NOT use ArenaState to read the arena DB. What's the reason?

  • ArenaState is too slow for a dashboard
  • ArenaState's constructor migrates (writes); the console opens mode=ro instead
  • strategy_arena can't be imported without streamlit
  • compare_strategies requires a raw connection

Q4. Why do the AppTest console tests auto-skip in the core dev environment?

  • They're too slow for CI
  • streamlit is an opt-in extra; importorskip enforces the streamlit-free core contract
  • AppTest needs a real browser
  • They only test mocks

  • Streamlit debounces buttons for 30 seconds
  • The button returns True only on the click-caused rerun
  • session_state suppresses repeat fetches
  • cache_data memoizes the fetch

## Summary
The native Streamlit dashboard is real: `streamlit_app/` now holds a pure,
read-only data layer (#73) and the three-tab console (#74) — arena
standings, equity analysis, and a manual-refresh live-signals tape,
mirroring your oil dashboard's layout patterns over this platform's

- The console deliberately does NOT use ArenaState to read the arena DB —

  excludes it.

## Overnight session #3 complete — 2 for 2 ✅

The Streamlit console is **real and runnable right now**:

```bash
uv run streamlit run streamlit_app/dashboard.py
```

(streamlit is already installed in your venv via the pre-approved `dashboard` extra — fresh clones need `uv sync --extra dashboard` first; plain `uv sync` stays streamlit-free by tested contract.)

**What shipped** — draft **PR #75**: https://github.com/bjl14710/algo_trading_practice/pull/75

The key design call: it deliberately bypasses `ArenaState` (whose constructor runs migrations, i.e. *writes*) and opens the DB with a SQLite `mode=ro` URI — a dashboard bug physically cannot touch a ledger, and a test pins that the connection refuses writes.

You now have four ways to drive the platform: Tkinter (`gui-hft`), classic webapp, lab-themed webapp (`?theme=lab`), and this native Streamlit console.

content.text:
It already exists — it's the **arena**, and the good news is your mental model just needs one correction: this platform trades **daily bars**, so "running constantly during the day" is unnecessary. One `arena-run live` tick per day is all it takes — each strategy has its own independent $100k paper ledger in `arena_state/arena.db`, and the tick is *self-backfilling*: if your laptop was closed for a week, the next tick deterministically replays the missed days. Nothing is lost by not running it continuously.

But it's never been seeded with real data — you've only ever seen it in tests. Let me set up the whole thing for real right now: screen the strategies on live market data, run the first paper tick, show you the standings, and install a scheduler so it ticks itself every weekday while you're at work.

"""Tests for the Strategy Arena orchestrator: state store, filter, live tick,
and the comparison report. All offline — synthetic frames, tmp_path SQLite."""
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from analyze_equity import compare_strategies
from strategies.daily import DailySignal, DailyStrategy
from strategy_arena import ArenaState, live_tick, passes_filter


class AlwaysLong(DailyStrategy):
    """Test double: long every bar once warmed up (warmup_bars=2)."""

    name = "always-long"

    def generate_signal(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> DailySignal:
        """Constant +1 with fixed confidence."""
        return DailySignal(position=1, confidence=1.0, reason="always long")


@pytest.fixture
def state(tmp_path):
    """Fresh arena DB per test."""
    return ArenaState(str(tmp_path / "arena.db"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter bar
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_filter_passes_lenient_bar():
    """Positive Sharpe and tolerable drawdown clear the universal bar."""
    assert passes_filter({"Sharpe": 0.4, "MaxDD": -0.12}, min_sharpe=0.0, max_dd=-0.30)


def test_filter_rejects_negative_sharpe_or_deep_drawdown():
    """Either clause failing excludes the strategy; missing metrics exclude too."""
    assert not passes_filter({"Sharpe": -0.1, "MaxDD": -0.05}, 0.0, -0.30)
    assert not passes_filter({"Sharpe": 1.2, "MaxDD": -0.45}, 0.0, -0.30)
    assert not passes_filter({}, 0.0, -0.30)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ArenaState
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_record_backtest_upserts_status(state):
    """Re-running a backtest overwrites the verdict instead of duplicating."""
    state.record_backtest("meanrev", "EXCLUDED", {"Sharpe": -0.2, "CAGR": -0.01, "MaxDD": -0.4})
    state.record_backtest("meanrev", "PASS", {"Sharpe": 0.5, "CAGR": 0.06, "MaxDD": -0.1})
    assert state.statuses() == {"meanrev": "PASS"}


def test_append_ledger_is_idempotent(state):
    """Inserting the same (strategy, date) rows twice keeps a single copy."""
    rows = [("2026-07-01", 1000.0), ("2026-07-02", 1010.0)]
    trades = [("2026-07-01", "AAA", 1, 0.9, 1.0, 0.01, "test")]
    assert state.append_ledger("s", rows, trades) == 2
    assert state.append_ledger("s", rows, trades) == 0
    n_eq = state.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM equity").fetchone()[0]
    n_tr = state.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trades").fetchone()[0]
    assert (n_eq, n_tr) == (2, 1)
    assert state.last_equity("s") == ("2026-07-02", 1010.0)


def test_gap_logged_once_per_strategy_day(state):
    """Gap logging is keyed on (strategy, date) — retries don't duplicate."""
    state.log_gap("s", "2026-07-01", "yfinance timeout")
    state.log_gap("s", "2026-07-01", "yfinance timeout (retry)")
    assert state.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gaps").fetchone()[0] == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# live_tick: seed, idempotency, auto-backfill
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_live_tick_seeds_then_reruns_as_noop_then_backfills(state, make_ohlcv):
    """The acceptance triple: first run seeds the ledger, a same-day rerun is
    a no-op, and extending the data backfills exactly the missed days with
    multiplicatively-chained equity (no return lost at run boundaries)."""
    closes5 = [100, 102, 104, 106, 108]
    data = {"AAA": make_ohlcv(closes5)}

    added = live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), data, top_n=1,
                      capital=1000.0, trade_cost_bps=0.0)
    # 5 bars minus the provisional final bar -> 4 stored days
    assert added == 4
    _, eq_last = state.last_equity("s")
    assert eq_last == pytest.approx(1000.0 * closes5[4] / closes5[1])

    # same data, same day -> nothing new
    assert live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), data, top_n=1,
                     capital=1000.0, trade_cost_bps=0.0) == 0

    # two more bars arrive (e.g. the arena missed a day) -> exactly 2 backfilled
    closes7 = closes5 + [110, 112]
    data7 = {"AAA": make_ohlcv(closes7)}
    assert live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), data7, top_n=1,
                     capital=1000.0, trade_cost_bps=0.0) == 2
    _, eq_final = state.last_equity("s")
    # continuous ledger equals buy-and-hold from the first traded bar
    assert eq_final == pytest.approx(1000.0 * closes7[6] / closes7[1])


def test_live_tick_records_trades_only_for_new_dates(state, make_ohlcv):
    """Trade rows land once per (strategy, date, ticker) across reruns."""
    data = {"AAA": make_ohlcv([100, 102, 104, 106])}
    live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), data, 1, 1000.0, 0.0)
    live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), data, 1, 1000.0, 0.0)
    trades = state.conn.execute("SELECT date, ticker FROM trades ORDER BY date").fetchall()
    assert len(trades) == len(set(trades))
    assert all(t == ("AAA",) or t[1] == "AAA" for t in trades)


def test_live_tick_empty_data_logs_gap(state):
    """A dead data feed becomes a gap row, not a crash."""
    assert live_tick(state, "s", AlwaysLong(), {}, 1, 1000.0, 0.0) == 0
    assert state.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gaps").fetchone()[0] == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# compare_strategies report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_compare_strategies_shows_excluded_and_divergence(state, make_ohlcv):
    """The report keeps EXCLUDED strategies visible and computes live-vs-
    backtest Sharpe divergence plus win rate for live strategies."""
    state.record_backtest("winner", "PASS", {"Sharpe": 1.0, "CAGR": 0.2, "MaxDD": -0.1})
    state.record_backtest("loser", "EXCLUDED", {"Sharpe": -0.5, "CAGR": -0.1, "MaxDD": -0.5})
    live_tick(state, "winner", AlwaysLong(),
              {"AAA": make_ohlcv([100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110])},
              top_n=1, capital=1000.0, trade_cost_bps=0.0)

    table = compare_strategies(state.conn).set_index("strategy")
    assert set(table.index) == {"winner", "loser"}

    loser = table.loc["loser"]
    assert loser["status"] == "EXCLUDED"
    assert loser["trades"] == 0
    assert loser["backtest_sharpe"] == pytest.approx(-0.5)

    winner = table.loc["winner"]
    assert winner["status"] == "PASS"
    assert winner["trades"] > 0
    assert winner["win_rate"] == 1.0  # monotonic uptrend, always long
    assert winner["sharpe_divergence"] == pytest.approx(
        winner["live_sharpe"] - winner["backtest_sharpe"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sizing mode persistence (screened configuration, reused by live)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_sizing_mode_defaults_to_equal_for_legacy_strategy(state):
    """A strategy never screened under this feature reads back as 'equal'."""
    assert state.sizing_mode("never-screened") == "equal"


def test_sizing_mode_persists_and_is_reused(state):
    """record_backtest stores the sizing mode; sizing_mode reads it back."""
    state.record_backtest("s", "PASS", {"Sharpe": 0.5, "CAGR": 0.1, "MaxDD": -0.1},
                          sizing="conf_vol")
    assert state.sizing_mode("s") == "conf_vol"
    # re-screening under a different mode updates it, not duplicates
    state.record_backtest("s", "PASS", {"Sharpe": 0.6, "CAGR": 0.1, "MaxDD": -0.1},
                          sizing="equal")
    assert state.sizing_mode("s") == "equal"


def test_arena_db_migration_adds_sizing_column_in_place(tmp_path):
    """A pre-existing arena.db (created before the sizing column existed)
    upgrades in place with no data loss."""
    import sqlite3

    db_path = str(tmp_path / "legacy_arena.db")
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE strategies (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL, "
        "backtest_sharpe REAL, backtest_cagr REAL, backtest_maxdd REAL, updated TEXT)"
    )
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO strategies VALUES ('old', 'PASS', 0.5, 0.1, -0.1, '2026-01-01')")
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# arena_daily.sh — one arena paper-trading tick + standings snapshot.
# Designed for launchd/cron: idempotent (a second run the same day is a
# no-op) and self-backfilling (missed days replay deterministically on the
# next run), so an unreliable schedule costs nothing.
#
# Install (macOS launchd, weekdays 17:30 local — see scripts/arena.plist):
#   cp scripts/arena.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.algotrading.arena.plist
#   launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.algotrading.arena.plist
# Disable:
#   launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.algotrading.arena.plist
set -euo pipefail

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"   # uv, for launchd's bare env
cd "$REPO_DIR"

LOG="arena_state/daily.log"
mkdir -p arena_state
{
  echo "===== arena tick $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ====="
  uv run arena-run live
  echo "----- standings -----"
  uv run arena-run report
  echo
} >> "$LOG" 2>&1

## The paper-money arena is live, seeded with real data, and ready to run itself

**Where it is:** each strategy has its own independent **$100k paper ledger** in `arena_state/arena.db`. It's daily-bar trading, so one tick per day is all it needs — and the tick is *self-backfilling*: laptop closed for a week costs nothing, the next run deterministically replays the gap. "Running constantly" is unnecessary by design.

**What I set up for you just now, on real market data (10 large-caps, realistic costs):**

| Strategy | Verdict | The story |
|---|---|---|
| **tsmom** | PASS → **live Sharpe 1.48**, 60% win rate, 57 trades | Currently your best — beating its own backtest |
| **lowvol** | PASS → live ~flat | Divergence monitor watching it (z −0.62, inside noise) |
| meanrev, engulfing, technical | EXCLUDED / demoted to REFERENCE | The research verdict confirmed: engulfing made +0.21% gross and **−2.10% net** — its "edge" is smaller than its trading costs |
| gbm | EXCLUDED | Decent returns (9.2% net) but −35.8% drawdown and $14.7k cost drag failed the bar |

**Your daily workflow (or rather, the absence of one):**
- **Automatic:** `bash scripts/arena_daily.sh` ticks + logs standings to `arena_state/daily.log` (tested, working). To make it fire every weekday at 5:30pm automatically, run these two lines yourself — the security layer rightly wouldn't let me install a persistent system agent on your behalf:
  ```bash
  cp scripts/arena.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.algotrading.arena.plist
  launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.algotrading.arena.plist
  ```
  (launchd fires missed runs on wake; undo anytime with `launchctl unload`.)
- **Check results:** `arena-run report` in a terminal, the **Arena** page at `localhost:8000/arena` (`web-hft`), or the Streamlit console's Arena tab — all read the same ledgers.

**Bonus: real-world use found and fixed a real bug.** `arena-run live` had been silently ticking the *wrong strategy list* — an argparse gotcha where `set_defaults` on the backtest subparser writes through to the shared parent action, poisoning live's default. Every prior test had passed `--strategies` explicitly, masking it. Fixed, regression-pinned, plus the live lookback default now covers tsmom's 273-bar warmup (it was silently all-holds before). Suite: **274 passed**. All committed and pushed on `feature/streamlit-console`.

One honest caveat: today's "live" ledger was seeded by replaying the last ~14 months — real forward-walking paper results start accumulating from today's ticks onward. The divergence z-test needs ~20 fresh days before its verdicts mean much.
